`AutoSwitchStrategy.fromStringCode(code)` returns the constant whose code equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive: `withIssue` matches, `WITHISSUE` and `withissue` do not) and null for null or an unknown code. It never throws.

`new ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean(mode, specs)` returns `mode` from `getSensitivityMode()` (null is not checked) and from `getNonSensitiveAttributes()` an unmodifiable set copy of `specs` (duplicates collapse, later changes to `specs` have no effect, and modifying the set throws `UnsupportedOperationException`). A null collection throws `NullPointerException`.
`ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean.DEFAULT` has mode `STANDARD` and an empty set of non-sensitive attributes.

The default permission shortcuts of `StructureConfiguration` call the generic methods with fixed `CoreAppPermissions` constants: `isEnabledForAnyone`, `getEnabledPermissionSubjects`, `setEnabledForAnyone` and `setEnabledPermissionSubjectsEncoded` use `USE`; the `Create`/`Creator` and `isStructureCreationAllowed` methods use `CREATE_STRUCTURE`; the `Synchronization` methods and `isSynchronizationAllowed` use `SYNCHRONIZATION`; the `Automation` methods and `isAutomationAccessAllowed` use `AUTOMATION`. Results of the generic methods are returned unchanged.

The default `setPickedProjectIds(LongIterable)` and `setPickedProjectIds(Collection<Long>)` call the string form with the IDs as a comma-separated decimal list in iteration order without spaces (10, 20, 30 gives `10,20,30`); an empty input gives `""` and null gives `""`.

The default `setPermissionSubjects(permission, subjects)` calls `setPermissionSubjectsEncoded(permission, text)` where text is each subject's `toEncodedString()` joined with commas in iteration order; null subjects give `""`.

In the plugin's configuration with nothing stored, `isEnabledForAllProjects()` is true, `isAllowedForAnyone` is true for every known permission, `getPermissionSubjects` is empty, `getPickedProjectIds()` is empty, `getDefaultStructureId` is 0 for any project and `getAttributeSensitivitySettings()` is mode `STANDARD` with no attributes. `isProjectEnabled(null)` is false.

In the plugin's configuration, `setDefaultStructureId(null, id)` sets the global default (null stores 0); `setDefaultStructureId(project, id)` sets a project default and a null ID removes it. `getDefaultStructureId(project)` returns the project's own default, else the global default, else 0; `isDefaultStructureSetForProject` is true only when the project has its own default.

In the plugin's configuration, `isAllowed(permission, null)` is false. For a user who passes `isStructureAvailable`, it is true when the permission is granted to anyone, when the user is a Jira administrator (with the administrator bypass on, the default), or when a stored permission subject matches the user; otherwise false. `isStructureAvailable` is false when the plugin is enabled for no project.

In the plugin's configuration, `getConfigurationScopeQuery()` is null and `addConfigurationScopeClause` adds nothing when the plugin is enabled for all projects; otherwise the clause restricts the project to the enabled project IDs (joined with AND; a new builder is made for null), and with no enabled project it restricts to project ID 2147483647.

`StructurePage` constants in order and their `getId()`: `STRUCTURE_BOARD` `structure`, `STRUCTURE_BOARD_WITH_DETAILS` `structure-with-details` (deprecated), `ISSUE_VIEW` `issue`, `PROJECT_TAB` `project`, `COMPONENT_TAB` `component`, `VERSION_TAB` `version`, `ISSUE_NAVIGATOR` `navigator`, `GADGET` `gadget`, `GREENHOPPER_TAB` `greenhopper`. Jackson writes a page as its ID string and reads it back through `forId`.
`StructurePage.forId(id)` returns the page with exactly this ID (case-sensitive: `issue` matches, `ISSUE` does not) and null for null or an unknown ID.
`StructurePage.enumSet(pages)` returns null for a null or empty collection; otherwise a new `EnumSet` with the given pages (duplicates collapse). A null element throws `NullPointerException`.

A new `UISettingsBean()` has no strategy for any page, both flags null and `isAnythingSet()` false. `setAutoSwitchStrategy(page, s)` stores `s` for that page only (other pages stay null), null removes it, and it returns the same bean; a null page throws `NullPointerException` (message `page is null`). `setAutoCollapseStructurePanel` and `setKeepStructureWhileNavigating` store their `Boolean` as is (null unsets). `isAnythingSet()` is true when any page strategy or either flag is set, including a flag set to false.

`new UISettingsBean(other)` copies the auto-switch strategy of every page and the auto-collapse flag from `other`, but not the keep-while-navigating flag, which stays null (as the original does); `new UISettingsBean(null)` is the same as the no-argument constructor.

The default `Structure.getOwner()` returns null when `getOwnerUserKey()` is null, without contacting Jira; otherwise it resolves the key to a Jira `ApplicationUser` and returns null when no such user exists.

The default `Structure.setOwner(user)` calls `setOwnerUserKey` with the user's key (`ApplicationUser.getKey()`), or with null when the user is null, and returns the very instance it was called on (not the value returned by `setOwnerUserKey`).

On a structure obtained from the plugin, every setter (`setName`, `setDescription`, `setOwnerUserKey`, `setPermissions`, `setEditRequiresParentIssuePermission`, `setArchived`) returns the same instance, and the new value is visible through the matching getter immediately, before `saveChanges()` is called.

On a structure obtained from the plugin, `setName(null)` makes `getName()` return the empty string; a name longer than 190 characters is stored abbreviated to 190 characters ending in `...`; `getDescription()` returns the empty string after `setDescription(null)`.

`saveChanges()` on a plugin structure whose name is blank (empty or whitespace) throws `IllegalStateException`, even when nothing was changed since the copy was obtained; with a non-blank name and no changes it returns the same instance without persisting anything.
`getEffectivePermission()` of a plugin structure that has never been saved (ID 0) returns `PermissionLevel.NONE`; for a saved structure it returns `ADMIN` while security is overridden.
`getPermissions()` of a plugin structure returns a new list of cloned rules on each call; adding to or clearing the returned list does not change what a later `getPermissions()` returns.

`new ForestVersion(forest, entry)` exposes the given forest and entry unchanged (same instances) in the public final fields `fullForest` and `entry`. The forest may be null; a null entry throws `NullPointerException`.

`ForestVersion.weight` is 128 plus a forest term for the full forest plus, for every change of the entry, 80 plus the forest term of the change's forest plus the list terms of its path-from, after-from, path-to and after-to lists (original rows are not counted). The forest term is 0 for a null or empty forest, otherwise 128 + 12 x number of rows; the list term is 0 for a null or empty list, otherwise 64 + 8 x number of elements. Example: an empty full forest and an entry with no changes give 128; a 3-row full forest and one ADD change with a 2-row forest, null from-lists, a path-to of 1 element and an empty after-to give 128+164+80+152+72 = 596.

`HistoryEntry`'s seven-argument constructor stores structure ID, version, previous version, timestamp, user key, synchronizer ID and changes, returned unchanged by `getStructure`, `getVersion`, `getPrevVersion`, `getTimestamp`, `getUserKey`, `getSynchronizer` and `getChanges`. A null synchronizer stays null. No argument is validated (versions need not be consecutive).
`HistoryEntry.getUserKey()` returns null when the constructor received either null or the empty string as user key; any other string (including a blank one such as a single space) is kept as given.

`HistoryEntry.getChanges()` returns the very list passed to the constructor: changes made to that list afterwards are visible through the entry, and the list is modifiable if the caller's list was (as the original does).

Two `HistoryEntry` objects are equal when structure ID, version, previous version, timestamp, user key, synchronizer ID and change lists are all equal (lists compared with `equals`); a difference in any one of them, such as the timestamp alone, makes them unequal. Equal entries have equal hash codes. An entry is never equal to null or to an object of another class.

`HistoryEntry.Change`'s constructor stores operation, forest, path-from, after-from, path-to, after-to, direction and original rows as given (same instances, nulls allowed, nothing validated); `getOperation`, `getForest`, `getPathFrom`, `getAfterFrom`, `getPathTo`, `getAfterTo`, `getDirection` and `getOriginalRows` return them unchanged.

Two `HistoryEntry.Change` objects are equal when operation, forest, the four position lists, direction and original rows are all equal (null equals null; lists and forests compared with their own `equals`); differing only in direction or only in original rows makes them unequal. Equal changes have equal hash codes.
`HistoryEntry.Operation` has constants ADD, COPY, MOVE, REMOVE in that order, with `getExternalName()` values `add`, `copy`, `move`, `remove`.

`HistoryEntry.Operation.forExternalName` returns the constant whose external name equals the argument exactly (`move` gives MOVE); a differently-cased text such as `MOVE` or `Move`, an unknown text, or null returns null (no exception).
`HistoryQuery.ALL_OPERATIONS` is the list [ADD, COPY, MOVE, REMOVE]; it is unmodifiable (`add` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`).

In the full `HistoryQuery` constructor the `operations` field becomes null when the given operations include all four constants (in any order, duplicates allowed); otherwise it is an immutable set of exactly the given operations. A null or empty operations argument gives an empty set (not null) (as the original does).

In the full `HistoryQuery` constructor each `LongList` argument (issues, structures, projects, synchronizers, in and out) is stored as the same instance when non-null, and as an empty `LongList` when null; the lists are neither copied nor sorted.

In the full `HistoryQuery` constructor the author and ancestor arguments are copied into immutable sets (null gives an empty set); changing the source collection later does not change the query, and modifying the field throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. A null element in one of these collections makes the constructor throw `NullPointerException` (as the original does).
`HistoryQuery` stores the min and max `Date` arguments as their millisecond values in `minDate`/`maxDate` (null stays null) and the start key unchanged in `startId`.

`new HistoryQuery(structureId, startId)` gives a query with `operations` null, `isStructuresSorted` containing only the structure ID, every other ID list empty, author and ancestor sets empty, `minDate` and `maxDate` null, and `startId` as given (may be null).

`HistoryQuery.toString()` mentions only conditions that are set (a query from `new HistoryQuery(5, null)` mentions the structure 5 but no start key; with start key 7 it also mentions 7), and repeated calls return equal text.

The `AbstractSynchronizer` constructor takes the sync audit log, structure manager and row manager from the given `StructureComponents` (one call each) and exposes them as the protected fields `myAuditLog`, `myStructureManager` and `myRowManager`; the bundle itself is kept in `myStructureComponents`.
`AbstractSynchronizer.getDescriptor()` returns null until `init(descriptor)` is called, then the descriptor passed to `init`; a later `init` replaces it.

`AbstractSynchronizer.storeParameters` returns null for null, the JSON text of a `Map` (for example a map with `a`=1 gives `{"a":1}`), and throws `IOException` for any non-map object, with a message naming the object, its class and that a `Map` was expected.

`AbstractSynchronizer.restoreParameters` returns null for null, parses a JSON object text into a string-keyed `Map` (so `restoreParameters(storeParameters(m))` equals `m` for JSON-compatible values), and throws `IOException` for malformed JSON.

`AbstractSynchronizer.castParameters` returns the same map instance when given a `Map`, and null when given null or a non-map (logging a warning in the latter case). `parametersAsMapObject` wraps the map in a `MapObject` or returns null in the same cases; `parametersAsNNMapObject` returns `MapObject.EMPTY` instead of null.
`AbstractSynchronizer.addDefaultFormParameters` leaves the given map unchanged.
`AbstractSynchronizer.getIssueIdByRow(row)` returns the item's long ID when the row's item is an issue identity, and 0 for any other item type.

`getIssueIdByRowId` looks the row up in the row manager and returns its issue ID (0 for non-issue rows); when the row manager throws `MissingRowException` it logs it through the current thread's `SyncLogger` and returns 0. `getIssueByRowId` returns null when that ID is 0 without consulting Jira.

`getIssue(long)` and `getIssue(String)` return the issue Jira's issue manager gives for the ID or key, or null when it gives none; when the lookup throws any exception, they log a warning and return null. `getIssueManager` throws `StructureRuntimeException` when Jira's issue manager is not available, and caches it once found.

`verifyStructureEditPermissions(structureId, log)` returns what the structure manager's `isAccessible(structureId, PermissionLevel.EDIT)` returns; when false it also logs a warning through the given `SyncLogger` saying it cannot run under the current user because that user may not edit the structure. The one-argument form uses `SyncLogger.get()`, so it fails with `IllegalStateException` when no logger is installed on the thread.

`AbstractSynchronizer.sync(instance, data, source)` calls `doSync` with the same arguments, then asks the audit log `isActionGroupRecorded(actions)` with the result's actions; only when true it calls `recordActions(instance, description, actions)` where description is a `MapObject` with `action`=`sync`, the result description's entries (e.g. `result`=`success`), `ownerKey` (instance's user key), `parameters` (instance parameters, empty map when null), and `jiraEvents` and `structureEvents` lists built from the sync data's events.

`AbstractSynchronizer.resync(instance, source)` calls `doResync` and records the result in the audit log as `sync` does, but with `action`=`resync` and without `jiraEvents`/`structureEvents` keys. If `doSync` or `doResync` throws, the exception propagates and the audit log is not called.

`AbstractSynchronizer.success(actions)` gives a run result whose actions are that same list and whose description is the map {`result`=`success`}. `failure(reason)`, `failure(throwable)` and `failure(throwable, reason)` give results with an empty action list and the description `SyncAuditLogHelper.getFailureDescription(reason, throwable)`; the nested `SyncRunAuditEntry.Success` and `SyncRunAuditEntry.Failure` constructors behave the same.
`SourceOfTruth` has constants JIRA and STRUCTURE (in that order) with `getCode()` values `jira` and `structure`.

`SourceOfTruth.fromCode` maps a code to its constant ignoring case (`JIRA`, `Jira` and `jira` all give JIRA). Null or an unknown code throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `Unknown code for SourceOfTruth ` followed by the argument (for null: `...SourceOfTruth null`).
`StructureSynchronizerException` is a checked exception (subclass of `Exception`): the one-argument constructor sets the message with no cause; the two-argument one sets message and cause.
The plugin's `SyncAuditLog.isActionGroupRecorded` returns true for a non-empty action list; for null or an empty list it returns false unless storing of empty groups is turned on by a system setting.

`SyncAuditLog.ActionGroup`'s constructor stores sync instance ID, module key, structure ID, timestamp, description and actions, returned by the matching getters. An empty-string module key is returned as null by `getSyncModuleKey()` (despite its not-null contract), null stays null, other keys unchanged. The description may be null.

`SyncAuditLog.ActionGroup.getActions()` is an unmodifiable view of the list passed to the constructor: modifying it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, but later changes to the original list show through. A null actions list makes the constructor throw `NullPointerException`.
`SyncAuditLogHelper.issueInfo(id, key)` returns an immutable map with `key`=key followed by `id`=id (a `Long`); when key is null the map has only `id`.
`SyncAuditLogHelper.issueInfo(Issue)` returns an empty map for null, otherwise the map of `issueInfo(issue.getId(), issue.getKey())`.

`SyncAuditLogHelper.issueInfo(long)` and the `ISSUE_INFO` function look the issue key up in Jira; when the issue is not found or the lookup fails (including when Jira is not available) the map contains only `id`. `ISSUE_INFO` applied to a null ID throws `NullPointerException`.

`issueConstantInfo` returns an empty map for null, otherwise a map with `name` then `id` (the constant's string ID), each omitted when null. `customFieldInfo` does the same for a custom field, using its name and numeric ID (`getIdAsLong`).

`createAuditLogEntryDescription(instance, data, aux)` returns a `MapObject` whose keys are, in order: `action` (`sync` when data is non-null, `resync` when null), every entry of aux, `ownerKey` (the instance's user key), `parameters` (instance parameters, an empty map when null) and, only when data is non-null, `jiraEvents` and `structureEvents` (lists of the data's events converted by `SyncEvents`). A key in aux that repeats one of these keys throws `IllegalArgumentException`; a null user key throws `NullPointerException` (as the original does).

`getFailureDescription(reason, throwable)` returns an immutable map: `result`=`failure`, then `reason` when non-null, then `exception` when non-null. The exception map has `message` (only when non-null), `class` (the exception's class name), `stackTrace` (the stack frames as a list of `StackTraceElement`) and, when there is a cause, `cause` described the same way recursively.
`SyncAuditLogHelper.isFailed(action)` is true exactly when the map's `result` value is the string `failure`; false for `success`, a missing key or a non-string value.
`SyncDirection` has constants INBOUND and OUTBOUND in that order; `CODE_INBOUND` is `IN` and `CODE_OUTBOUND` is `OUT`.
`SyncDirection.getCode` returns `IN` for INBOUND, `OUT` for OUTBOUND and the four-letter string `null` for a null argument.

`SyncDirection.fromCode` returns INBOUND for `IN`, OUTBOUND for `OUT`, and null for null or the string `null`; any other text, including lower-case `in`, throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message is that text.
`SyncEvent.compareTo` compares only timestamps: an event with the smaller timestamp is less, events with equal timestamps compare as 0 even if their kind or content differ.

`new SyncEvent.Jira(timestamp, instanceId, event)` exposes the timestamp, the sync instance ID (null allowed) and the event via `getTimestamp`, `getSyncInstanceId` and `getEvent`; `getAffectedIssuesSorted()` returns what the event's `getAffectedIssuesSorted()` returns. A null event throws `NullPointerException`.

`new SyncEvent.Structure(entry)` takes its timestamp from `entry.getTimestamp()` and its sync instance ID from `entry.getSynchronizer()`; `getHistoryEntry()` returns the entry. A null entry throws `NullPointerException`.

`SyncEvent.Jira.toString()` is `j(`, then `:` and the instance ID when there is one, then the UTC time of day as `HH:mm:ss.SSS` followed by `Z`, then `,`, the event's text and `)`; for example timestamp 0, instance 5 gives text starting `j(:500:00:00.000Z,`. `SyncEvent.Structure.toString()` has the same form starting with `s(` and the history entry's text.

`SyncEvents.JIRA_EVENT_TO_MAP` maps null to null and a Jira sync event to an immutable map with, in order, `type` (the text of the event's change type), `issues` (a list with `SyncAuditLogHelper.issueInfo` of each affected issue ID, in order), `timestamp` (a `Long`) and `syncInstanceId` (the instance ID, or 0 when null).

`SyncEvents.STRUCTURE_EVENT_TO_MAP` maps null to null and a structure sync event to an immutable map with, in order, `version` (the history entry's version, an `Integer`), `timestamp` and `syncInstanceId` (0 when the entry has no synchronizer).
With no recorded moves, `HierarchyHelper.getParent(row)` returns the row ID of the row's parent in the forest, or 0 for a top-level row. A row not in the index throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

After `recordMove(row, newParent)`, `getParent(row)` returns newParent, and later `recordMove` calls for the same row replace earlier ones. Recording a move under 0 (or under a row not in the forest) makes the row report parent 0, i.e. top level. Other rows' parents are unaffected; the forest itself is not changed.

`HierarchyHelper.isInSubtree(row, owner)` is true when owner is a proper ancestor of row, following parents with recorded moves applied (so a recorded move into or out of the owner's subtree changes the answer). A row is not in its own subtree. Row 0 gives false; owner 0 gives true for any non-zero row, even one not in the forest. Otherwise a row or owner not in the forest throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

`SyncLogger.get()` returns the logger installed on the current thread with `SyncLogger.set`, and throws `IllegalStateException` when none is installed (or after `set(null)`). Loggers installed on one thread are not seen by other threads. `isInfo()` and `isDebug()` report the installed logger's levels and also throw `IllegalStateException` when none is installed.

`SyncLogger.set` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (and installs nothing) when the current thread's context class loader is not the class loader that loaded `SyncLogger`, including when it is null.

A new `SyncLogger` has the empty prefix. `setPrefix(null)` sets the empty prefix. `pushPrefix(p)` appends a space and p (from the empty prefix `pushPrefix("a")` gives ` a`, then `pushPrefix("b")` gives ` a b`); `popPrefix()` restores the prefix from before the matching push; `popPrefix()` with no outstanding push throws `NoSuchElementException`.

`SyncLogger.createLogMessage(args...)` starts with the prefix and appends each argument's `String.valueOf`, putting one space before an argument unless the text so far is empty or the argument is a string or `Character` whose first character is in Unicode category 'other punctuation' (such as `,` `:` `.` `!` `/`) or 'control' (such as a newline). With an empty prefix: (`a`, 1, null) gives `a 1 null`; (`x`, `:`, `y`) gives `x: y`; (`a`, `(b)`) gives `a (b)`; (`a`, ``, `b`) gives `a  b`. Nested `Object[]` arguments are flattened; a null array gives just the prefix. With prefix `P`, (`a`) gives `P a`.

`info`, `debug`, `warn` and `error` pass `createLogMessage(args)` to the underlying slf4j `Logger` at that level only when the level is enabled (nothing is called on the logger otherwise). `infoException` always passes the throwable; `debugException`, `warnException` and `errorException` pass it only when it is non-null, otherwise log the text alone. `isInfoEnabled` and `isDebugEnabled` report the underlying logger; `getLogger`/`setLogger` read and replace it.

`warnExceptionIfDebug(ex, args)` does nothing when warn is disabled. When debug is also enabled it logs the text with the throwable at warn level. Otherwise it logs at warn level without the throwable, with the exception's message appended to the text as one more space-separated argument (for a null exception just the text).

`isAutoSync()` returns the constructor's auto flag. `isOneTimeSync()` is true only when a sync instance was given and its ID is 0. `selectBySyncMode(a, r, o)` returns a when auto, otherwise o for a one-time sync, otherwise r (also when no instance was given).

`defaultPrefix()` is the empty string when no sync instance was given. Otherwise it is the synchronizer descriptor's label (the synchronizer's class name when the label is null or empty; `<unavailable> ` plus the module key when the instance has no synchronizer), then ` autosync`, ` one-time sync` or ` full sync`, then ` #<instance id>` unless one-time, then ` for structure ` and `'<name>' (#<id>)`, or `#<id>` when the structure cannot be read.

With debug disabled, `issue(Long)` gives `null` for null, the issue key when Jira finds the issue, otherwise the number as text; `issue(Issue)` gives `null` for null, the issue key, or `#<id>` when the key is null. With debug enabled both give `(<key> <id>)` when a key is known, otherwise just the ID. `appendIssue` appends the same text as `issue(Long)` to the builder and returns it.

`issues(Iterable)` and `issues(LongIterable)` return `null` for null, `[]` for an empty input, and otherwise the `issue` texts in input order joined by `, ` inside square brackets (e.g. `[A-1, A-2]`).

`SyncLogger.row(id)` gives `0` for 0 and `r` followed by the number for negative IDs (`row(-5)` is `r-5`) without consulting the row manager; for positive IDs it gives the row's item text followed by ` (row <id>)`, or `<missing row <id>>` when the row manager throws `MissingRowException`.

`appendItem(ItemIdentity, sb)` appends issue text (as `appendIssue`) for issue identities and `<item type>/<id>` for any other item, using the long ID or the string ID as the identity has; `appendItem(rowId, sb)` does the same for the row's item, or appends `<missing row <id>>` for a missing row.

`forest(f)`/`appendForest` produce `<rowId>:<depth>:<item>` for each row of the forest in order, joined by `,` with no spaces (empty forest gives the empty string). `itemForest`/`appendItemForest` do the same taking items from the item forest, with `<missing row <id>>` for rows it does not know. `rows`/`appendRows` produce `<rowId>:<item>` joined by `,`.

`warnStructureException(e)` logs a warning and returns its text for four errors: structure missing or not accessible (text `cannot run because the structure does not exist or is not accessible for user <username>`), forest change prohibited by parent permissions (`Error while synchronizing <row text>: <problem details>`), edit denied (`cannot run under user <username> because he or she does not have permissions to edit the structure`), plugin access denied (`cannot run under <username>: Structure plugin is not enabled for this user`). The returned text starts with the prefix; the logged text carries the prefix twice when the prefix is non-empty (as the original does). Other errors are logged as `encountered a problem` via `warnExceptionIfDebug` and null is returned.

`SyncLogger.username()` returns the display name of the sync instance's owner (or of the current user when no instance was given), and `(null)` when there is no such user (for example a null user key).

`EmptyTemplate.isEnabled()` is always true, `getInitialStep()` is `__end`, and `configureNewStructure` does nothing to the structure (no setter or save is called). Its inherited defaults are unchanged (see `NewStructureTemplate`).
`EmptyTemplate.createStep(step, params, context)` always throws `StructureTemplateException` whose message is `context.getText("s.tpl.error.unknown-step", context.htmlEncode(step))`.

`NewStructureTemplate` defaults: `getCreateButtonTextKey()` is `s.tpl.btn.finish.name`; `prepareNewStructureUrl(s)` is `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=` followed by `s.getId()` (e.g. `...?s=42`); `shouldRedirectForNewStructure()` and `hasCustomFinalStep()` are false.

`NewStructureTemplateStep.END_STEP` is `__end`, `START_STEP` is `__start`, `CREATE_STRUCTURE` is `__create`. `NewStructureTemplateStep.Direction` has FORWARD and BACK in that order; `isBack()` is true only for BACK.

`StructureTemplateException` is a checked exception: `(message)` sets the message, `(message, cause)` sets both, and `(cause)` sets the cause with the message equal to `cause.toString()` (null when the cause is null).
`ColumnDisplayMode.AUTO_FIT` is 1 and `SCROLLABLE` is 2; `isValid` is true for 1 and 2 only (false for 0, 3, 11, -1). The class has no public constructor.
`RowDisplayMode.ONE_LINE` is 11 and `TEXT_WRAPPING` is 12; `isValid` is true for 11 and 12 only (false for 1, 2, 10, 13). The class has no public constructor.
`StructureViewBean.EMPTY` has ID 0, empty name and description, null owner, an empty `getPermissions()` list and `ViewSpecification.EMPTY` as specification.

`StructureViewBean.Builder.build()` with a non-zero ID, a non-blank name and a specification builder gives a bean with that ID and name, the description (empty string when unset), an equal copy of the owner (null when unset), equal copies of the rules (empty list when unset) and the specification built from the builder.

`StructureViewBean.Builder.build()` throws `IllegalStateException` (message starting `builder is not in valid state: `) when the ID is null or 0, the name is null or blank (only whitespace), or no specification builder is set. `isValidExceptId()` is true when name is non-blank and a specification is set; `isValid()` additionally requires a non-null, non-zero ID (a negative ID counts as valid).

`StructureViewBean.getOwner()` returns a new copy on each call (equal but not the same instance) and `getPermissions()` returns a new list of cloned rules each call; modifying the returned list does not affect the bean.

Two `StructureViewBean`s built from equal inputs are equal and have equal hash codes; a difference in ID, name, description, owner, rules or specification (for example only the column display mode) makes them unequal.

A new `StructureViewBean.Builder` has every property unset: `getId`, `getName`, `getDescription`, `getOwner`, `getSpecification` return null, `hasOwner()` and `hasPermissions()` are false and `getPermissions()` is an empty list. Setters store the values; `setPermissions` stores a copy (null unsets, an empty collection makes `hasPermissions()` true); `setOwner` stores a copy; `getSpecification()` returns the very builder that was set.

`new StructureViewBean.Builder(bean)` copies ID, name, description, owner, rules and a builder of the bean's specification, so `build()` on it gives a bean equal to the original; `new Builder(null)` gives an empty builder.
`StructureViewBean.Builder.clone()` returns an independent copy: changing the clone's ID, name, rules or its specification builder's columns does not change the original builder, and vice versa.

`a.updatePropertiesOf(b)` copies into builder b each of ID, name, description, owner, rules and specification that is set (non-null) in a, leaving b's other properties unchanged; afterwards b's specification builder is the same instance as a's.
`new StructureViewMenuItem(view, preferred)` returns the same view from `getView()` (null allowed) and the flag from `isPreferred()`.

`ViewSettings.ALL_PAGES` contains exactly STRUCTURE_BOARD, ISSUE_VIEW, PROJECT_TAB and GADGET; `PAGES_WITH_DEFAULT_VIEW` exactly STRUCTURE_BOARD, ISSUE_VIEW and PROJECT_TAB; `NO_PAGES` is empty. All three are unmodifiable.

`ViewSettings.EMPTY_SETTINGS` and the result of building a fresh `ViewSettings.Builder` are undefined: `isDefined()` false, `getAssociatedViews()` an empty list, `getDefaultViewForPage` null for every page, `hasView` false. After `makeDefined()` (and no views) the built settings are defined with an empty list and are not equal to `EMPTY_SETTINGS`.

`ViewSettings.Builder.addView(id, false)` appends a view that is on all menus (`getMenuPages()` equals `ALL_PAGES`) and default nowhere; `addView(id, true)` also makes it default on STRUCTURE_BOARD, ISSUE_VIEW and PROJECT_TAB. `addViews(ids...)` appends each as non-default, in order; `addViews(null)` does nothing. Builder methods return the builder.

Adding a view ID that is already in a `ViewSettings.Builder` first removes the old entry, so each ID appears once; with a negative index the view moves to the end. Example: views 1,2,3 then `addView(-1, 1, null, null)` gives 2,3,1; `addView(0, 3, null, null)` gives 3,1,2. The index is checked against the size before the removal and adjusted when the removed entry was before it.

`ViewSettings.Builder.addView(index, id, menu, defaults)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an ID of 0 or less (message `cannot set parameters for view <id>`) and `IndexOutOfBoundsException` (message `bad index <index>`) when the index is greater than the current number of views; index equal to the size appends.

In `ViewSettings.Builder.addView(index, id, menu, defaults)`, null or empty menu pages mean all pages and null or empty default pages mean none; menu pages outside `ALL_PAGES` and default pages outside `PAGES_WITH_DEFAULT_VIEW` (such as GADGET) are dropped.

`ViewSettings.getDefaultViewForPage(page)` returns the ID of the first view, in list order, that is default for the page, or null. COMPONENT_TAB and VERSION_TAB are treated as PROJECT_TAB; null and any page not in `ALL_PAGES` (e.g. ISSUE_NAVIGATOR, the deprecated board-with-details page) are treated as STRUCTURE_BOARD. GADGET is never a default page.
`ViewSettings.hasView(id)` is true when a view with that ID is in the list; false for null, for an unknown ID and for undefined settings.

`ViewSettings.getAssociatedViews()` is unmodifiable, and the built settings do not change when the builder is changed afterwards. `getViews()` of the builder returns a new list (null when undefined) and `setViews` copies the list (null makes it undefined); association builders with view ID 0 are skipped by `build()`.
`new ViewSettings.Builder(settings)` copies the views of defined settings in order, so building it gives settings equal to the original; for null or undefined settings the builder is undefined.
Two `ViewSettings` are equal when both are undefined or both have equal view lists (same order); hash codes agree with equality.

`ViewSettings.AssociatedView.isOnMenu(page)` and `isDefault(page)` check the page against its menu and default pages after mapping COMPONENT_TAB and VERSION_TAB to PROJECT_TAB and null or other pages outside `ALL_PAGES` to STRUCTURE_BOARD. Its `getMenuPages()` and `getDefaultPages()` are unmodifiable.

`ViewSettings.AssociatedView.Builder.build()` returns null when the view ID is 0 (any other ID, even negative, builds). A built association with unset menu pages has `ALL_PAGES` as menu pages and with unset default pages has an empty set.

`ViewSettings.AssociatedView.Builder.setMenuPages`: null, an empty set or a set equal to `ALL_PAGES` leave the menu pages unset (`getMenuPages()` null). The deprecated board-with-details page is replaced by STRUCTURE_BOARD and PROJECT_TAB; other pages outside `ALL_PAGES` are dropped, which can leave an empty (but set) menu, giving a view on no menu. The caller's set is not modified; `getMenuPages()` returns a copy.

`ViewSettings.AssociatedView.Builder.setDefaultPages` keeps only pages in `PAGES_WITH_DEFAULT_VIEW`; null or an empty set leaves default pages unset (`getDefaultPages()` null). `getDefaultPages()` returns a copy. `new Builder(view)` copies view ID and pages from an association, and `new Builder(null)` gives view ID 0.
Two `ViewSettings.AssociatedView`s are equal when view ID, menu pages and default pages are equal; hash codes agree.

`ViewSpecification.EMPTY` and a spec built from a fresh `ViewSpecification.Builder` have no columns, column display mode 1 (`AUTO_FIT`), row display mode 11 (`ONE_LINE`) and no pins; the two are equal.

`ViewSpecification.Builder.setColumnDisplayMode` stores 1 or 2 and replaces any other value with 1; `setRowDisplayMode` stores 11 or 12 and replaces any other value with 11. Both return the builder; the built spec reports the stored modes.

`ViewSpecification.Builder.addColumn(key)` gives the new column the csid one greater than the largest csid of the builder's columns that parses as an integer (non-numeric csids such as `main` are ignored; with none the first csid is `1`). Example: after `addMainColumn()`, `addColumn("a")` gets `1` and `addColumn("b")` gets `2`; with an existing csid `7`, the next is `8`.

`addMainColumn()` appends a column with key and csid `main`; `addFieldColumn(f)` a `field` column with parameter `field`=f; `addTimeAggregateColumn(f)` and `addFieldSumColumn(f)` both a `field` column with `field`=f and `aggregate`=`sum`; `addProgressColumn()` a `progress` column with no parameters; `addIconsColumn(f1, f2...)` an `icons` column with parameter `fields` = the list of the given strings. All except `addMainColumn` use the next numeric csid, and all return the builder.
`addTPColumn()` appends an `icons` column with parameter `fields` = [`issuetype`, `priority`] and a name taken from the localized text for the key `s.w.column.tp.label` (needs Jira's i18n).

`addColumn(key, csid)` appends a column builder with that key and csid and returns it, so further changes to it show up in the next `build()`. `addColumns(builders...)` appends the given builders by reference; null does nothing. `removeColumn(csid)` removes every column builder whose csid equals the argument (null removes those with a null csid).
`ViewSpecification.Builder.build()` keeps the column order and silently drops column builders with a null or empty csid or key.
`ViewSpecification.getColumns()` and `getPins()` are unmodifiable lists, and later changes to the builder's column list or display modes do not change an already built spec.

A built `ViewSpecification` shares the builder's pin list: adding to the list returned by the builder's `getPins()` after `build()` makes the new pin appear in the spec's `getPins()` (as the original does). `setPins` replaces the builder's list with a copy (null gives an empty list), after which earlier specs no longer change.
`ViewSpecification.Builder.getColumns()` returns the live mutable list of column builders (changes through it affect the builder); `setColumns` copies the given list (null gives an empty list).

`new ViewSpecification.Builder(spec)` copies columns, both display modes and pins, so its `build()` equals the spec; null gives defaults. `clone()` copies the column builders and pins, so changing a column's parameters or the pins in the clone does not affect the original.
Two `ViewSpecification`s are equal when columns, column display mode, row display mode and pins are equal; specs differing only in row display mode are unequal but have the same hash code.

`ViewSpecification.Column.Builder.build()` throws `IllegalStateException` (message starting `column builder is not in valid state: `) unless csid and key are both non-empty; `isValid()` reports that. The built column returns the csid, key and name (name may be null).

`ViewSpecification.Column.getParameters()` is never null (empty when the builder had none) and is a deep, unmodifiable copy: putting into it, or into a list nested in it, throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, and changing the builder afterwards does not affect the column. Entry order is preserved.

`Column.Builder.setParameter(name, value)` stores a copy of the value (lists and maps copied deeply, so later changes to the caller's list do not show) and creates the map on first use; a null value or `removeParameter(name)` removes the entry; a null name throws `NullPointerException`. Values must be `String`, `Integer`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, or lists or string-keyed maps of these; anything else (for example a `Float`, a null inside a list, or a map with a non-string key) throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Returns the builder.

`Column.Builder.getParameters()` is null until a parameter is set and returns the live map afterwards. `setParameters(map)` stores a deep mutable copy, and null or an empty map makes `getParameters()` null. `setStringListParameter(name, a, b)` sets the parameter to the list [a, b].

`new ViewSpecification.Column.Builder(column)` copies csid, key, name and a mutable deep copy of the parameters (null when the column has none); null gives an empty builder. `clone()` gives a copy whose parameter map is independent of the original's.
Two `ViewSpecification.Column`s are equal when csid, key, name and parameters are equal; hash codes agree.

ComparableTuple is a final class implementing Comparable<ComparableTuple> with no public constructor. Its public members are exactly: the constant NIL; the static factories of(long), of(double), of(String), of(String, String), of(long, long), of(String[]), of(Long[]), of(String, long), of(String, long, String) and of(java.util.List) each returning a ComparableTuple; and compareTo(ComparableTuple), equals(Object), hashCode() and toString().

of(long), of(double) and of(String) each return a one-element tuple holding the given value; of(long) and of(double) never throw (NaN and infinities are accepted), of(String) accepts the empty string but throws IllegalArgumentException when the string is null. With int literals, of(999) and of(-5) resolve to the long factory and hold integer numbers.

of(String, String), of(long, long), of(String, long) and of(String, long, String) return tuples of their arguments in argument order, e.g. of("x", 7, "y") holds the three elements "x", 7, "y". of(String, String) throws IllegalArgumentException if either string is null; of(String, long) if the string is null; of(String, long, String) if the first or the last string is null. of(long, long) never throws.

of(String[]) and of(Long[]) return a tuple of the array elements in order. The array is copied: changing the array after the call does not change the tuple (of(new String[]{"a","b"}) still equals of("a","b") after element 0 of the array is set to "z"). A null array throws IllegalArgumentException; an empty array gives an empty tuple equal to NIL. The tuple has no mutators, so it is immutable.

Null elements inside the array passed to of(String[]) or of(Long[]) are not rejected at creation (as the original does). Such a tuple later throws NullPointerException from hashCode() and when the null is compared against a number at the same position; toString() prints the null element as the text null.

of(java.util.List) builds a tuple from the list elements in order. Each element must be a String, any java.lang.Number, or a ComparableTuple; a nested ComparableTuple is flattened, its elements inserted in its place. Example: of(Arrays.asList("a", of(1, 2), 3L)) equals of(Arrays.asList("a", 1L, 2L, 3L)) and prints ('a',1,2,3). An empty list gives an empty tuple.

of(java.util.List) throws IllegalArgumentException when the list is null, when any element is null (e.g. Arrays.asList("a", null)), or when any element is not a String, Number or ComparableTuple (e.g. a list holding new Object()).

compareTo compares the tuples position by position up to the shorter length and returns the result of the first position that differs. Two strings compare with String.compareTo (case-sensitive), so the raw String.compareTo difference may be returned. Examples: of(1, 2) < of(1, 3); of("b", "a") > of("a", "z"); of("a", 5).compareTo(of("a", 5)) == 0.

At the same position a number is always smaller than a string, whatever their values: of(5).compareTo(of("a")) < 0, of(999).compareTo(of("0")) < 0 and of("0").compareTo(of(-5)) > 0. The result for such a mixed position is exactly -1 (number on this side) or 1 (string on this side).

When all shared positions are equal, the shorter tuple is smaller (-1) and the longer one larger (1); equal lengths give 0. So of("a") < of("a", "b") and NIL is smaller than every non-empty tuple, e.g. NIL.compareTo(of(0)) < 0.

Two numbers at the same position compare first by their long values (truncated toward zero) and, only when those are equal, by their double values; the result is -1, 0 or 1. Integer and floating numbers therefore compare by value: of(2L) equals of(2.0), of(2.5) > of(2L) and of(2.5) < of(3L); numbers of any Number class from the List factory compare the same way.

A NaN element has long value 0 and its double comparison is never equal, so comparing a NaN against any number whose long value is 0 (including another NaN, or 0, or 0.5) returns 1 from both sides (as the original does, this breaks the Comparable contract); of(Double.NaN) is not equal to another of(Double.NaN), though an instance equals itself. Against numbers with a non-zero long value NaN behaves like 0.

equals is true for the same instance, and otherwise only for another ComparableTuple whose compareTo result is 0; it is false for null and for objects of other classes. Thus of(2L).equals(of(2.0)) is true, and of("a", "b") equals of(new String[]{"a", "b"}).

hashCode starts at 0 and for each element in order multiplies the running value by 31 (int arithmetic, wrapping) and adds the element's hash: String.hashCode() for strings and Double.hashCode of the doubleValue() for numbers. Equal tuples such as of(2L) and of(2.0) therefore have equal hash codes, and NIL has hash code 0.

toString returns the elements in parentheses, separated by commas without spaces; strings are wrapped in single quotes without any escaping, numbers use their own toString. Examples: of("x", 7, "y") gives ('x',7,'y'); NIL gives (); of(1.5) gives (1.5); of(2.0) gives (2.0); of(Arrays.asList("a", of(1, 2), 3L)) gives ('a',1,2,3).

NIL is a shared tuple with no elements: it prints as (), has hash code 0, equals any other empty tuple (such as of(new String[0]) or of(Collections.emptyList())) and sorts before every non-empty tuple.

info(source, message) writes the text source + " " + message at INFO level to the wrapped org.slf4j.Logger, and warn(source, message) writes the same text at WARN; the three-argument forms pass the Throwable along with the text. The first message for a source key is always written. The logger's enabled levels are not consulted before throttling.

After a message for a source key is written, further messages for the same key arriving within the interval (elapsed System.nanoTime() difference less than or equal to the interval) are dropped and counted. info and warn share one throttle per key; different keys are independent. The default interval is 5 minutes; the two-argument constructor sets it in nanoseconds.

When a message for a key is written again after some were dropped, a summary line is written first: "<count> info log entries from <source> were not shown" at INFO if the first call ever made for that key was info, or "<count> warnings from <source> were not shown" at WARN if it was warn. The count is then reset to 0; no summary is written when nothing was dropped.

reset() forgets all source keys: the next message for any key is written at once and pending dropped counts are discarded without a summary line. setInterval(long) changes the suppression interval (nanoseconds, unvalidated) for all keys from the next message on.

new I18nText(key, args...) stores the key and a new array of the arguments in which null stays null, any java.lang.Number is kept as the same object and every other object is replaced by its toString() text (e.g. a StringBuilder "a" becomes the String "a"). Calling it with no arguments stores an empty array; passing a null varargs array throws NullPointerException. The no-argument constructor leaves both key and arguments null.

getI18nKey returns the key and getArguments returns the stored array itself (not a copy). setI18nKey replaces the key without checks, and setArguments stores the given array as is (no copying and no normalization; null allowed).

Two I18nText objects are equal when they have exactly the same runtime class, equal keys (null equals null) and argument arrays equal element by element (null array equal only to a null array). new I18nText("k", 1, "a") equals new I18nText("k", 1, "a") but not new I18nText("k", 1L, "a") (Integer 1 vs Long 1). Equal objects have equal hash codes (computed in the 17/37 style of Apache Commons Lang HashCodeBuilder).

toString returns the key alone when the arguments array is null or empty (null when the key is null); otherwise the key immediately followed by the arguments joined with commas, null arguments as empty text: key a.b with arguments x and 1 gives a.bx,1; key k with arguments null and x gives k,x.
I18nText binds to JSON with Jackson through the properties i18nKey and arguments: the main constructor is the Jackson creator for these two properties, and the getters expose them for serialization.

new IndexedForest(forest) wraps the forest without copying (a null forest throws NullPointerException). size() is the forest size, getForest() returns the same forest instance, depth(i) and row(i) return the forest's depth and row ID at position i (out-of-range positions fail like the forest's accessors). The forest must not change while the index is used.

subtreeEnd(i) returns the position just past the last descendant of row i, i.e. the first later position whose depth is not greater than row i's depth, or size() if none. For rows [1,2,3,4] with depths [0,1,1,0]: subtreeEnd(0)=3, subtreeEnd(1)=2, subtreeEnd(2)=3, subtreeEnd(3)=4. Any negative position returns size(); a position at or beyond size() throws an index exception.

parent(i) returns the position of row i's parent, or -1 if row i has depth 0 or i is negative. For depths [0,1,1,0]: parent(1)=0, parent(2)=0, parent(0)=-1, parent(3)=-1. For depths [0,1,2,1]: parent(2)=1 and parent(3)=0.

firstChild(i) returns i+1 when that row exists and is exactly one level deeper than row i, else -1; firstChild(-1) returns 0 for a non-empty forest and -1 for an empty one; other out-of-range positions give -1. nextSibling(i) returns subtreeEnd(i) when that position exists and has the same depth as row i, else -1 (also -1 for a negative position or one at or beyond size()). For depths [0,1,1,0]: firstChild(0)=1, firstChild(1)=-1, nextSibling(1)=2, nextSibling(2)=-1, nextSibling(0)=3, nextSibling(3)=-1.

children(i) returns a com.almworks.integers.IntIterator over the positions of row i's direct children in forest order (empty for a leaf or an out-of-range position other than -1); children(-1) and roots() iterate the positions of the top-level rows. childrenRows(i) returns the children's row IDs (not positions) as a new LongList, or LongList.EMPTY when there are none. rows(indices) lazily maps each position from the given IntIterator to its row ID.
root(i) returns the position of the top-level ancestor of row i (i itself when row i has depth 0); a negative i is returned unchanged. For depths [0,1,2,0,1]: root(2)=0, root(4)=3, root(3)=3.

IndexedRowTree.create(forest) returns a new tree holding the whole forest under its super-root (same order and nesting, so toForest() reproduces the rows and depths). getNodeWithRowId(id) returns the node for that row ID, the super-root for ID 0, and null for an ID not in the tree; hasRow(id) tells whether a node with that ID is in the tree and is false for 0.

Nodes added later through insertNode or appendForest become findable by row ID. remove(node) unregisters the node and all of its descendants: afterwards hasRow is false and getNodeWithRowId returns null for each of them. moveNode keeps the moved nodes registered.

Row IDs must be unique: creating a second node with an ID already in the tree raises AssertionError when Java assertions are enabled; without assertions the new node silently replaces the old one in the lookup.
new IndexedRowTree() and new IndexedRowTree(size) create empty trees (only the super-root); size is only a capacity hint, and a negative size throws IllegalArgumentException.

isMutuallyExclusive(LongList, LongList) is true when the lists share no value (order and duplicates do not matter) and true when either list is empty; e.g. [1,2] and [3,4] give true, [1,2] and [2,5] give false. The lists are not modified; null lists throw NullPointerException.
isMutuallyExclusive(LongSet, LongSet) is true when the two sets have no common value, including when either is empty, and false otherwise; null sets throw NullPointerException.

new ItemDisplayable(description, url) stores both values unchanged and without checks; getDescription() and getUrl() return them (url may be null). There are no setters and no custom equals, hashCode or toString (identity semantics).

new JavaListToLongListAdapter(list, f) is a read-only LongList view: size() is the source list's current size and get(i) applies f to the source element at i on every call (nothing cached), so later changes to the source list show through. An out-of-range index throws what the source list throws (typically IndexOutOfBoundsException). Other LongList operations (iteration, toNativeArray, equals) work through these two methods.

The static getters (getProjectManager, getIssueManager, getConstantsManager, getVersionManager, getOptionsManager, getUserManager, getGroupManager, getUserUtil, getPluginAccessor, getPermissionManager, getApplicationProperties, getAvatarManager, getComponentClassManager, getGlobalPermissionManager, getProjectComponentManager, getJiraAuthenticationContext) and getComponent/getComponentOfType return null when Jira cannot provide the service, otherwise a dynamic proxy implementing the requested interface that forwards to the service. The proxy is cached per interface class, shared by all these methods: later calls return the same proxy until the cache is cleared.

Each call on a returned proxy runs with the calling thread's context class loader set to the class loader of the real service object, restored afterwards even when the call fails; an exception thrown by the service is rethrown as is (not wrapped).

getOSGiComponentInstanceOfType(interface) looks up an OSGi service and returns it wrapped in the same kind of class-loader-switching proxy, or null if none; this result is not cached, every call creates a new proxy.
clearCaches(), afterPropertiesSet() and destroy() all empty the shared proxy cache, so the next lookups wrap freshly obtained services; clearUserCaches(user) does nothing.

withThreadContextClassLoaderOf(object, code) runs code.call() with the current thread's context class loader set to the loader of object (if object is a Class, that class's loader; otherwise the loader of its runtime class, null for bootstrap classes), returns its result, and always restores the previous context class loader, also when code throws; the exception propagates unchanged. A null object throws NullPointerException before the code runs.

Every JiraFunc property extractor (for example PROJECT_ID, PROJECT_KEY, ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_KEY, ISSUE_SUMMARY, ISSUECONSTANT_ID, PROJECTCONSTANT_NAME, USER_KEY, LABEL_LABEL, OPTION_ID, LINK_ID) returns null for a null argument and otherwise the corresponding getter value of the Jira object (which may itself be null). ISSUETYPE_SUBTASK is the exception: it returns Boolean.FALSE for null and otherwise whether the issue type is a sub-task type.

Some constants declare their result class so that La.array works: PROJECT_ID, PROJECT_KEY, PROJECT_DESCRIPTION, PRINCIPAL_NAME, GROUP_NAME, FIELD_NAME, ISSUECONSTANT_ID, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME_LOCAL, VERSION_ACTIVE (Boolean), VERSION_SEQUENCE, VERSION_PROJECT, the PROJECTCONSTANT_* constants, ISSUE_PROJECTID, ISSUE_PRIORITYID, ISSUE_RESOLUTIONID, ISSUE_STATUSID, ISSUE_SUMMARY, ISSUE_DESCRIPTION, ISSUE_ENVIRONMENT, ISSUE_KEY, ISSUE_ORIGINAL_ESTIMATE, ISSUE_REMAINING_ESTIMATE, ISSUE_TIME_SPENT, ISSUE_TOTAL_TIME, ISSUE_VOTES, ISSUE_WATCHES, USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER, the ISSUE_ASSIGNEE/REPORTER/CREATOR constants and their *ID forms, the four Timestamp constants, LABEL_LABEL, SECURITY_LEVEL_ID, SECURITY_LEVEL_NAME and OPTION_ID. Others, such as PROJECT_NAME, ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_WORK_RATIO and ISSUE_ISSUETYPEID, declare none, so La.array on them throws UnsupportedOperationException.
USER_NAME and APPLICATION_USER_NAME both map an ApplicationUser to its display name (not the login name); USER_KEY maps it to its user key.

VERSION_ACTIVE returns TRUE for a version that is not archived and FALSE for an archived one (null for null). NEGATED_ISSUECONSTANT_SEQUENCE returns the negated sequence of an issue constant, null if the constant or its sequence is null. ISSUETYPE_NAME and ISSUECONSTANT_NAME_LOCAL return the translated name, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME the raw name.

ISSUE_TOTAL_TIME returns the issue's time spent plus remaining estimate, a missing one counting as 0; it returns null when both are missing, when the sum is 0 or negative, or for a null issue (e.g. spent 3600 and no estimate gives 3600).
OPTION_NAME returns the option's value, or for an option with a parent option the parent's value, " - ", then the option's value (e.g. Europe - France); null for null.
GENERICVALUE_LONG_ID and GENERICVALUE_STRING_ID read the field id of a GenericValue as Long or String; null input or any exception during reading gives null.

KEY_PROJECT, ID_PROJECT, ID_ISSUETYPE, ID_STATUS, ID_PRIORITY, ID_RESOLUTION, ID_COMPONENT, ID_VERSION and ID_OPTION look the object up through the corresponding Jira manager (obtained via JiraComponents) on every call and return null for a null argument without querying; ID_COMPONENT also returns null when Jira reports the component as not found. USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER resolves a key through JiraUsers.byKey.

ISSUE_ISSUETYPEID, ISSUE_PRIORITYID, ISSUE_RESOLUTIONID and ISSUE_STATUSID return the ID of the issue's type, priority, resolution or status (null if the issue or the constant is null). ISSUE_ASSIGNEE, ISSUE_REPORTER and ISSUE_CREATOR map an issue to the ApplicationUser of its assignee, reporter or creator key (null when the key is null).
VALID_ISSUE_KEY returns its argument unchanged when Jira's key syntax check accepts it as an issue key, otherwise null (null for null); it does not check that the issue exists.
CANONICAL_VERSION_NAME maps a Version to CoreIdentities.canonicalVersionName of its name; a null version gives null.

accessibleBy(user, permission) returns a predicate on Project that is FALSE for null and otherwise asks Jira's permission manager (fetched once at creation) on every call whether the user (null = anonymous) has the permission on the project; it declares Boolean as result class. If no permission manager is available it returns a constant-false function (AssertionError with assertions enabled). browseableBy(user) is accessibleBy with the browse-projects permission.

hasCustomField(field) returns a constant-false function for a null field. Otherwise it returns a predicate on Project that is FALSE for null, TRUE for every project when the field is configured for all projects, and else TRUE only for projects whose IDs were in the field's associated projects when hasCustomField was called (a snapshot).
byKey(null), from(null), getKeyFor((User) null), getKeyFor((ApplicationUser) null) and toDirectoryUser(null) all return null.

For non-null input, byKey, from and getKeyFor(User) return Jira's own user conversion result while the thread context class loader is temporarily set to the loader of Jira's user classes and restored afterwards (also on exceptions); getKeyFor(ApplicationUser) and toDirectoryUser call Jira's conversion directly without switching.

copyParameters(params, allowNull, makeImmutable, verify) with a null or empty map returns null if allowNull is true, otherwise an immutable empty map if makeImmutable is true, otherwise a new mutable empty map. A non-empty map gives the same result as mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, params).

mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, maps...) returns a new insertion-ordered map with the entries of all maps in argument order; a later map's value replaces an earlier one's for the same key while the key keeps its first position; null maps and a null varargs array are skipped. Values are deep-copied. With makeImmutable the result and all nested lists and maps are unmodifiable (UnsupportedOperationException on change); otherwise all are mutable.

With verify true, mergeParameters throws IllegalArgumentException with message "null key" for a null key, "non-string key: <key>" for a non-String key, and the checkValidParameter error for an invalid value.

copyParameter(value, makeImmutable) converts org.json JSONArray/JSONObject values to plain lists and maps, copies lists into new ArrayLists and maps into new insertion-ordered maps whose keys become String.valueOf(key), recursively; any other value (including null) is returned as the same object. With makeImmutable the new lists and maps are unmodifiable.

checkValidParameter accepts String, Integer, Long, Double and Boolean values and lists and String-keyed maps of such values (recursively, JSONArray/JSONObject converted first). It throws IllegalArgumentException with message "null value" for null, "invalid value type: <class name>" for other types (Float, Short, BigDecimal included), "invalid map: non-string key <key>" for a non-String key; nested errors are wrapped as "invalid list: invalid value at index <i>: <inner>" or "invalid map: invalid value for key <key>: <inner>" with the inner exception as cause. A cyclic or too deep structure gives message "stack overflow".

unwrapJsonCollection turns a JSONArray into a java.util.List and a JSONObject into a java.util.HashMap (recursively, JSON null becoming Java null) and returns any other value unchanged; a conversion failure becomes IllegalArgumentException with message starting "failed to convert json object: ". jsonToList and jsonToMap do the conversion directly and throw NullPointerException for null.
La implements java.util.function.Function and Predicate: apply(x) returns la(x) and test(x) returns accepts(x).

accepts(x) is true when la(x) is truthy: non-null and not equal to Boolean.FALSE, Integer 0 or Long 0. So results Double 0.0, Short 0, the empty string and TRUE are accepted; null, FALSE, 0 and 0L are rejected.
La.adapt(f) returns a La that calls the java.util.function.Function f; a null f throws NullPointerException.

La.constant(r) returns a function always returning r (null allowed). constant(Boolean.TRUE) returns the same shared instance as constantTrue() and constant(Boolean.FALSE) the same as constantFalse(); these return TRUE and FALSE for every argument.
La.isEqual(v) returns a predicate whose result is TRUE when v.equals(argument); for a null v it is TRUE only for null arguments.

La.inCollection(c) is TRUE when c.contains(argument), seeing later changes to c, and a constant-false function for null c. La.instanceOf(cls) is TRUE for non-null instances of cls, constant false for a null class. La.cast(cls) returns the argument when it is an instance of cls and null otherwise; for a null class it always returns null.

La.compose(g, f) returns x -> g.la(f.la(x)) (null intermediate results passed through) and throws NullPointerException if either is null; the result declares g's result class. h.apply(f) equals compose(h, f) and h.supply(g) equals compose(g, h).

La.self() is a shared identity function. La.notNull() is a shared predicate giving TRUE for non-null and FALSE for null arguments. La.stringValue() maps an object to its toString() and null to null, declaring String as result class. La.notNull(la, onNull) returns la's result or onNull when that is null, keeps la's result class, and throws NullPointerException for a null la.
La.fromMap(map, rClass) returns a function giving map.get(argument) (null when absent, live view of the map) with rClass as declared result class; a null map throws NullPointerException.

filter(Iterable) returns a new ArrayList of the elements, in order, that this function accepts (empty for null). filter(Iterator) returns a lazy filtering iterator (empty iterator for null). filterIterable(Iterable) returns a lazy Iterable that filters a fresh source iterator each time it is iterated (empty for null).

hashSet(c) and linkedHashSet(c) return a new HashSet/LinkedHashSet of this function's results for all elements, including null and falsy results, duplicates collapsed (LinkedHashSet in first-occurrence order); a null collection gives an empty set.

arrayList(Collection) and arrayList(Iterator) return a new mutable list of the results of all elements in order, falsy and null results included; null input gives a new empty list. arrayList(from, false) leaves out non-truthy results. arrayList(T...) maps the varargs the same way, but for a null or empty array it returns an immutable empty list.

iterator(Iterable) and iterable(Iterable) give lazy views of the results, computed on each next(); remove() is forwarded to the source iterator; a null source gives no elements. transform(Iterator) and transformIterable(Iterable) are lazy mapping views too, but a null source fails with NullPointerException when used.

La.longList(c, f) returns a new LongList of f's results that are non-null and strictly positive, in order (zero, negative and null results dropped), and LongList.EMPTY for a null or empty collection. La.intList does the same for Integer results, returning IntList.EMPTY for null or empty input.

addTo(from, to, acceptFalsy) adds the result for each element of a collection or iterator to `to` in order, skipping non-truthy results when acceptFalsy is false, and returns `to`; a null source adds nothing.

array(c) and array(c, acceptFalsy) return a new array whose component type is the function's declared result class, with the results in order; with acceptFalsy false, non-truthy results are dropped and the array is shortened. A null collection gives an empty array. If no result class was declared, UnsupportedOperationException is thrown (even for null input); if the collection yields more elements than its size() reported, IllegalStateException.

mapInto(c, map) puts result -> element for each element, mapInto(c, map, valueFn) puts result -> valueFn(element); elements whose key is null are skipped, later duplicates overwrite earlier ones, and the given map is returned. hashMap(c) / hashMap(c, valueFn) return a new HashMap and linkedHashMap(c, valueFn) a new LinkedHashMap built the same way; null collections give empty maps.

indexOf(list, sample) and lastIndexOf(list, sample) return the first/last position whose result equals sample (null matches null), or -1 if none or the list is null. find(c, sample) returns the first element whose result equals sample (null matches null), or null if none or the collection is null or empty.

any(iterable) is true when at least one element is accepted, stopping at the first one, and false for null or empty input. not() returns a predicate that is TRUE exactly when this function rejects the argument. and(second) returns a predicate that is TRUE when both accept, evaluating second only if this one accepts.
memoize() returns a non-thread-safe wrapper that calls the original once per distinct argument (by equals) and returns the stored result afterwards; null arguments and null results are cached too.

memoizeConcurrent() returns a thread-safe caching wrapper that calls the original at most once per argument in the absence of races; null arguments or null results throw NullPointerException (AssertionError when assertions are enabled). Null results are never cached.

comparator(cmp) returns a Comparator comparing two arguments by cmp applied to their results; a null cmp throws IllegalArgumentException with message "comparator is null". La.comparator(f) orders arguments by the natural order of f's results with null results first. La.LaComparator(function, comparator) throws IllegalArgumentException "function is null" or "comparator is null" for null arguments. La.ComparableComparator.compare returns 0 for two nulls, -1 if only the first is null, 1 if only the second is null, else b1.compareTo(b2).

liftToList() returns a function from an Iterable to the list of this function's results for its elements in order (all results kept): null maps to null, an empty iterable to an immutable empty list, otherwise a new mutable list.

image(c) returns a live read-only Collection view of this function's truthy results over c (non-truthy results skipped, duplicates kept); size() re-evaluates the function over the whole source each time; a null source gives an immutable empty list.

The La.FilterIterator returned by filter(Iterator) reads ahead: hasNext() advances the source until an accepted element is found and repeated hasNext() calls do not advance further; next() returns that element or throws NoSuchElementException when none is left; remove() always throws UnsupportedOperationException.

La.TransformIterator.hasNext() reports whether the source has more elements, next() returns the function's result for the next source element (possibly null), and remove() removes from the source iterator.
La2 implements java.util.function.BiFunction: apply(a, b) returns la(a, b). la(a1) returns a one-argument La that, given a2, returns la(a1, a2).
La2.sum adds two Integers with int arithmetic (overflow wraps, e.g. sum.la(2, 3) is 5); null arguments throw NullPointerException.
La2.uncurry(curried) returns a two-argument function computing curried.la(a1) and applying the result to a2; if curried.la(a1) is null, the result is null.

La2.const2(r).f() returns a two-argument function always returning r. La2.bind2(f).create() returns a two-argument function that ignores its first argument and returns f.la(second). The holder classes La2.Const and La2.Binder2 can also be created with their public constructors.
La3 is a La of its first argument: la(a1) (and therefore apply(a1)) returns a La2 that, given (a2, a3), returns la(a1, a2, a3).
La3.bind12(f).create() returns a three-argument function that returns f.la(a1, a2) and ignores the third argument; La3.Binder12 can also be built with its public constructor.

Limits holds int constants all equal to 190: MAX_MODULE_KEY_LENGTH, MAX_ITEM_STRING_ID_LENGTH, NODEID_MAX_LENGTH, MAX_SPEC_ID_LENGTH, MAX_NAME_LENGTH, MAX_USER_KEY_LENGTH and MAX_PATH_LENGTH. The class cannot be instantiated.

getMessageWithCauseChain(t) returns the toString() of t and of each cause in order, separated by "; ", e.g. "java.lang.IllegalStateException: x; java.io.IOException: y"; it returns the empty string for null.

warnExceptionIfDebug(log, message, t) logs at WARN: when DEBUG is enabled on log, message with t attached; otherwise, for non-null t, the text message + " " + the cause chain text without a stack trace; for null t just message.

A LongFilteringIterator yields, in order, only the values of the source LongIterator that pass the filter: with a java.util.function.LongPredicate those for which it returns true, with a La<Long, ?> those whose result is truthy. Filtering [1,2,3,4] with an is-even predicate yields 2, 4. The La constructor throws NullPointerException for a null filter.

split(iterator, filter) reads the whole source and returns a com.atlassian.jira.util.lang.Pair of two independent iterators over those values in order: first the accepted ones, second the rejected ones (e.g. [1,2,3,4] with is-even gives 2,4 and 1,3).

new LongListHashIndex(list) maps each value of the list to its position; indexOf(v) returns that position or -1 for a value not in the list, and size() is the number of distinct values. For a value occurring more than once the last occurrence's position is kept. Later changes to the list are not seen.
new LongListHashIndex(map) indexes an explicit value-to-position map, skipping entries with a null key, a null value or a negative value; indexOf returns the mapped position or -1.

new MapObject(JSONObject) wraps the given org.json object without copying (later changes show through); null is treated as an empty object. new MapObject(Map) builds a new JSONObject from the map. MapObject.from(obj) returns a MapObject for a JSONObject or a java.util.Map and null for anything else, including null. EMPTY is a shared instance with no keys.
isEmpty() is true when there are no keys; has(key) is true when the key is present; keys() iterates the current keys; get(key) returns the raw value or null when absent.

getObject(name) returns the value as a MapObject when it is a JSONObject or a java.util.Map, otherwise null (absent or other type). traverse(name) does the same but returns EMPTY instead of null, so chained lookups never fail.

getString(key) returns the value as text (a number 5 gives "5") or null when absent. getLong/getInt return the numeric value (numeric strings parsed) or 0 (or the given default) when absent or not convertible. getBoolean(key) is true for Boolean.TRUE or the string true in any case, otherwise false; getBoolean(key, default) returns the default when absent or not convertible. These follow org.json's lenient opt rules.

getLongList(key) and getIntList(key) return the numeric elements of the array under key in order (longValue()/intValue()), skipping non-numeric elements including numeric strings and nulls; a java.util.Collection value is treated like an array. A null key, an absent or non-array value or an empty array gives an immutable empty list.

getObjectList(key) returns the array elements that are JSON objects or maps, each as a MapObject; getRawObjectList(key) returns the raw elements skipping Java nulls; getStringList(key) returns elements as text; getList(key, extractor) applies the extractor to each index and keeps non-null results. transform(array, extractor) does the same for an array and returns an immutable empty list for a null or empty array. MAP_OBJECT_ARRAY_EXTRACTOR turns an element into a MapObject via from (null otherwise).

asImmutableMap() returns an unmodifiable map deep-converted from the JSON content (nested objects as maps, arrays as lists), built on the first call and cached; a top-level JSON null value makes it throw NullPointerException; JSON conversion errors become IllegalArgumentException starting "failed to convert json object:".

toString() returns the backing JSON object's compact JSON text. equals requires exactly the same class and backing JSON objects that are equal by JSONObject.equals; hashCode is the backing object's hashCode.

MapUtils.isSubMap(map, sub) is true when every entry of sub is present in map with an equal value (null values compared too); an empty sub is a sub-map of any map. E.g. {a=1,b=2} contains {a=1} but not {a=2} or {c=1}. Null arguments throw NullPointerException.

longOrZero(n) and doubleOrZero(n) return n's longValue()/doubleValue() or 0 for null. longOrNull(n) returns the same Long object if n is a Long, else a boxed longValue(), null for null; doubleOrNull likewise for Double. The (argument, function) forms apply the function first and return 0 (or null) without calling anything when the argument or the function is null.
nonNegativeLong and nonNegativeDouble return the value clamped to at least 0 (null counts as 0); nonNegativeDouble(NaN) stays NaN and -0.0 gives 0.0.

nonNegativeDoubleAddOrNull(a, b) is null if both are null, else the sum of the clamped values (null as 0). longAddOrNull(Number, Number) is null if both are null, the longValue of the non-null one if one is null, else the sum (wrapping, no clamping). longAddOrNull(long, Long) returns a when b is null, else a + b.
NumericFunctions.equals(a, b) is true when both are null, false when exactly one is, else a.equals(b), so Long 1 and Integer 1 are not equal.
Ref holds a value in the public field value: new Ref() holds null, new Ref(v) holds v, and the field can be read and assigned freely. toString() returns String.valueOf(value), i.e. "null" when empty.
A new RowTree contains only the super-root (row ID 0, flags 0, no children): toString() is the empty string and toForest() is an empty forest.

appendForest(forest) adds copies of all forest rows as new nodes with flags 0, the forest's top-level rows placed after the current last top-level node, keeping order and nesting. Appending a forest 1(2,3),4 to an empty tree gives toString() (1(2,3),4); appending forest 5 afterwards gives (1(2,3),4,5).

appendForest(forest, underNode, afterNode) places the forest's top-level rows as children of underNode right after afterNode, or before all existing children when afterNode is null. E.g. a tree (1(9)) with forest 2,3 appended under node 1 with afterNode null gives (1(2,3,9)).

The six-argument appendForest(forest, parentNode, afterNode, parentIndex, flags, rowFilter) copies the whole forest when parentIndex is negative, otherwise only the descendants of forest position parentIndex; copied top-level rows go under parentNode after afterNode (first if null), every new node gets flags, and a row rejected by a non-null rowFilter is skipped with its whole subtree. It returns the forest position just past the copied range (the forest size when copying everything).

insertNode(rowId, flags, parent, after) creates a leaf node and inserts it as a child of parent right after `after`, or as the first child when `after` is null, and returns it. moveNode(node, parent, after) detaches the node with its subtree and inserts it the same way, returning the node.
remove(node) detaches the node with its whole subtree from the tree; removing the super-root throws IllegalArgumentException with message "cannot remove super-root".
toForest() returns a new ArrayForest of all nodes except the super-root in depth-first pre-order, top-level nodes at depth 0, without flags; later tree changes do not affect it.

RowTree.Node.toString() returns the row ID when the node has no flags, else the row ID, # and the flags in decimal, e.g. 42 or 42#3. toFullString() (and append(StringBuilder)) gives the row ID (omitted for 0) followed, when there are children, by the children's full strings in parentheses separated by commas without spaces, e.g. 5(6,7(8)); flags are not shown.

RowTree.Node.hasFlags(mask) is true when all bits of mask are set (always true for 0); addFlags(mask) ORs the bits in. findFirstWithFlags(flags) returns this node or the first descendant in depth-first pre-order having those flags, or null.

RowTree.Node exposes getRowId, getParent (the super-root for top-level nodes), getFirstChild, getLastChild, getNextSibling and getPrevSibling (null when absent). getParent on the super-root or a detached node returns null, or raises AssertionError when assertions are enabled.

RowTree.Node.writeTo(rows, depths, depth) writes the subtree in pre-order: if depth >= 0 the node itself first with that depth, then each child with depth + 1; with -1 only descendants are written, children at depth 0. collectDirectChildren(collector) adds the row IDs of the direct children in order.

RunnableE.andThen(another) returns an action that runs this action and then another; if this action throws, another is not run and the exception propagates. A null another fails with NullPointerException only when the combined action runs, after this action has completed.
SpecParams.getObject(name) returns the nested value as a SpecParams when it is a JSON object or a java.util.Map, and null if it is absent or of another type.

getAttributeParameter(name, expectedFormat) reads an object under name with keys id, optional format and optional params and returns an AttributeSpec with that id, the params map (null if absent or not an object) and expectedFormat as format. It returns null when the object is missing, when both a stored format and expectedFormat exist and the stored one is neither expectedFormat's ID nor the ID of ValueFormat.ANY, or when the spec cannot be built (e.g. blank id or a colon in it). With a null expectedFormat the standard ValueFormat named by the stored format is used, and null is returned if there is none. getAttributeParameter(expectedFormat) uses the name attribute.

STRING_LONG parses a string as a decimal long after trimming whitespace (" 42 " gives 42) and returns null for null or unparsable text (decimals, out of range).
