The module keeps its key but carries no behaviour: the replacement holds no vendor certificate and verifies no certificate or signed licence material, and nothing in the plugin depends on such a check (SPEC.md 1.1).

Asked whether an update is available for any plugin key (the plugin's own, a companion app's, an unknown or an uninstalled one), it answers no (false), immediately and without contacting the Atlassian Marketplace or any other server; it throws nothing (SPEC.md 1.8). The `info-popup` "update available" flags it feeds are therefore always false.
Clearing the plugin's caches (all users or one user) changes nothing about its answers; it keeps no state that a clear could affect.

Generating its fragment inserts, as top-level rows, the issues returned by the fixed JQL query `issue in issueHistory() ORDER BY lastViewed DESC` (the current user's recently viewed issues, most recently viewed first), searched with the plugin's sorted search as the current StructureAuth user (see `helper`, searchAndSortQuery). A `jql` parameter, if present, is ignored for the inserted rows.

The `limit` parameter (integer) caps the number of inserted issues: a missing, zero or negative limit means no limit; a positive n inserts at most the first n issues of the query order. When a refresh inserts at least `limit` issues (limit > 0), the generation reports that this generator hit its limit (shown as generation trouble). The default form value of `limit` for a new inserter is 1000.

When the plugin is not enabled for all projects, the query is narrowed with the plugin's configured project-scope clause before searching, so issues from projects outside the scope are never inserted; when it is enabled for all projects the query is used unchanged.

Each generated fragment asks to be regenerated after a fixed interval even if nothing changed: 1 minute by default, set in milliseconds by dark feature `structure.issue.inserter.refreshRecentInterval` (read once, when the component is created). It behaves like a TimedUpdateChecker with that interval.

Besides the timer, the fragment is regenerated when a changed-items batch contains any item of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-sprint`, `:type-version`, `:type-project`, `:type-project-component` or the (misspelt) `com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-membership`; or an issue already inserted; or an issue inside the project scope that now matches the query (checked with a match search, whose failure counts as no match). Changes of issues outside the scope are ignored.

If the Jira search fails with a SearchException, a warning is logged and the fragment stays empty; nothing is thrown to the generation. When the Jira index is unavailable the search gives no issues (see `helper`).

Shown on a form, the parameters give `limit` (and `jql` when stored). Building parameters from a form returns a map with `jql` (the form value with leading/trailing horizontal whitespace removed, validated as JQL only when non-blank: a parse error or Jira validation error is added under field `jql`; a present but blank value gets error `s.ext.gen.jql.param.jql.error.no-jql`) and `limit` (the form value as an integer, or null).
Without a `jql` parameter the inserter offers no action handler, so it takes no part in deciding user edits (add, move, remove) of the rows it inserted.
The hard maximum generation time is dark feature `structure.gfs.generationTimeHardLimit` in seconds (default 600), clamped to at least 5 and at most 1800, read once when the component is created.

The generation time limit of a forest spec is the per-structure property `generationTimeLimit` (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_PROPERTY) of the spec's structure when the spec has a structure id and the stored value is non-zero; otherwise the global property `generationTimeLimit` (AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY, default 30). The result is capped at the hard limit (min of the two); it is not raised to the 5 s minimum. A null spec or one without a structure id uses the global value.

Setting a time limit below 5 s throws IllegalArgumentException `Generation time limit should be more than 5s` (5 itself is accepted); above the hard limit throws IllegalArgumentException `Generation time limit should be less than hard limit`; for a non-null spec without a structure id it throws IllegalArgumentException `Forest spec should contain structure id to specify time limit`. Nothing is stored in these cases.

Setting a valid limit for a null spec stores the global property `generationTimeLimit`; for a structure spec it stores the structure property `generationTimeLimit` and immediately applies the new limit to every generation currently running for any spec with that structure id.

The manager tracks, in memory per node and per forest spec, the generations running for that spec (in the order registered). Registering a generation succeeds unless the spec is blocked; for a blocked spec the generation is not registered and the caller is told so, so it does not run.
Unregistering a generation reports whether it was registered for that spec; once a spec has no running generations and is not blocked, its entry is dropped (an unknown spec reports false).

Blocking a spec marks it stopped even when nothing is running, clears any recorded generator times, and returns (unmodifiable) the generations that were running, so the caller can cancel them; blocking an already blocked spec returns an empty list and changes nothing. The 'block if running' variant blocks only a spec that has an entry (something running or already blocked) and otherwise does nothing.

Unblocking returns true exactly when the spec was blocked; it clears the recorded generator times and keeps the entry only while generations are still registered. A spec is reported blocked only while marked so; nothing is blocked after a restart (state is not persisted).

Per-generator timings of a spec (generator row id to time) are kept only while the spec is blocked: recording them for a spec that is not blocked is ignored, and reading them for a spec with nothing recorded gives an empty map. Blocking or unblocking clears them.

When a refresh runs out of its generation time limit, the spec is blocked and every generation running for it is cancelled; the forest then stays stopped until resumed (REST `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/resume`).
An issue identity whose numeric id is between 1 and 2147483647 maps to that id as its code, without storing anything; mapping it again always gives the same code.

Any other identity (non-issue items, and issues with an id of 0, negative or above 2147483647) gets a negative code assigned on first request: -1, then -2, -3, ... in request order. The same identity (by equals) always gets the same code for the life of the node; the mapping is in memory only and starts again from -1 after a restart.
Decoding gives null for 0, the issue identity with that id for a positive code, the identity assigned to a negative code, and null for a negative code never assigned.
Mapping a null identity throws IllegalArgumentException `itemId must not be null`. Mapping and decoding are safe for concurrent use (one lock guards the assigned codes).

Each transient row created gets the next odd id 1, 3, 5, ... (the n-th row since start gets 2n-1), held in memory only; numbering starts again at 1 after a restart. The row keeps its item identity, semantics, creator id and original id. This is the store behind the transient rows of `structure-row-manager`.

Semantics, creator id and original id are kept as 32-bit values: a value outside the int range is logged as an error and kept as 0. Reading a row returns a TransientRow with the stored creator and original ids.

Reading a row by id throws MissingRowException for an id that is not transient (0, negative or even) and for a transient id that was never created (or was lost on restart); otherwise it returns the row with its item resolved lazily by `item-resolver` per the access mode.

Scanning a list of ids visits them in the given order and stops as soon as the predicate returns false. An id that is not transient throws IllegalArgumentException `<id> is not a transient row id`. A transient id with no row goes to the missing collector, or throws MissingRowException when no collector is given.
Finding rows of an item reports the ids of all its transient rows, newest first, until the consumer returns false (the search then reports that it was stopped); a null item reports nothing.

Finding rows of an item made by one creator reports only the rows with that creator id, newest first, stopping when the consumer returns false. The per-creator index behind it is cached and dropped after 60 s (dark feature `structure.ftrm.cache.timeout`; concurrency `structure.ftrm.cache.concurrency`) and rebuilt from all rows of the creator on the next use, with the same results. If loading the index fails, a warning is logged and nothing is reported.

Transient rows are never deleted one by one, also not when their creator generator is gone: they live until restart. The only removal drops all transient rows at once, either keeping the numbering (the next id continues) or resetting it so the next row is 1 again; nothing in the plugin triggers that removal on Jira 9.12.

On start it registers usage statistics with `statistics-manager`: `transientTotalRowCount` (number of transient rows) together with `transientTotalRowCount.<bin>` where bin is the first of 1000, 10000, 30000, 50000, 70000, 100000, 200000, 300000, 400000, 500000, 1000000, 2000000, 5000000 not below the count, or `inf`; and `transientRowsItemCreatorCacheMissToTotal` = index rebuilds / index lookups, left out while no lookup happened.

Item identities of transient rows are encoded through `item-identity-mapper`; if a stored code can no longer be decoded, the row counts as missing (MissingRowException with message `cannot unmap item identity from idx <code>, row <id> cannot be used`, or the id goes to the missing collector with a warning).

Creating a short-lived generator stores the given GeneratorSpec in memory only and returns the next odd id 1, 3, 5, ... (counting from start of the node; never persisted, restarted at 1 after a restart). This is the store behind `generator-manager`'s transient generators.

Reading by an id returns the stored spec as given at creation, or null for an id never created or already deleted. For an id that is not positive and odd: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws AssertionError; with them disabled 0 and negative ids give null.

Deleting returns true when a generator with that id was removed and false when there was none; ids are never reused. Non-transient ids behave as for reading (AssertionError with assertions on). Reads and writes are safe concurrently (read/write lock).

Each HTTP session id has its own clipboard forest, kept in memory on the node: the first request for a session creates an empty clipboard, later requests return the same one. Clipboards are never shared between sessions and are lost on restart.

Adding (pasting) a fragment into a clipboard first empties it (except on a dry run), then puts the fragment at the top level whatever under/after/before were given. Each row becomes a new transient row (creator 0, original 0) with the same item and semantics, and the action result maps each old row id to its new id; with parameter `reuseRows` true and no id shared with the clipboard's rows, the fragment's row ids are kept. A dry run (`dryRun` true) changes nothing.

Removing from a clipboard is accepted only when the given row ids are exactly its top-level rows in their order, and then removes everything; any other row list fails with StructureException UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION. Move and copy actions on a clipboard always fail with UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION.

A clipboard's forest version has a random signature chosen when the clipboard is created and a counter starting at 0 that grows by the number of forest changes of each edit. An update request from the current version gets an empty incremental update; from a version at most 2 changes back an incremental update; from anything older or another signature a full update.

Clipboards not requested for more than 30 minutes (dark feature `almworks.attributes.dev.clipboard.timeout`, milliseconds; negative counts as 0) are emptied and dropped. The sweep runs when some clipboard is requested, at most once per minute, before the requested one is looked up; a later request for a dropped session gets a new empty clipboard with a new signature.

Clearing one session's clipboard removes all its rows and returns the forest update since the version before clearing; it returns null when the session has no clipboard. The clipboard itself stays. REST uses this after rows were moved through the clipboard (`viaClipboard`).
A backup restore empties and drops every clipboard of the node.
Manual adjustments are globally enabled unless dark feature `structure.gfs.manualAdjustments.enable` is false (default true); the value is read on first use and kept until restart.

A structure has manual adjustments enabled exactly when its structure property `manualAdjustments.enable` (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_PROPERTY) reads as `true` (ignoring case; missing means false). Enabling or disabling stores `true`/`false` there and then reports a change of item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-gfs-manual-adjustments/<structureId>` to ItemTracker.
Whether new structures get manual adjustments enabled is the global property `manualAdjustments.enableForNewStructure` (AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY, default false); setting it stores the boolean there.

Adjustments apply only to a forest spec equal to the plain unsecured spec of its structure (no version, transformation, title or user): for such a spec the structure id is used, for any other spec (or no structure) 0, which means no adjustments.

Adjustments are applied to a generated forest (and offered when handling user edits) only when they are globally enabled, the spec's structure id is positive and the structure has them enabled; when handling user edits, the current user must also pass the permission rule. Each structure gets one transient row (item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-gfs-manual-adjustments/<structureId>`, semantics 0, no creator, no original) created on first need and reused for the life of the node as the creator of adjustment rows; if it cannot be created, no adjustments are applied.

Who may make manual adjustments is set by dark feature `structure.gfs.manualAdjustments.editPermission`: unset or an unknown value lets every user; `EDIT`, `AUTOMATE`, `CONTROL` or `ADMIN` (ignoring case; CONTROL means ADMIN) requires that the current user's StructureManager.getStructurePermission for the structure includes PermissionLevel EDIT, AUTOMATE or ADMIN; no permission level means not allowed.

Applying an empty list of changes does nothing. A non-empty list is stored through `adjustment-store` (SPEC table AO_8BAD1B_MANUAL_ADJUSTMENTS), and afterwards, also when storing failed, a change of the structure's adjustments item is reported to ItemTracker so the forest regenerates. Deleting all adjustments of a structure goes through `adjustment-store` and also always reports that change. Structure id 0 reports nothing. Reading returns what `adjustment-store` holds.

On start it registers usage statistics with `statistics-manager`: `manuallyAdjustedStructuresCount` (structures with at least one stored adjustment), `manualAdjustmentsMovesCount`, `manualAdjustmentsAddsCount` and `manualAdjustmentsCount` (moves plus adds), counted over all stored rows each time statistics are taken.

For a field grouper's `fieldId` it provides the handler for user moves: system fields `priority`, `components`, `versions`, `fixVersions`, `labels`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `status` (changed through effects) and `project`, `issuetype`, `resolution`, `creator` (never changed). For a custom field id the handler depends on the field's type: single select, multi select, cascading select, labels, project picker, version picker (single or multiple), user picker, multi-user picker, group picker (single or multiple), the ScriptRunner single issue picker, and Insight/Assets object fields that support effects. Any other field, or an unknown custom field id, has no handler. The sprint grouper gets a sprint handler for the agile sprint field.

Groups without a value are folder items of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder` with string ids `s.grouper.field.+<name>`, for example `s.grouper.field.+no-priority`, `+unassigned`, `+no-reporter`, `+no-creator`, `+no-status`, `+unresolved`, `+no-issue-type`, `+no-project`, `+no-labels`, `+no-version` (affects and version fields), `+no-fix-version`, `+no-components`, `+no-option`, `+no-user`, `+no-group`, `+no-issue`, `+no-insight-object`; the group for rows that are not issues is `s.grouper.field.+not-an-issue`; for sprints the empty group is `s.grouper.sprint.no-sprint`. Moving into a field's empty group clears the field.

Moving a row that is neither an issue nor a memo/planning task into any group except the not-an-issue group is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.move-non-issue`; into the not-an-issue group (or to no group) it is neither blocked nor given an effect. Moving an issue, memo or planning task into the not-an-issue group is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.move-issue`.

For a row being created (an issue without id, or a memo/planning task with id Long.MAX_VALUE) a move only validates the target value (where the field has rules, see the project and archived checks) and on success gives an empty effect; no Jira change is made for the new row.

Moving an existing issue to a group of a single-valued field produces the CoreEffects effect setting the field to the target value, or to null when moved into the empty group: setIssuePriority, assignIssue, setIssueReporter, setIssueStatus, setSingleSelectCustomField, setCascadeCustomField, setProjectPickerCustomField, setSingleVersionCustomField, setSingleUserCustomField, setSingleGroupCustomField; the ScriptRunner issue picker gets its own set effect. Moving to a status group equal to the issue's current status gives an empty effect.

For multi-valued fields, moving an existing issue into the empty group sets the field to an empty collection (CoreEffects.setIssueComponents, setIssueAffectedVersions, setIssueFixVersions, setCustomFieldOptions, setCustomFieldUsers, setCustomFieldGroups, setCustomFieldVersions, and the label and Insight set effects). Moving to another group gives a 'move' effect that replaces the source group's value by the target value (source null when coming from outside a group), for the effect provider modules `com.almworks.jira.structure:components-effect-provider`, `:affects-versions-effect-provider`, `:fix-versions-effect-provider`, `:labels-effect-provider`, `:multi-labels-custom-field-effect-provider`, `:multi-select-custom-field-effect-provider`, `:multi-user-custom-field-effect-provider`, `:multi-group-custom-field-effect-provider`, `:multi-versions-custom-field-effect-provider` (and the Insight object provider).

Moving an issue between sprint groups gives the CoreEffects.setSprint effect for the target sprint id (null for the no-sprint group) with extra parameters `from` = the source sprint id and `sameBoard` = true. Reordering sprint groups is always blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.reorder` (with the manual-adjustment suggestion when possible).

Project, issue type, resolution and creator are never changed: moving an existing issue is allowed with an empty effect only when the target group's value equals the issue's current one (project id, issue type id, resolution id, creator user key; moving into the empty group counts as the value null, so an unresolved issue may go to `+unresolved`), and otherwise blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.project`, `.issueType`, `.resolution` or `.creator`. A new issue placed in a group with a different value is blocked with the same key plus `.new-issue`.

Every effect produced is sent with parameter `sendNotifications` = true. When the move is applied, the effect provider registered for the effect's module key is found through `extension-service`; no provider blocks with `s.ext.gen.block.no-effect-provider`, an error response blocks with its localized error, an empty response is a no-op, otherwise the change is offered with the provider's localized success message. The undo effect returned when it runs (again with `sendNotifications` true) becomes the inverse; undoing before it ran does nothing, and running the inverse records no further undo.

For a new issue placed in a components, affects-version or fix-version group, a value from another project than the issue's is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.component-project` or `.version-project` (arguments: value name, issue key), or the `.new-issue` variant when the issue has no key yet; an archived version is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.create.archived.version` (argument: version name). For a multi-version custom field both checks use `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.version-project` (no new-issue variant) and the same archived key.

Moving an existing memo or planning task changes it through the memo field effect: module `com.almworks.jira.structure:memo-field-effect-provider` with parameters `memo` = the item identity text, `field` = the field id, `value` = the target value in the stored field format of SPEC (null when cleared). This works for priority, assignee, reporter, sprint and custom fields that `structure-field-manager` knows; status, Insight fields and custom fields it does not know are blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.move-non-issue`.

For multi-valued fields of an existing memo or planning task, moving into the empty group sets the field to null; otherwise the new value is the current value (as read with validation) without the source value and with the target value appended unless already present, items compared by version id, component id, label text, option id, user key or group name. Multi-valued custom fields not known to `structure-field-manager` are blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.move-non-issue`.

For a new memo or planning task placed in a components or version group: an item with no project value is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.itemfield.block.not-supported` (argument `project`); a version from another project with `s.ext.gen.grouper.itemfield.block.version-project.new-item`, an archived version with `s.ext.gen.grouper.itemfield.block.create.archived.version`; a component from another project with `s.ext.gen.grouper.itemfield.block.component-project` (the key meant for existing items, as the original does). Arguments are the value name and the item key (`MEMO:<id>` / `PT:<id>`).

Reordering groups of these fields is never supported: moving the empty group or the not-an-issue group, or placing a group right after one of them, is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.invalid-order`; a group whose value (or both neighbours' values) cannot be read is blocked with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.invalid-group`; any other reorder with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.reorder-not-supported`. When manual adjustment is possible in that context the message is wrapped in `s.ext.gen.block.suggest-adjustment`.

Link type options list every Jira issue link type (IssueLinkTypeManager) with id, name and labels: when the outward and inward descriptions are equal, the outward label is `s.gen.links.direction.outward` and the inward label `s.gen.links.direction.inward` (each with the description as argument) and the 'any' label is the description itself; otherwise outward and inward are the descriptions and 'any' is `s.gen.links.direction.any` (outward, inward). Hidden link types are listed the same way from `hidden-links-helper`.

The link direction of a generator is inward when boolean parameter `inward` is true; otherwise parameter `direction` ignoring case: `outward`, `inward` or `any`; missing or any other value means outward.

The link type is parameter `linkTypeId` (a long); missing gives no link type; otherwise Jira's link type with that id, but only if `hidden-links-helper` says it is visible to users (an unknown or hidden type gives none).

When issue linking is disabled in Jira, filling a new form, showing parameters on a form and building parameters from a form all throw GeneratorUnavailableException with message `linking is disabled` and the localized `s.gen.links.error.links-disabled`.

Building parameters from a form: no `linkTypeId` adds error `s.gen.links.error.no-type-selected` under field `linkTypeId` and returns an empty map; an unknown or hidden type adds `s.gen.links.error.no-type` (argument: the id) and returns an empty map; otherwise the map has `linkTypeId`, `direction` (the form's string as given, possibly null) and, when the direction is any, `shortestPaths` = true.

Showing parameters on a form puts `linkTypeId` and the parsed `direction` there (plus the support object for the template). For a summary, when the link type is found, it adds `linkTypeName` (the type's name) and `linkDirectionName` (the option label for the direction); otherwise it adds nothing.

For a moved row that is not an issue, link handlers yield (let other generators decide) with `s.ext.gen.links.yield.not-an-issue`. An issue that cannot be resolved is blocked with `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue`; one the current user lacks Jira's LINK_ISSUES permission on (unless StructureAuth security is overridden) is blocked with `s.ext.gen.links.block.no-link-perm`. A new issue without an id counts as id Long.MAX_VALUE.

Handling a link change for a new issue (id Long.MAX_VALUE) gives an empty effect; making an issue a child of itself (issue = new parent) is blocked with `s.gen.links.error.link-to-self`; anything else gives an effect with its inverse.

When the link effect is evaluated: linking disabled blocks with `s.gen.links.error.links-disabled`; a missing or hidden link type blocks with `s.gen.links.block.no-link-type`; the issue, old parent and new parent are checked as for moved rows (no-issue, no-link-perm).

The links to change are worked out once, as the current user, through `bulk-link-processor` (for parent P being left, new parent Q, issue X, the given link type): leaving P removes the link P->X when the direction includes outward and X->P when it includes inward (each if it exists). Joining Q: outward creates Q->X unless it exists; inward creates X->Q unless it exists; any creates Q->X only when neither Q->X nor X->Q exists. Removing all links: with inward, X's outward links of the type; with outward, X's inward links of the type; only links whose other end the user may link (LINK_ISSUES or security overridden).

Nothing to change gives an empty effect. Otherwise the effect is described as `s.ext.gen.links.effect.add` (link Q-X), `.remove` (link P-X), `.move` (P-X, Q-X) or, for remove-all, `s.ext.gen.links.effect.removeAllOfType` (link type name, X's key). A link is written `<parent key> <phrase> <child key>` where the phrase is the link type's inward description when the direction is inward or any, else its outward description.

Running the effect opens a new link transaction as the current user, removes each planned link that still exists, creates each planned new link and commits. The inverse re-creates the removed links and removes the created ones, with the same checks (old and new parent swapped); undoing a remove-all is described with `s.ext.gen.links.effect.add` for one link or `s.ext.gen.links.effect.add.n` (first link, number of further links, issue key) for more.

To build an issue-update effect it makes Jira issue input parameters that keep every value not provided (IssueInputParameters.setRetainExistingValuesWhenParameterNotProvided(true, true)), lets the provider fill in the new value, and validates with IssueService.validateUpdate as the current StructureAuth user. An invalid result becomes an error response whose message joins Jira's error messages and field errors with `, `.

When validation passes but the validated field values do not contain the target field id (the field is not on the issue's edit screen), the response is error `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with the field name and the issue key.

The resulting effect, when applied, first builds its undo effect (from the values before the change), then calls IssueService.update as the same user with EventDispatchOption.ISSUE_UPDATED and send-mail set from the effect's `sendNotifications` boolean parameter, and returns the undo.

A system field is identified by its Jira field id, which is also used as its name in messages. A custom field target is chosen by the effect's `customField` parameter, restricted to custom fields of a given type class or type keys; its name in messages is the parameter's description, or `<?>`.

Old/new value comparisons: two nulls are equal and a null never equals a non-null; non-null values compare by a key (for example the id), or by the custom field type's string form, or as strings with null read as the empty string.

When an effect batch is optimized, effects are grouped by the values of the given parameters (groups in first-seen order). If every group has one effect, the list is returned unchanged; otherwise each group is merged into one effect and groups that merge to nothing are dropped.

Merging a group of effects that set one value keeps the last effect. If earlier effects had other values for that parameter, the kept effect gets parameter `conflicts`: the distinct other values in first-seen order, a null value written as {"empty": true}; with no differing value the last effect is returned unchanged. An empty group merges to nothing.

An effect description with conflicts is rendered as `
M
`, where T is `s.ext.effect.conflict-resolution-warning` in the user's language, C the extra CSS classes joined by spaces, and M the HTML-encoded i18n text of the key with the arguments inserted unencoded (quotes around placeholders removed) using the user's locale. Encoding a plain value encodes its text (null as `null`); an i18n text is first localized for the current user.

It defines these field value types, by key: `single-user`, `single-date`, `single-duration`, `single-line-text`, `multi-line-text`, `single-project`, `single-version`, `single-issue-type`, `single-priority`, `single-date-time`, `single-number`, `multi-label`, `multi-version`, `multi-component`, `single-sprint` (only when the agile sprint services are available), `multi-user`, `single-group`, `multi-group`, `single-option`, `multi-option`. There is no resolution type. The catalogue is built once on first use and not refreshed.

Jira custom field type keys map to types: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:` `userpicker` single-user, `datepicker` single-date, `textfield` single-line-text, `textarea` multi-line-text, `project` single-project, `version` single-version, `float` single-number, `datetime` single-date-time, `labels` multi-label, `multiversion` multi-version, `multiuserpicker` multi-user, `grouppicker` single-group, `multigrouppicker` multi-group, `select` single-option, `multiselect` multi-option; `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-sprint` single-sprint (only when that type exists). Every other key has no type.

Each type writes and reads the per-field string stored in a generic item's `fields` map exactly as SPEC's AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM.C_PARAMETERS notes describe (user key, `yyyy-MM-dd`, milliseconds, JSON lists, project id as a floating number, and so on). A null value stores nothing; a stored string that cannot be read back (or names a missing user, version, option, ...) reads as null and is logged as a warning, never thrown.

User input is parsed per type: null gives null; texts treat `` as null; dates use Jira's date-picker format (blank gives null), falling back to ISO `yyyy-MM-dd`; durations use Jira's duration format (for example `2h 30m`, blank gives null) and give milliseconds; date-times fall back to ISO local date-time in the logged-in user's time zone; numbers, priorities and issue types by Jira id; single user, project, version, group, option and sprint values by id. When an input fails the editor form and a second accepted form exists, that one is tried before reporting an error.

An invalid duration reports `createissue.error.original.estimate.invalid` for `timeoriginalestimate`, `createissue.error.remaining.estimate.invalid` for `timeestimate`, `s.column.editor.timespent.error` for `timespent`, and Jira's parse error text for other duration fields.

For single-valued option-backed types (user, project, issue type, priority, version, group, option, sprint) a text input not found as an id is looked up by name. For multi-valued ones (versions, components, users, groups, options), when no element could be read and the input is text, it is split on commas, each part trimmed and looked up by id then name; unknown parts and duplicates (same id) are dropped and an empty result is null. Label lists drop nulls and duplicates, keeping order.

Validating a value against a field configuration fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.invisible-field` (field name) when the configuration hides the field, and with `s.ext.type.memo.error.required-field` (field name) when the value is empty (null, empty text or empty list) and the field is required. An empty label list validates to null.

For option-backed single values, a value that is not a valid option of the field's option source (per the configuration's option-source spec, for the current StructureAuth user) fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field` (field name, value's display text). For multi values, invalid elements fail with the same key listing their display texts, but the failure still carries the valid elements (or null when none), so a read keeps the valid ones; with no invalid element the valid list is returned (null when empty).

Display text: users by display name, dates in Jira's date-picker format, durations in the plugin's duration format, priorities and issue types by their translated name in the user's language, sprints and groups by name; other values through `value-text-converter`.

HTML views: single-line text is HTML-encoded; multi-line text is rendered as wiki markup when the field's renderer is `atlassian-wiki-renderer`, else as text with `
` line breaks; durations as formatted text and sprints and groups as encoded names (empty string for null); labels, components, priority and issue type through Jira's velocity templates (`templates/plugins/fields/view/view-label.vm`, `templates/jira/issue/field/components-columnview.vm`, `.../priority-columnview.vm`, `.../issuetype-columnview.vm`); custom-field-backed types through their Jira type's `column-view` template, or `view` when it has none.

Values given to formulas: a date becomes the epoch milliseconds of the start of that day in the formula's time zone (time format); a date-time its epoch milliseconds; a duration its milliseconds (duration format); a number the number; users, projects, issue types, priorities, versions, components, groups, options, sprints and labels become item identities (lists for multi-valued types); texts stay text. Null stays null.

For backups, option-backed values are exported as a map from stored value to the option's name (looked up without a user, ignoring restrictions), and on restore are found again by name; a name not found fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field` (field name and the name, or the stored value). For multi values the found ones are kept and the missing names listed in the error. Other types export and resolve nothing.

The catalogue starts with these Jira system fields in this order, each with its type: `summary` (single-line text, renderer `jira-text-renderer`), `description` (multi-line text, `atlassian-wiki-renderer`), `assignee` (user), `duedate` (date), `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent` (duration), `environment` (multi-line text, `atlassian-wiki-renderer`), `reporter` (user), `priority`, `issuetype`, `project`, `labels` (labels), `versions`, `fixVersions` (multi-version, frother-control renderer), `components` (multi-component, frother-control renderer). A field whose type is missing is left out.

After the system fields come Jira's custom fields (in CustomFieldManager order) whose type key maps to a type of `structure-field-type-manager`; others are left out. A custom field's renderer type comes from its item in Jira's default field layout, when there is one.

A system field's id is its Jira field id and also its plain name; its localized name is the Jira field's name key translated in the requested locale. A custom field's id is `customfield_<n>`, its plain name the untranslated name, and its localized name Jira's translation for the locale, or the untranslated name when there is none.
Looking up a field by id returns the catalogue entry or null for an id not in it (an unsupported custom field, or an unknown id).

The catalogue is reloaded from Jira at most 60 s after it was built (a tuning setting in seconds; its key is not contract), so new or removed custom fields show within a minute; clearing the plugin's caches reloads it at the next use; clearing one user's caches does nothing. A failure to build it surfaces as StructureRuntimeException.

The fixed system fields (summary, description, assignee, due date, estimates, time spent, environment, reporter, priority, issue type, project, labels, affects and fix versions, components) are also available directly, built once and not refreshed; they are used by memos, planning tasks, groupers and effectors.

For memos the field configuration shows and allows editing exactly `summary`, `description`, `assignee`, `duedate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate` and `timespent`, requires none, and asks no Jira configuration.

Under the memo (and migration) configuration, an option-backed field's options come from the type's option source with no project and no filters, except `FIELD_OPTIONS` which gets `customField` = the field id; fields without options have none.
For a planning task the configuration is that of `jira-field-visibility-service` for the task's stored project and issue type (read without validation) and the current StructureAuth user.

Planning-task option sources: field `project` uses PROJECTS with `checkStructureConfig`, `checkCreateIssues`, `excludeInactive`; field `assignee` uses USERS with `excludeInactive`, `checkAssignable` and the task's project; otherwise by source PROJECTS (`checkStructureConfig`, `excludeInactive`), VERSIONS, COMPONENTS, USERS, SPRINTS (`excludeInactive`), ISSUE_TYPES (`excludeSubtasks`), FIELD_OPTIONS (`customField`, `excludeInactive`, and `issueTypeId` when known). The task's project id is passed for ISSUE_TYPES, PRIORITIES, VERSIONS, COMPONENTS, FIELD_OPTIONS, SPRINTS and assignee only. When the project is not visible to the user, every option-backed field gets the empty source `EMPTY`.

Applying field updates checks each one: a field the configuration does not let edit fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.uneditable-field` (field name in the user's language); otherwise the type's validation applies (see `structure-field-type-manager`). Each failure is reported for its field and that field is not written; valid ones are written in SPEC's stored format: summary to the item name, description to the item description, others into the `fields` map (null removes the key, an empty map removes `fields`, and the estimate fill-in applies).

When an item is created, every catalogue field except `summary` that the configuration requires and that is neither being set nor already stored is checked as if set to null, so a missing required field fails (with `s.ext.type.memo.error.required-field`, or `uneditable-field` when the user may not edit it).

A planning task is visible to a user only when its stored project is visible to that user per `jira-field-visibility-service` (no project means not visible); memos are always visible by this check (structure ownership is checked elsewhere).

For backup restore, a planning task needs its project key and issue type name: no key fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.project-required`, an unknown key with `s.ext.type.memo.error.project-not-found` (key); no issue type name with `s.ext.type.memo.error.issue-type-required`, a name matching no Jira issue type exactly with `s.ext.type.memo.error.issue-type-not-found` (name). Otherwise, and for memos, the configuration lets every field be shown and edited and requires none.
For planning tasks, `project` and `issuetype` are always visible and required, even when the project or issue type is unknown.
`timespent` is never visible, required or editable for planning tasks; `timeoriginalestimate` and `timeestimate` are checked as Jira's `timetracking` field.

Any other field is visible only when both the project and the issue type are known, Jira's field layout for that project and issue type has the field and does not hide it, and the field is on the create-issue screen (any tab) of the project's issue type screen scheme for that issue type; a custom field on that screen counts only when it is in scope for the project and issue type. Without a screen scheme or create screen nothing else is visible.

A visible field is required when its field layout item is required, it has no default value, and it is on the create screen. Defaults: reporter and priority always have one; assignee has one unless the project's default assignee is the project lead (assignee type 2) and the lead is missing or not assignable (ASSIGNABLE_USER); description and custom fields have one when the field configuration for the project and issue type gives a non-empty default value.

A visible field is editable when: `assignee` and the user has ASSIGN_ISSUES on the project; `reporter` and MODIFY_REPORTER; `duedate` and SCHEDULE_ISSUES; a custom field that Jira marks not editable never; the agile sprint field with SCHEDULE_ISSUES; anything else always. Permissions are checked for the user on the project as for issue creation; without a project they fail.

A project is visible to a user when it is a valid option of the PROJECTS option source with `checkStructureConfig`, `checkCreateIssues` and `excludeInactive` for that user (anonymous when the user is null); a null project is never visible.

Answers are cached per (project id, issue type id, user key) and dropped 60 s after they were computed (dark feature `FieldConfigService.refreshTimeout`, seconds); the per-user project option source expires 1 hour after its last use (dark feature `FieldConfigService.projectVisibilityLifespan`, hours). Clearing the plugin's caches drops both; clearing one user's caches drops only that user's entries. A failure to compute them surfaces as an unchecked exception.

The key of a memo is `MEMO:<id>`, of a planning task `PT:<id>`, of any other item null. The board link of a generic item is `<base URL>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<owning structure id>#layout=details&itemId=<HTML-encoded item identity>`.
For formulas, a memo or planning task gives: `key` its key; `name` and `summary` the item name; `description` the description (undefined/null when absent).

Formula field `history` gives the list of the item's history records as items `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group/<record id>` (from `generic-item-history-manager`); `created` the time of its create record and `updated` the latest record time (epoch ms); `creator` the user item of the create record's author (null when none). For many items at once only `history` is loaded in bulk.

Any other formula field name is turned into a field id (`affectedversions` -> `versions`, `fixversions` and also `versions` -> `fixVersions`, `attachments` -> `attachment`, `originalestimate` -> `timeoriginalestimate`, `remainingestimate` -> `timeestimate`) and looked up in `structure-field-manager`; if not found, a field whose name matches after removing whitespace, punctuation and control characters and lower-casing is used; none gives undefined. The value is read with validation (invalid reads as null) and given in its formula form (see `structure-field-type-manager`).

When a memo or planning task is created or edited from client values, `description` is taken from the values and the field values from the `params` map (field id to editor value); only fields known to `structure-field-manager` that the configuration shows and lets edit are used, others are ignored. Each is parsed as user input; a parse error is recorded under the field id in the user's language.

On edit, any parse error means nothing is applied. On create, all values are applied and all errors collected, and required fields not given are checked too. Validation errors (see `generic-item-field-config-service`) are added under the field id unless that field already has an error. The remaining `params` are then passed on to the item type (for example a memo's colour and icon).

A field view of an item identity loads the item through GenericItemManager.getItem (its cache; no permission or app-access check) and gives nothing when the item does not exist; its configuration comes from `generic-item-field-config-service` for the item's type and the current user. For a list of identities it keeps the order and leaves out missing items.

Reading a field reads the stored string (summary from the name, description from the description, others from `fields`), converts it with the field type and validates it with the configuration: a failure reads as null, except for multi-valued option-backed fields (versions, components, users, groups, options) where the valid elements are kept and only invalid ones dropped.
The fields of a view are the catalogue fields whose ids are keys of the item's `fields` map; keys unknown to `structure-field-manager` are skipped.

Reading or setting a custom field through the typed accessors throws IllegalArgumentException `Field <field name> is unsupported` when `structure-field-manager` does not know it and `Field <field name> is of wrong type` when its type does not match the accessor (text accepts single- and multi-line text).

An update builder records field values for one identity (the last value per field wins) and stores them as `memo-manager` and `planning-task-manager` describe: it reads the item through GenericItemService as the current user, applies and validates the recorded values (failure: StructureException UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED with the field's localized message), then runs GenericItemService.validateUpdate and update and throws their exception, or UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED with the joined error messages when there is none.

The same builder can only validate: it gives the first problem as a localized text (field error, or the item service's error) or null when the update would pass, and stores nothing; `memo-field-effect-provider` uses this before applying a change.

When a backup is restored, a generic item's `fields` map is rebuilt only from the restored field values, validated with the migration configuration; a failing field throws StructureException UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED for that item with the field's message. Other parameters (such as a memo's colour) are kept.

Converting an issue to planning-task field values always starts with the issue's project and issue type, and uses the planning-task configuration of that project and issue type for the current StructureAuth user.

It then takes every other field of `structure-field-manager` (in catalogue order) that this configuration shows, is not excluded by the caller and exists as a Jira field: the issue's value is read and converted to the field's value with `field-information-provider`; fields it has no conversion for, and empty results, are skipped. Hidden fields (for example `timespent`, or fields not on the create screen) are never copied.

Copying into a planning task validates and writes these values like any field update (see `generic-item-field-config-service`): fields the user may not edit or whose value is invalid there are not copied and get a localized error under their field id in the caller's error collection; the others are written.
When a planning task is created with an issue as its sample, the issue's values are copied this way with `summary` excluded (the summary is given separately).

The maintenance schedule is kept in `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY` (through property-service): `maintenance.scheduled.enabled` (absent means true: scheduled maintenance is on by default), `maintenance.scheduled.time` (`H:M` without zero padding, e.g. `3:0`; absent, malformed, an hour outside 0..23 or a minute outside 0..59 each fall back separately to hour 3 and minute 0), `maintenance.scheduled.crontab.enabled` (absent means false) and `maintenance.scheduled.crontab.schedule` (absent means `0 3 * * *`). With nothing stored the schedule reports: scheduled, daily at 03:00, cron off, cron text `0 3 * * *`.

In daily-time mode the next run time is computed in the JVM default time zone as today at the stored hour and minute with seconds and milliseconds zero; if that instant is not strictly after now, it is the same hour and minute on the next calendar day. Example: at 02:59:30 with time `3:0` the next run is 03:00:00 today; at exactly 03:00:00 or later it is 03:00:00 tomorrow. (On a day where the hour does not exist because of a daylight-saving jump, Calendar lenient rules apply and the minute is set to 0 when the resulting hour moved past the requested one.)

In cron mode the next run time is the first instant strictly after now matched by the stored 5-field schedule (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in the JVM default time zone with seconds fixed to 0, using Spring's `CronExpression` semantics after prefixing the text with `0 ` (so the stored value is a standard 5-field crontab, e.g. `0 3 * * *` = daily 03:00, `*/15 * * * *` = every quarter hour).

Each time the next run is computed it is stored as `maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime` (epoch ms, decimal) and `maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime.tz` (the Java time-zone id it was computed in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`), and logged at WARN level. Asking for the next scheduled run time returns the stored value when it is positive; when it is absent or 0 it is computed and stored first.

When the stored `maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime.tz` differs from the JVM's current default time zone, the stored next-run instant is reinterpreted so that it keeps the same wall-clock time: the instant is converted to local fields in the saved zone (seconds and milliseconds zeroed) and those fields are then taken as local time in the current zone. The adjusted value is used for the due check and returned, but not written back. Example: 03:00 Europe/Berlin becomes 03:00 in the new zone.

When the plugin starts (unless the component is already stopped) the module registers one recurring job with scheduled-job-manager under the key `maintenance.scheduled.job` (whose last run time scheduled-job-manager keeps under `sjm.maintenance.scheduled.job`); when the plugin stops it marks itself stopped and removes that job. The job is due when the component is not stopped, scheduled maintenance is enabled, and the next scheduled run time (see the next-run claims) is at or before now. Licence state never blocks it (the replacement has no licence checks).

When the scheduled job runs, the module first computes and stores the following next run time (so the same slot is not run twice), then runs maintenance with the scheduled parameters, reporting progress through a new process handle (process-handle-manager) created for the job's current user (normally none).

A manual 'run now' request: throws `StructureStoppedException` when the component is stopped; otherwise creates a new process handle for the calling user, submits the maintenance run as a system background job through job-manager, stores `maintenance.manual.lastRunTime` = now (epoch ms) and returns the process handle id when the job manager accepted the job (job id > 0), or 0 when it did not. The run uses the stored manual parameters. It does not wait for the run.

A maintenance run executes as superuser (no permission checks) and first tries, without waiting, to take the Jira cluster lock `com.almworks.jira.structure.maintenance`. If the lock is held (another run on any node), it logs a warning and returns false without running any task and without touching the process handle or the success flag. Otherwise it sets the process to RUNNING, stores `maintenance.scheduled.currentProcessId` = the process handle id, runs the tasks, and finally (whatever happened) removes `maintenance.scheduled.currentProcessId`, sets the process to FINISHED, releases the lock and stores `maintenance.successful` = whether all tasks succeeded.

A run reads its parameters (the JSON object in `maintenance.manual.parameters` for a manual run, `maintenance.scheduled.parameters` for a scheduled run; absent or unparsable JSON means all defaults) and runs these tasks in this order, each only when its key is enabled (a value of exactly `true` or `false`; anything else means the default): `backup` (default on), `removeOldBackups` (on), `cleanupFavorites` (on), `cleanupForests` (on), `cleanupViews` (on), `cleanupSynchronizers` (on), `cleanupStructureProperties` (on), `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords` (on), `reindexHistory` (on), `cleanupPerspectives` (on), `reindexStructures` (on), `removeOldChangeHistory` (on), `removeOldEffectorProcesses` (on), `removeOldProcessStates` (on), `cleanupItemTracker` (off).

Numeric task options are read from the same parameter map; a value that is not an integer or is out of range falls back to the default: `removeOldBackups-minFilesToKeep` (default 5, minimum 1), `removeOldBackups-minDaysToKeep` (15, min 1), `cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep` (30, min 1), `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords-daysToKeep` (30, min 0), `removeOldChangeHistory-daysToKeep` (30, min 0), `removeOldChangeHistory-changesPerStructureToKeep` (1000, min 0), `removeOldEffectorProcesses-daysToKeep` (30, min 0), `removeOldEffectorProcesses-waitingPreviewHoursToKeep` (24, min 0). `backup-saveHistory` is a boolean option, default true.

Tasks run one after another; a task that returns failure or throws (any exception or linkage error) marks the run unsuccessful (logged with the parameters) but the remaining tasks still run. Before each task the run stops early (returning failure) if the component has been stopped or the thread was interrupted; an `InterruptedException` from a task also ends the run. When the run ends early because the component was stopped, `maintenance.successful` keeps whatever outcome the tasks so far had (true if none failed) (as the original does).

Saving the scheduled-maintenance form: `scheduled` must be exactly `true` or `false` (absent counts as `false`); any other value makes the save fail (returns false, nothing stored). `false` stores `maintenance.scheduled.enabled` = false and succeeds immediately without touching any other key. Throws `StructureStoppedException` when the component is stopped.

When the form enables scheduling, `crontabEnabled` (exactly `true` means on, anything else off) is stored as `maintenance.scheduled.crontab.enabled` first. In cron mode `crontabSchedule` is required and must parse as a 5-field cron expression (see next-run-cron) and must not contain `?` or `*` directly preceded by a non-space character or directly followed by a character other than `,`, `/` or whitespace (so `*/5 * * * *` is accepted, `5* * * * *` or `*5 * * * *` is not); a missing or illegal schedule throws an invalid-parameter error naming the field `crontab` (the cron-enabled flag stays stored). A valid schedule is stored in `maintenance.scheduled.crontab.schedule`.

When the form enables scheduling without cron, `scheduledHour` must be an integer 0..23 and `scheduledMinute` 0..59; otherwise the save fails (returns false) with only the cron flag stored. Valid values are stored as `maintenance.scheduled.time` = `<hour>:<minute>` without zero padding (e.g. `7:5`).

Task options in a submitted form (scheduled or run-once) are validated and normalised: each task boolean key must be `true`, `false` or absent (absent is stored as `false`, i.e. an unchecked checkbox); a numeric option is checked only when its task key is present in the form and must then parse as an integer above 0 (`removeOldBackups-*`, `cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep`) or at least 0 (the other day/count options); `backup-saveHistory` is checked only when `backup` is present. Any violation makes the whole save fail (returns false, nothing stored). On success the normalised values are merged into the stored JSON object (keys not in the submission keep their stored values). For the scheduled form the next run time is then recomputed and stored, the parameters saved, and `maintenance.scheduled.enabled` set to true; the save returns true. Run-once parameters go to `maintenance.manual.parameters`.

Reading the form parameters for the manual or scheduled form returns the stored JSON object as a string map completed with defaults: every task key and option listed for the tasks is present, a stored value is kept only if it is `true`/`false` (booleans) or a valid number in range (options), otherwise the default is filled in (`cleanupItemTracker` false, other tasks true, numbers as listed with the task options). Throws `StructureStoppedException` when stopped.

Status read-outs (each throws `StructureStoppedException` when stopped): the currently running maintenance process id is `maintenance.scheduled.currentProcessId` (0 when absent, i.e. no run in progress on any node); the last manual run time is `maintenance.manual.lastRunTime` (0 when never); the last scheduled run time is scheduled-job-manager's last run time for job `maintenance.scheduled.job`; whether the last run was successful is `maintenance.successful` (absent means true).

Task `backup`: writes a zipped backup into Jira's export directory (`<jira-home>/export`) named and suffixed exactly as SPEC.md §1.6 describes for the scheduled maintenance backup (`structure-yyyyMMdd-HHmm.zip` in server local time, US locale, then `-1` … `-9`), including structure history unless `backup-saveHistory` is `false`, through backup-manager with every other backup option at its default. If the export directory is unavailable, or all ten names exist, it fails without writing.

Task `removeOldBackups`: in Jira's export directory considers only regular files whose whole name matches `^structure-\d{8}-\d{4}(-\d)?\.zip$`. If there are no more than `minFilesToKeep` of them nothing is deleted. Otherwise the candidates are those whose date-time parsed from the name (local time) is earlier than now minus `minDaysToKeep` days; if there are more candidates than (count − minFilesToKeep), only that many are deleted, choosing the smallest names without extension first (case-insensitive). Each deletion is retried up to 5 times with 1 s pauses; any file that cannot be deleted makes the task fail. A missing export directory fails the task. (Non-positive stored options never reach the task: they fall back to the defaults 5 and 15.)

Tasks delegated to other modules, with the behaviour claimed there: `cleanupFavorites` uses favorite-manager's removal of rows for missing users or structures; `cleanupStructureProperties` uses structure-property-service's removal of rows of deleted structures; `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords` uses sync-audit-log's purge with the cut-off now minus `daysToKeep` days (negative values treated as 0); `cleanupPerspectives` deletes perspectives (perspective-manager / perspective-io) whose last-used time is before now minus `daysToKeep` days (a stored value below 1 falls back to 30); `cleanupItemTracker` clears item-tracker's Data Center event journal and does nothing on a single-node server; `reindexStructures` rebuilds structure-manager's issue-to-structure index (`AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX`).
Task `reindexHistory` does nothing and always succeeds (it is kept only so the option key remains valid).

Task `cleanupSynchronizers`: as superuser, for every installed synchronizer definition whose structure is not accessible (i.e. no longer exists), uninstalls that synchronizer through sync-manager; always succeeds.

Task `cleanupViews`: as superuser, collects the ids of all existing views (view-manager), then removes from the global default view settings and from each structure's own (defined) view settings, archived structures included, every associated view that refers to a view id that no longer exists, keeping the other entries in their order; settings with no dangling reference are not rewritten. Always succeeds unless an exception escapes.

Task `cleanupForests`: as superuser, scans the stored forest of every structure (archived included) and finds rows whose row id is unknown to the row manager ('missing') or whose item an item type reports as no longer existing ('dead'; only item types that can tell, e.g. deleted issues). A dead or missing row with no children, or whose children are all dead/missing, is removed with its subtree. A dead row that has at least one live child subtree is kept, only its fully dead child subtrees being removed; a missing row (or loop marker) with a live descendant is replaced by a new folder titled with the i18n text `s.ext.it.folder.missing` at the same position, the children moved under it, and the original row removed. A failure on one structure marks the task failed and continues with the next; when nothing is found it succeeds without changes.

Task `removeOldChangeHistory`, per structure (archived included), with D = daysToKeep, K = changesPerStructureToKeep and cut-off = now − D days: if D = 0 and K = 0, the whole history is cleared. Otherwise it counts entries at or after the cut-off (0 when D = 0): if that count is 0 and K = 0 the history is cleared; if the count is ≥ K, entries older than the earliest entry at or after the cut-off are deleted; otherwise, if the structure has more than K entries, all but the latest K entries are deleted. So an entry is kept when it is newer than D days or among the latest K. Afterwards history-service and forest-service caches are cleared. Always succeeds.

Task `removeOldEffectorProcesses` asks effector-process storage to delete finished effector processes older than now − daysToKeep days and processes still calculating or waiting for preview confirmation older than now − waitingPreviewHoursToKeep hours. Task `removeOldProcessStates` deletes `AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE` rows older than a fixed 30 days through process-handle-manager, except those referenced by effector processes. Both always succeed.

Saving a new perspective requires a logged-in current user (`StructureAuth`) who may use Structure (the helper's 'use' permission); otherwise it throws `StructureException` with `StructureErrors.PERSPECTIVE_CREATION_DENIED` (REST: 403 on `POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/share`). Licence state never blocks it. Checked before the spec.

A perspective spec that is null or empty is refused with `StructureException` `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER`; any non-empty text is accepted unparsed (it need not be valid JSON at save time). A valid spec is stored through perspective-io as a new `AO_8BAD1B_PERSPECTIVE` row with `C_LAST_USED` = now (epoch ms) and a new random id (see perspective-io), and the stored perspective (id and spec text verbatim) is returned.
'May this user create perspectives?' answers true exactly when the user is not null (anonymous never) and may use Structure; it is what the REST bootstrap reports as `canCreatePerspective`.

Loading a perspective by id goes through perspective-io, which refreshes its `C_LAST_USED` to now; an unknown id gives an empty result. The returned spec has saved-column references refreshed: the spec is read as a JSON object, and for each of the top-level objects `primary` and `secondary` that has a `viewSpec`, that view specification is passed through saved-column-manager's adjustment (unmodified references re-expanded from `AO_8BAD1B_SAVED_COLUMN`, references to deleted saved columns removed) and the object is re-serialised keeping every other key and value. The stored row is not rewritten.

If the stored spec cannot be parsed as such an object (not JSON, or a `viewSpec` that is not a valid view specification), the perspective is returned exactly as stored and a warning is logged (rate-limited); loading does not fail.

Iterating over all perspectives (used by backup) visits every stored perspective with the same saved-column adjustment as a single load, without changing `C_LAST_USED`, and stops when the visitor returns false; restoring a list of perspectives hands them to perspective-io with now as their last-used time. Neither of these two checks whether the component is stopped.
Deleting unused perspectives removes, through perspective-io, every perspective whose `C_LAST_USED` is before the given epoch-ms cut-off (used by maintenance task `cleanupPerspectives`).
After the plugin stops, saving, loading, deleting unused perspectives and the 'may create' check throw `StructureStoppedException`.
When the plugin starts the module registers a usage-statistics source with statistics-manager that reports `perspectiveCount` = the current number of rows in `AO_8BAD1B_PERSPECTIVE` (as a double).

E-mailing a perspective whose id is unknown throws `StructureException` with the plugin's 'entity does not exist or is inaccessible' error (code 6017, category NOT_FOUND; REST 404 with a `structure-error`) and sends nothing. Loading the perspective refreshes its last-used time.

The structure of a perspective is read from the stored spec at JSON path `primary.forestSpec.structureId` (as a number). A spec that is not parsable JSON throws `StructureException` `StructureErrors.GENERIC_ERROR` ('Failed to get structure from perspective: …'). When that path is absent the mail is sent without any structure check, with page title `Structure`. When present, the structure is loaded with VIEW permission for the current user; if it does not exist or is not viewable the `StructureException` from structure-manager propagates and nothing is sent.

When the perspective shows a structure and the current user both administers that structure and has Jira's global 'browse users' (USER_PICKER) permission, then before mailing each recipient whose structure permission level does not include VIEW gets a new rule 'set level VIEW for user <recipient>' (`PermissionRule.SetLevel` on `PermissionSubject.JiraUser`) unless an identical rule already exists; the new rules are inserted at the start of the structure's permission list in recipient order and the structure is saved (the save happens even when no rule was added). Without both conditions permissions are untouched.

One mail per recipient is sent through mail-sender with template `shared-perspective` and parameters: `actor` (the current user's display info), `perspectiveId`, `message` (the given text, or `Take a look at this page.` when null or empty), `pageTitle` (the structure's name, or `Structure` when the perspective has no structure) and, only with a structure, `highlightTitle` = true. Recipients are mailed in the given order.

The panel configuration (REST `GET`/`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`, shape `panel-configuration`) carries the current user's UI settings for the page's project as resolved by structure-configuration (user overrides over system values), and the auto-switch strategy for the requested `StructurePage` from those settings; when none is set it is `AutoSwitchStrategy.PLUGIN_DEFAULT_AUTOSWITCH_STRATEGY` (`STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE`).

The default structure reported is the project's default (structure-configuration; the global default when there is no project). If that structure is archived: with a project, the global default is used instead when it differs and is not archived, otherwise there is no default; without a project there is no default. The default is then loaded with VIEW permission for the current user; if that fails (missing, not viewable, none configured) the configuration has no default structure and no default is used for the choice below.

The initial structure is the first of these that the current user can view (each candidate is loaded with VIEW permission; a failure moves on to the next): (1) the only structure viewable by the user, when exactly one exists (the configuration is then also flagged single-structure); (2) the explicitly preferred structure id; (3) when 'keep structure while navigating' is on or unset, the structure from the navigation hint; (4) the strategy's choice. If none succeeds there is no initial structure.

A navigation hint (cookie `structure3.navigation.hint`) yields a structure only when there is a current issue, the hint is non-empty and split on `|` has at least 3 parts, the third part equals the issue key exactly, and the first part parses as a positive structure id; otherwise it is ignored.

The strategy's choice uses the user's most recent accessible structure (recents-manager) as 'current': `DEFAULT_STRUCTURE` picks the default structure, else the current one; `AUTOSWITCH_OFF` picks the current one, else the default; `STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE` without an issue behaves as `AUTOSWITCH_OFF`.

`STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE` with an issue picks, in order: the current structure if its stored forest contains the issue; the default structure if it contains the issue; among the viewable structures containing the issue, the only one if there is exactly one (even archived), otherwise the first of the user's recent structures, skipping the most recent one, that is an unarchived member of that set, otherwise the first unarchived one of the set, otherwise the default structure. When no viewable structure contains the issue, the current structure is picked if it is not archived and the user can view it, else the default.

Matching for every search of this module: the query is trimmed; an empty (or null) query matches every candidate; otherwise a candidate matches when its search text contains the query as a literal substring, ignoring case (Unicode-aware). This is the behaviour behind `GET /rest/structure/2.0/group-picker` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/{share-with,projects,agile-boards,versions}`.
Matches are ordered by the length of their search text, shortest first; candidates of equal length (and all candidates for an empty query) keep the source order.

The result limit is the instance limit (dark feature `structure.create.namesSearch.resultLimit`, default 20; a non-positive setting means 20), lowered to the requested `maxResults` only when that is positive and below the limit. When more items match than the limit, only the first `limit` are returned and the group's `footer` is the localized text with the shown and total counts (keys `s.manage.edit.select.groups.footer`, `...roles.footer`, `...projects.footer`, `...boards.footer`, `...versions.footer`, e.g. 'Showing 20 of 35 matching groups'); otherwise there is no footer. When nothing matches there is no group at all.

Each returned item (`picker-search-result` groups) has `value` and `id` = the candidate's value, `label`, `title`, `html` = the search text HTML-escaped with the matched part wrapped in `` and `` (no wrapping for an empty query), and `params` only when the candidate has extra parameters.

Group search: candidates are the groups the current user may see (helper's available groups: all groups for Jira admins or when the instance exposes all groups, otherwise the user's own groups); value, label and search text = group name, no title; the group is labelled with the localized `s.manage.edit.select.groups.label` ('Groups').

Project-role search: candidates are the helper's available project roles; value = role id (decimal), label and search text = role name, title = role description; group label localized `s.tpl.step.general.share.roles.title` ('Project Roles').

Project search: candidates are the projects enabled for Structure that the current user can browse (helper); value = project id, label and search text = project name, title = project description; no group label.

Agile board search: candidates are the agile boards (rapid views) visible to the current user from gh-integration (none when Jira Software is absent); value = board id, label, title and search text = board name; no group label.

Version search for given project ids: candidates are the unarchived versions of each project (Jira `VersionManager`, no browse-permission check), value = version id, label and title = version name, params `versionFullName` = `<version name> (<project name>)` and `projectId`; with more than one project the search text (used for matching, ordering and the html) is the full name, otherwise the version name. Candidates are first sorted by search text (plain string order) before the length ordering is applied.

The administrator-defined help content is stored in `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY` key `welcomeScreen.help` as compact JSON with keys `title`, `content` (wiki markup) and `contactKeys` (array of user keys); null values are omitted. Saving writes the JSON (overwriting); clearing removes the row.

Reading the help content returns nothing when the property is absent; otherwise the JSON is parsed (unknown keys ignored); unparsable JSON also yields nothing (a warning is logged). Missing keys read as null.

The contacts of the help content are built from `contactKeys` in order, one per key, each with the display data of rest-user-builder (key, name, display name, avatar URL, profile URL); the user's own view is used as the 'looker' for the avatar and the inactive suffix, and the default locale when the key no longer resolves (then name and display name are the localized 'Anonymous User', the avatar is the anonymous avatar and there is no profile URL). No `contactKeys` gives no contacts.
The help content's HTML is the wiki `content` rendered by the given Jira renderer, or, when no renderer is available, the content HTML-escaped.

When the plugin starts the module registers a usage-statistics source reporting `helpTipsDefined` = 1.0 while `welcomeScreen.help` is set and nothing otherwise. The grid bootstrap (`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`) reports `hideHelpAdminTips` = true when help is enabled (dark feature `structure.welcome.enabled`, default true) and no help content is stored.

Building the display data (`user-display-info`) for a user key that resolves to a Jira user: `userKey` = the key, `name` = username, `displayName` = the display name, or for an inactive user the localized `s.ext.it.user.summary.inactive` text with the display name (English '<name> (Inactive)') in the looker's locale, `profileUrl` = `<base url>/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<URL-encoded username, UTF-8>`, `avatarUrl` = Jira `AvatarService.getAvatarURL(looker, user)` as text. The looker defaults to the current user.

For a non-null user key that resolves to no user: `userKey` = the key, `name` and `displayName` = the localized 'Anonymous User' (`s.generic.anonymous.fullname`), `avatarUrl` = `<base url>/secure/useravatar?avatarId=<Jira's anonymous avatar id>` (null when Jira's avatar manager is unavailable), no `profileUrl`.
For a null user key the result is the anonymous user: `userKey` = empty string, `name` = `displayName` = localized 'Anonymous User', `avatarUrl` = the anonymous avatar URL, no `profileUrl`.

Building from a permission subject returns the display data of the user for a `PermissionSubject.JiraUser` (by its user key, as seen by the given user) and null for any other subject (groups, roles, anyone).

The gadget variant takes a user (possibly null) and never consults Jira's user or avatar services: for a user it fills `userKey`, `name` and `displayName` from the user (null values become empty strings); for null all three are empty strings; `avatarUrl` and `profileUrl` are always empty strings.

Creating a migration configuration inserts one `AO_8BAD1B_MIGRATION_CONFIG` row and returns its new auto-increment `ID`: `C_NAME` = name, `C_STATUS` = the status name (`DRAFT`, `READY`, `RUNNING`, `DONE` or `FAILED`), `C_STRUCTURE_IDS` = the structure ids as a JSON array of numbers in the given order (`[]` for none), `C_EXTENSION_KEYS` = the extension keys as a JSON array of strings, or NULL when the set is empty, `C_RUN_AT` = run time (epoch ms or NULL), `C_EDITED_AT` = edit time (epoch ms), `C_EDITED_BY` = editor's user key. The id given in the input is ignored. Name uniqueness is enforced only by the column's unique constraint (a duplicate name fails with the database error).
Updating configuration `id` overwrites all seven columns of that row with the given values (same encodings as create) and saves it; an id with no row is silently ignored.
Deleting configuration `id` removes that row; a missing id is not an error.

Getting by id returns the configuration of that row or nothing when absent. Finding by name returns the first row whose `C_NAME` equals the name exactly (database comparison), or nothing. A read configuration has: id, name, status parsed from `C_STATUS` by exact constant name (an unknown text fails with `IllegalArgumentException`), structure ids decoded from `C_STRUCTURE_IDS` (a JSON array of numbers, null elements read as 0, or a single bare number), extension keys decoded from `C_EXTENSION_KEYS` (NULL, empty or unparsable reads as an empty set), run time (possibly null), edit time and editor.

A row whose `C_STRUCTURE_IDS` is the empty string (which the module never writes) cannot be read: Jackson finds no content and the read fails with its `IOException` subtype instead of returning an empty selection (as the original does).
Listing returns every configuration, sorted by name with a `java.text.Collator` for the current user's Jira locale (default strength, so case and accent differences order but do not merge).
Statuses `READY`, `DONE` and `FAILED` are runnable (a migration may use the configuration); `DRAFT` and `RUNNING` are not. cloud-data-migrator applies this rule.
Every operation (create, update, delete, get, find, list) throws `StructureStoppedException` while the plugin is stopped.

The exporter reads every dashboard from Jira's `PortalPageManager.getAll()` and, for each one with an id and an owner (dashboards without an owner, such as the system dashboard, are skipped), every gadget configuration from `PortletConfigurationManager.getByPortalPage(id)`. A dashboard whose reading throws is skipped (logged with its id) and the export continues; the totals are logged at INFO.

A gadget is exported only when its module key is `com.almworks.jira.structure:structure-gadget`. The key is the gadget's complete module key when Jira knows it; otherwise it is taken from the raw path of its OpenSocial spec URI: the URL-decoded text between `rest/gadgets/1.0/g/` and the next `/` (no such marker or empty text: not a Structure gadget).

A Structure gadget is exported only when its user preference `isConfigured` is exactly `true` and its `structureId` preference is in scope: the export of all gadgets accepts any value (even a missing one), while the export restricted to a set of structure ids requires `structureId` to parse as a long contained in the set.
