Migrate from backup: after resolution the item's `fields` parameter holds only the resolved fields; all other parameters stay, and a parameter with a null value is removed. If nothing is left, `fields` is removed. A `summary` or `description` key among the fields sets the item's name or description instead of staying in `fields`. Because `fields` is rebuilt from nothing, the usual estimate rule applies: an item with a non-blank `timeoriginalestimate` and a blank `timeestimate` also gets `timeestimate` with the same value, and the other way round. Example: `{"fields": {"timeoriginalestimate": "7200"}}` comes out as `{"fields": {"timeoriginalestimate": "7200", "timeestimate": "7200"}}`.

Migrate from backup: every item that went through resolution without a validation failure, even with nothing to change, is saved through `GenericItemManager.updateItem` with the new structure id as owning structure, which adds one change record (old and new item, the current user, the current time) after the creation record, and marks the item as changed. Together with `migrateGenericItemHistory`, items that have records in the backup then lose those local records in favour of the backup's. An item that no longer exists when its turn comes is skipped silently.

Migrate from backup: a generic item that appears in two migrated structures is created once and queued for the first structure that named it. The second structure to be saved gets its own copy of the item, made from the item as it was then, and that copy is never resolved: it keeps the backup's field ids and values and reports nothing (as the original does).

Migrate from backup, with `migrateGenericItemHistory`: the old and new item of each `historyRecord` in the backup go through the same resolution (old only when `oldName` is not blank), with the same problems reported, each distinct text once. A validation failure drops that one record and reports `Found problems while restoring generic item history record for item <new id>; <exception text>`, once per distinct text, after the section ends. A record whose item was not resolved adds the general problem `A generic item for history mapping is not found`, and one with a blank `newName` adds `An updated item is not found in history record`; both are dropped. Records of a structure not read successfully are dropped with only a log line.

Migrate from backup: the old and new items stored in a migrated generic-item history record carry the backup's structure id as owning structure, not the new one, while the item itself carries the new id. Example: backup structure 5 migrated to 12: the item's owning structure is 12, its history snapshots say 5 (as the original does).

Migrate from backup: field problems never fail the migration: the result is still `Structure Migration Completed Successfully`, under the warnings text. A structure that has only field problems is listed among the invalid structures, with its name and new id, and its problems follow its other problems, HTML-encoded, in the order first found, with identical texts shown once. `ErrorsContainer.getStructureFieldResolutionProblems()` holds them per structure in that order, and `getInvalidStructures()` includes those structures.

Migrate from backup: forest items' field problems are recorded under the structure's new id, but the result page's list converts every key from backup id to new id once more. So when a new id equals the backup id of another migrated structure, the problems appear under that other structure. Example: backup 5 becomes 7 and backup 7 becomes 9: a problem of an item now in structure 7 is listed under 9 (as the original does).

Migrate from backup: problems from generic-item history are recorded under the backup structure id and those of forest items under the new id. When the two differ and a structure has both, the conversion for the result page gives both the same key, and one set replaces the other instead of being merged, so only one set is listed; which one depends on hash order and is not defined (as the original does).

The migrate options page does not try field resolution: reading the backup for the preview checks no field and gives no warning about fields that will not resolve. They show up only on the result page.

Restore (`RestoreOperation`, the restore page) uses the same field matching, value mapping, planning task check, validation and problem texts as migrate, and it runs at the same moment, at the end of the `structureFields` section, with the same result when there is no such section. Restoring a backup onto an instance whose custom field ids differ therefore moves values to the field of the same name, type and properties, as in migrate.

Restore differs from migrate in these ways. Items keep their backup id and get their owning structure when created, so nothing depends on structure ids changing. Only items with a non-empty `fields` map are resolved: an item without fields is not touched, gets no extra change record, and a planning task with no fields gets no `Project is required` problem. Items of all structures met in the file are resolved, even of a structure that failed to save, and an item that could not be restored is skipped silently. Problems are recorded under the backup structure id, which is also the id on the result page, with no second conversion, so the wrong-structure and lost-problems cases of migrate cannot happen.

A backup file that the current reader refuses and that the restore page then reads with the older format reader gets no field resolution: `structureFields` and generic-item history sections in it are ignored, with no problem reported.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` with a blank `forest` whose `under`, `after` or `before` is a transient row id, sent with a `version` whose signature differs from the source's current one, does not give the signature-mismatch reply. Working out the first row of the empty fragment throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, nothing catches it, and the request answers 500, `text/plain`, with the exception's message as body (`Index 0 out of bounds for length 0` on Java 11 and later), plus an error in the server log. There is no `forest-update-response`, so no `updateError`, no `forestUpdates` and no resynchronization of the client (as the original does). Example: `{"spec": {"structureId": 1}, "version": {"signature": 1, "version": 5}, "actions": [{"action": "add", "forest": "", "under": 7}]}` with current signature 2. The same happens for a `copy` with a blank `forest` and `originalRowIds: []`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: when an empty-fragment action ends the request with a 500, the action itself changes nothing, and its `cutFrom` removal (tried only as a dry run so far) has not happened, nor is the clipboard cleared. Actions earlier in the same request stay applied, with their effects, but the 500 reports nothing about them: no `successfulActions`, no `forestUpdates`, no `effects`. The usage counter `updateForest` has been raised for the action, and `updateForest.errors` has not.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` or `copy` with a blank `forest` on a structure's forest, when the signature check passes, is first checked as any other add: `under`, `after` or `before` missing from the forest gives 200 with `updateError.error`, `row` 0 and message `Row <id> is not in the forest.`, and a coordinate under the wrong parent gives `Row <id> is not under row <parent>.`; lack of edit permission is reported as usual. If all of that passes, it fails like the signature case: 500, `text/plain`, body `Index 0 out of bounds for length 0` on Java 11 and later, and nothing is changed, also with `dryRun` (as the original does). So on a structure an empty `add` never succeeds, even though the blank `forest` was accepted.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` with a blank `forest` and no coordinates on the caller's clipboard forest succeeds and counts in `successfulActions`. It empties the clipboard, as any add there first clears it, and adds nothing, so `oldRowIds` and `newRowIds` stay absent; with `dryRun` the clipboard keeps its rows. With a transient coordinate and a changed signature the signature case still applies: 500, not the mismatch reply.

The `servlet-filter` `end-of-life-decorator` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) is declared on `/secure/Dashboard.jspa`, `/secure/AdminSummary.jspa`, `/secure/admin/*`, `/secure/StructureAdmin*` and `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa`. Licensing being fixed as licensed, valid and not expiring, it never adds the `end-of-life` web resource to any page, for any user, including Jira administrators and for bundled extension apps.

For every request on its URL patterns the filter calls the filter chain exactly once with the same request and response objects, and changes no header, cookie or session attribute. A request or response that is not HTTP is passed on the same way.

The `servlet-filter` `stats-offer-decorator` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) acts on `/secure/AdminSummary.jspa`, `/secure/admin/*` and `/secure/StructureAdmin*`, for any HTTP method. It does its work before calling the chain and does nothing after it; the request and response objects go down the chain unchanged.

Only a Jira system administrator is considered: it asks Jira's `GlobalPermissionManager.hasPermission(GlobalPermissionKey.SYSTEM_ADMIN, user)` for the current `StructureAuth` user (null when anonymous). A user with only `GlobalPermissionKey.ADMINISTER`, or anyone else the check refuses, gets no resource and `statistics-manager` is not consulted.

For a system administrator it asks `statistics-manager` whether to show the offer to that user (the rule is claimed for `statistics-manager`: not yet enabled, not dismissed, enough users). If yes it requires the web resource `com.almworks.jira.structure:stats-offer` on the page (through the page resource manager, as `StructurePluginHelper.requireResource` does); if no it adds nothing.

When the permission check, the offer check or adding the resource throws, the failure is swallowed and the chain still runs. Exception to this: `ThreadDeath` and any `VirtualMachineError` (such as `OutOfMemoryError`) are rethrown and do reach the caller. A failure whose root cause is `StructureStoppedException` is not logged at all. Any other failure is logged at error level, except that a failure with the same class name and message as the last one logged at error level, less than 3,600,000 ms (1 hour) ago, is logged at info level; each filter instance remembers its own last failure.
A request or response that is not an `HttpServletRequest`/`HttpServletResponse` is passed down the chain with no check made and no resource added.

The `servlet-filter` `plugin-manager-helper` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) is declared on `/plugins/servlet/upm` and `/plugins/servlet/upm*`. There being no vendor-provided licence to explain in the plugin manager, it never adds the `plugin-manager-helper-rc` web resource, for any user or any bundled extension app.

For every request on its URL patterns the filter calls the chain exactly once with the same request and response objects and changes no header, cookie or session attribute. A request or response that is not HTTP is passed on the same way.

The `servlet-filter` `issue-change-interceptor` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) is declared on `/secure/MoveIssueLink.jspa`, `/secure/VoteOrWatchIssue.jspa`, `/rest/api/2/issue/*/watchers`, `/rest/api/1.0/issues/*/watchers`, `/secure/SetRank.jspa`, `/secure/Rank.jspa`, `/secure/PageRank.jspa`, `/rest/greenhopper/1.0/epics/*` and `/rest/api/2/issue/*/subtask/move`. Those requests change issues without Jira's usual issue events, so around each one it works out the affected issues before the chain and reports them to `IssueEventBridge.reportChanges(ids, type)` (module `event-bridge`) after the chain. The response is never touched, and the request's content is not changed (see the claim on the epic body capture).

A request whose URI ends with `Rank.jspa` (`/secure/SetRank.jspa`, `/secure/Rank.jspa`, `/secure/PageRank.jspa`), with any HTTP method, reports `JiraChangeType.GH_RANK_UPDATED` for the issues given by its `id` and `issueKeys` parameters.
A request whose URI ends with `MoveIssueLink.jspa`, with any HTTP method, reports `JiraChangeType.SUBTASKS_REORDERED` for the issues given by its `id` and `issueKeys` parameters.

A request whose URI ends with `VoteOrWatchIssue.jspa` or with `watchers`, with any HTTP method (a read-only GET of a watcher list included), reports `JiraChangeType.ISSUE_UPDATED` for the issues given by its `id` and `issueKeys` parameters, plus the numeric id taken from a URI containing `/issues/<digits>/watchers` when that id is greater than 0 and fits a long.

For `/rest/api/2/issue/<id>/watchers` the id in the URI is not picked up, because only the plural form `/issues/<digits>/watchers` is recognised (as the original does): such a request reports an issue only when it also carries an `id` or `issueKeys` parameter. A key instead of digits in the URL (`/rest/api/1.0/issues/ABC-1/watchers`) is not picked up either.

The `id` parameter counts when it parses with `Long.parseLong` (no trimming) and is greater than 0. Missing, unparseable, zero or negative values are ignored. The value is reported as given: the filter does not check that such an issue exists or that the user may see it.

The `issueKeys` parameter is a comma-separated list. Each part is trimmed, empty parts are skipped, and each key is resolved with Jira's `IssueManager.getIssueObject(key)`, without a permission check. A key with no issue (or an issue with a null id) is skipped. A key lookup that throws an `Exception` is logged as a warning and only that key is skipped.

A `PUT` (exact, upper case) whose URI contains `/rest/greenhopper/1.0/epics/` and ends with `/add` or `/remove` reports `JiraChangeType.ISSUE_UPDATED` for the issues named in the JSON body's `issueKeys` array, resolved after the chain ran, as for the `issueKeys` parameter. The `id` and `issueKeys` request parameters are not read for it. Any other method or ending under `epics/` reports no issue.

For an epic add or remove the chain receives a request wrapper instead of the original request. Its content is the same: everything the downstream code reads through `getInputStream()` or `getReader()` (single reads, array reads, `readLine`) comes back unchanged and is only copied aside; `available`, `close`, `mark`, `reset`, `skip`, `markSupported`, `ready`, `isFinished`, `isReady` and `setReadListener` act on the real stream or reader, and every other request method behaves as on the original request. Repeated calls to `getInputStream()` return the same stream object, likewise `getReader()`. This is the only request or response object the filter ever replaces.

The copy of an epic request's body holds at most its first 102,400 bytes (when read as bytes) or 102,400 characters (when read as characters); the downstream reader still gets all of it. Only what the downstream code really read is copied, so a body it never read gives no issues. A body cut off by the limit normally fails to parse and gives no issues. The copy is decoded with the request's character encoding, or the JVM default charset when the encoding is missing, illegal or unsupported.

The epic body is read as a JSON object. Without an `issueKeys` array, or with a body that is not valid JSON, no issue is found and that is logged at debug level only; the request is not affected. A failure reading the copy is logged as a warning.

A `POST` (exact, upper case) whose URI contains `/rest/api/2/issue/<digits>/subtask/move` reports `JiraChangeType.SUBTASKS_REORDERED` for the numeric id in the URI, which is the parent issue. Parameters are not read. With an issue key instead of digits, or any other method, no issue is reported. Digits too long for a long count as a preparation failure: nothing is reported and the request goes on.

The report is made once per request, after the chain returned, whether the chain succeeded or threw, and whatever the response status: an exception from the chain still propagates to the caller after the report. The issue ids are passed sorted ascending with duplicates removed, so an issue named by both `id` and `issueKeys` is reported once. A request that yields no ids reaches no `IssueListener` (see `event-bridge`), with type `JiraChangeType.UNKNOWN_CHANGE` when no rule applied.

A failure while working out the issues is swallowed, nothing is then reported for that request, and the chain still runs. A failure while reporting after the chain is swallowed too. Both are handled as claimed for `stats-offer-decorator` (`ThreadDeath` and `VirtualMachineError` are rethrown; `StructureStoppedException` as root cause is silent; other failures are logged with the hourly repeat rule).

For rank, link-move, vote-or-watch and watcher requests the `id` and `issueKeys` parameters are read with `getParameter` before the chain runs, so a form-encoded body is parsed by the container at that point. No other request kind has its parameters read by the filter.
A request or response that is not HTTP is passed down the chain and nothing is reported.

The `servlet-filter` `bulk-change-interceptor` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) acts on `/secure/Bulk*`. It acts only when the HTTP session already exists (it never creates one) and its attribute `jira.bulkeditbean` holds the Structure bulk-edit selection created by `ww-structure`: a `BulkEditBean` subclass carrying a home URL and a `SearchRequest`. Otherwise (no session, no attribute, or Jira's own plain `BulkEditBean`) the request and response pass through unchanged and the session is left alone.

During the chain the session attribute `jira.issue.navigator.search.request` holds the selection's `SearchRequest`. After the chain the previous value of that attribute is put back, also when the chain threw; a previous value of null puts null back, which removes the attribute.
When the selection has no `SearchRequest`, a new empty `SearchRequest` is created, stored on the selection (so later requests reuse it) and used as the session search for this request.

When the selection's home URL is non-null and non-empty, the chain receives a response wrapper: a `sendRedirect` whose location contains `/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa` goes to the home URL as given, and any other location is unchanged. Everything else on the response behaves as on the original. With a null or empty home URL the original response goes down the chain and redirects to the navigator stay as they are.

After the chain, also when it threw, if `jira.bulkeditbean` now holds a different `BulkEditBean` (Jira created its own), that bean's `getSelectedIssues()` are copied into the Structure selection (both `initSelectedIssues` and `setIssuesInUse`) and the Structure selection is put back under `jira.bulkeditbean`. If the attribute is unchanged, or was removed or now holds something that is not a `BulkEditBean`, nothing is copied and the attribute stays as it is.

The search attribute is restored after the selection is handled, in the same protected step: if copying the issues back fails, the failure is swallowed and the session keeps the selection's search instead of the previous one (as the original does).

A failure before the chain is swallowed and the chain still runs, with the response wrapper if it had already been set up; the search is restored afterwards only if it had been swapped. A failure after the chain is swallowed too, and an exception from the chain itself propagates. Handling is as claimed for `stats-offer-decorator` (`ThreadDeath` and `VirtualMachineError` are rethrown).
A request or response that is not HTTP is passed down the chain and the session is not touched.

The `servlet-filter` `tempo-internal-issues-interceptor` (location `before-decoration`, weight 200) is declared on `/rest/tempo-core/*/issues/*`, but it acts only on an exact `PUT` whose URI contains `/rest/tempo-core/1/issues/` and ends with `issues/<key>`, where the key ends with a dash and digits. Other versions in the URL, other methods, sub-paths (`.../issues/ABC-1/worklogs`) and numeric ids are passed through with nothing reported. The request and response objects go down the chain unchanged.

For an accepted request the key is resolved before the chain with Jira's `IssueManager.getIssueObject(key)`, without a permission check. After the chain, whether it succeeded or threw and whatever the status, `IssueEventBridge.reportChanges` is called once with that one issue id and `JiraChangeType.ISSUE_UPDATED`. An exception from the chain still propagates after the report.
When the key has no issue, nothing is reported and the request goes on normally.
When the issue lookup throws, the failure is handled as claimed for `stats-offer-decorator`, nothing is reported and the chain still runs. `ThreadDeath` and `VirtualMachineError` are rethrown.

The report after the chain is not protected, unlike `issue-change-interceptor`: anything thrown by `IssueEventBridge.reportChanges` (in practice an `Error` from a listener, see `event-bridge`) leaves the filter and reaches the caller, replacing any exception from the chain (as the original does).

The filter does not check whether Tempo is installed. Without Tempo a matching `PUT` for an existing issue key is still reported as updated, whatever the answer to the request itself; the filter otherwise has no effect.

The `servlet-filter` `security-filter` (location `before-login`, weight 200, dispatchers `REQUEST`, `INCLUDE`, `FORWARD`, `ERROR`) acts on `/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa`, for anonymous and logged-in users alike, and is declared with Atlassian's unrestricted-access annotation so that it is never refused. It sets the page's `Content-Security-Policy` so that the page may be framed by `'self'` and by the applications linked to Jira. Other headers, `X-Frame-Options` included, are not touched by it.

Before the chain it takes the response's current `Content-Security-Policy` (possibly none) and sets the combined policy on the response, so the header is present even when nothing downstream sets one. With no current header the value is `frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`, or just `frame-ancestors 'self'` with no application links.

The chain receives a response wrapper. A `setHeader` whose name equals `Content-Security-Policy` ignoring case sets the combined policy of the given value instead of the value itself, under the exact name `Content-Security-Policy`. Other `setHeader` calls pass through unchanged. `addHeader` is not intercepted, for this header either, and goes straight to the real response.

When the policy has a directive that starts, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, with `frame-ancestors ` (with the space), the directive is rewritten in place and the directives are joined with `;`: its existing sources come first in their order, then `'self'` and the link origins, without duplicates, separated by one space. Example with one link: `default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors https://a.example` becomes `default-src 'self';frame-ancestors https://a.example 'self' https://b.example`. A trailing `;` is lost and other directives keep their own spacing. Applying the filter again (on a forward) changes nothing, because of the de-duplication.
A `frame-ancestors` directive whose only source is `'none'` (ignoring case) is replaced by `frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`.

A policy with no such directive gets one appended, with a `;` added first when the trimmed policy does not end with one: `default-src 'self'` becomes `default-src 'self';frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`. A null, empty or blank policy gives only the directive. A bare `frame-ancestors` with no following space does not count as a directive, so a second one is appended.

The origins are computed from `ReadOnlyApplicationLinkService.getApplicationLinks()`: for each link both `getDisplayUrl()` and `getRpcUrl()` count, reduced to `scheme://host` plus `:port` when a port is given, except that port 443 with `https` and port 80 with `http` are dropped. Path, query and user info are removed, and equal origins appear once. The directive always begins with `'self'`; the order of the origins after it is not defined.

The origins are kept in the Atlassian cache `com.almworks.jira.structure.app-links` (one entry, created by a cache loader on the first request after a clear) and reused for all requests. Any `ApplicationLinkEvent` on Jira's `EventPublisher` clears the cache, so a link change shows on the next request.
The filter registers its listener on `EventPublisher` when created; `destroy()` unregisters it and logs a warning that it is stopping.

When computing or setting the policy before the chain throws an `Exception` (for example when application links cannot be read), it is logged as an error and the chain is never called: the request ends with an empty response (as the original does).

An `Exception` thrown by the chain, `IOException` and `ServletException` included, or by a later policy update, is logged as an error (`Unexpected exception in servlet filter`) and does not propagate, so the container's error handling never sees it (as the original does). An `Error` does propagate.
A request or response that is not HTTP goes down the chain unchanged. An `Exception` from that chain is logged and swallowed too.

The `servlet-filter` `partitioned-cookie-header-filter` (location `after-encoding`, no weight, dispatcher `REQUEST`) is declared on `/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa` and `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate*`, with Atlassian's unrestricted-access annotation. It acts only on requests with scheme `https` and method `POST`, both compared ignoring case. Anything else, including any request the container reports as `http`, goes down the chain with the original objects.

For an acting request whose URI does not end with `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate` (the gadget page login post), the chain gets a response wrapper: when `sendRedirect` is called, the `Set-Cookie` headers are rewritten first and then the redirect goes on to the same location. A response that does not redirect (such as a failed login that shows the form again) keeps its cookies as they were.

For an acting request whose URI ends with `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate`, the filter acts only when the request parameter `s_partitioned` is exactly `true` (case-sensitive). Otherwise the original response goes down the chain.

With `s_partitioned=true` the chain gets a response wrapper: on every `setHeader` call, whatever the header, the `Set-Cookie` headers present at that moment are rewritten and then the header is set. `addHeader`, `addCookie` and `sendRedirect` trigger nothing, so cookies added after the last `setHeader` stay as they are. A `setHeader` of `Set-Cookie` itself stores its value unmodified.

Rewriting appends to each target cookie's header, in this order, `; Secure`, `; SameSite=None` and `; Partitioned`. Each attribute is skipped when its name (`Secure`, `SameSite`, `Partitioned`) already occurs anywhere in that header text, compared case-sensitively, so an existing `SameSite=Lax` stays Lax and a lower-case `secure` gets a second `Secure`. All else in the header is kept, and rewriting twice changes nothing.

The target cookies are `JSESSIONID`, `INGRESSCOOKIE` and the names in dark feature `structure.partitioned.cookies.additional`, a comma-separated list read at each rewrite; names are trimmed, empty ones skipped, and matched case-sensitively against the cookie name. Other cookies keep their header text unchanged.
A rewrite replaces all the `Set-Cookie` headers: the first usable one with `setHeader`, the others with `addHeader`, in the original order. Blank headers are skipped.

A `Set-Cookie` header that `java.net.HttpCookie.parse` rejects (a warning is logged) or that parses into other than one cookie is not written back, so it disappears from the response when any other usable `Set-Cookie` header exists (as the original does). When no usable header exists, nothing is rewritten and all headers stay.
The filter catches nothing: an exception from the chain, or from a rewrite, reaches the caller. It has no effect on the page's content and does not change the request.

`GET /plugins/servlet/structure/excel` and `POST` of the same path run the same export, reading the parameters of SPEC.md section 1.4 through `getParameterMap()` (the first value counts when a parameter is repeated), so a POST may carry them in a form body. Any path matching `/structure/excel*` under `/plugins/servlet` is served alike.

The servlet makes no access check of its own and needs no login: an anonymous caller gets what the forest and permission checks below allow. Access is decided by `forest-service` when it resolves the forest, by `view-manager` for a saved view, and by row visibility.

Before anything else it caches Jira's Velocity request context for this request, with SAL `ApplicationProperties.getBaseUrl(UrlMode.ABSOLUTE)` as base URL (see `velocity-request-context-factory-bridge`), so that links rendered in cells use that base URL. It does not clear it afterwards.

A missing, empty or unreadable `forestSpec`, or one that is the JSON `null`, answers `500` through `sendError` with the message `spec not available: <the parameter's value>` (`null` when missing). Nothing else happens: no view is read and no statistic is recorded.

A readable `forestSpec` rejected by `ForestSpec.fromRest` (for example neither or several of `structureId`, `sQuery` and clipboard, or `version` without `structureId`) answers `500` with that exception's message, not `400`.

A `StructureException` answers through `sendError(status, e.getLocalizedMessage())`: `503` when the error is `StructureErrors.AUTOMATION_FAILED`, otherwise by the error's category: `INVALID_INPUT` 400, `NO_PERMISSION` 403, `NOT_FOUND` 404, any other 500. It is logged as a warning with the structure id, taken from parameter `s` when it is a number and from the forest spec otherwise. `s` affects nothing else.
Any other `Exception` or a `LinkageError` answers `sendError(500, e.getLocalizedMessage())`, which may be a null message, and is logged as a warning. Other `Error`s propagate to the container.

The workbook is built completely before the response is touched, so a failure while building gives a clean error status. Then the response is `reset()`, the buffer size set to 8192, and besides the `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition` of SPEC.md section 1.4 it gets `Last-Modified` = now and `Expires` = now + 1 ms. The `<name>` is encoded like JavaScript's `encodeURIComponent`.
`xlsx` selects the `.xlsx` format when its value, trimmed and ignoring case, is `true`; any other value or none gives `.xls`.

In the file name, non-letter and non-digit characters at the start of the display name are dropped, not turned into `_`; letters and digits are those of `Character.isLetterOrDigit`, so non-Latin letters stay. The time is the moment the forest was read, formatted in the JVM's default time zone, not the user's. For example `  --Q3` at that same time gives `Q3_261028_1405.xlsx`.
After the workbook is built and before it is written, `statistics-manager` gets `addUniqueUserCountAsync("activeUser")`. A failed export records nothing.

The columns come from the saved view when `viewId` is a non-zero number, read from `view-manager` with `PermissionLevel.VIEW`. Otherwise from `viewSpec` when non-empty. A `viewId` that is not a number counts as absent.

When the saved view does not exist or cannot be viewed, the export does not fail and does not try `viewSpec`: it uses the default view, which has the `issuekey` field column followed by the main column. The same default is used when neither parameter gives a view, when `viewSpec` cannot be read, and when its content is invalid. So no view problem ever answers `403` or `404`.

The columns of the view are exported in view order, without those with key `handle` or `actions`. When the view's column display mode is `ColumnDisplayMode.SCROLLABLE`, the pinned columns (`ViewSpecification.getPins()`) come first in pin order and the others follow in view order.

For each column, providers from `extension-service` are tried in the order (column key, `ms-excel`), (column key, any format), (any key, `ms-excel`), (any key, any format), and within each pair in module order. The first that returns a renderer, or several through the export request context (see `exportrenderer-excel-joined`), wins. A `StructureProviderException` skips the column with a warning. A provider that throws anything else is ignored for the rest of the export. A column with no renderer is skipped with a warning, and a renderer whose `prepare` throws is left out; the other columns are exported.
A renderer that throws an `Exception` or `LinkageError` in `configureColumn` or `renderCell` is logged and not called again for that export; its remaining cells stay blank and the export succeeds.

While renderers run, the export context holds `ExportContextKeys.Export.VIEW_SPECIFICATION` and, from sheet creation on, the POI objects under `ExportContextKeys.Excel`: `POI_WORKBOOK`, `POI_HELPER`, `POI_SHEET`, and for the current cell `POI_ROWNUM` (0-based sheet row), `POI_ROW`, `POI_COLUMN` (0-based) and `POI_CELL`. The header is set up through `configureColumn` and data through `renderCell`, once per kept row and column.

The rows are those of the current forest of the `forestSpec` from `ForestService.getForestSource`, after removing generator rows, effector rows and rows that no longer exist, and applying `clientFilter`. Filtering is as `Forest.filter`: sub-rows of a removed row stay and move up. Collapsed rows are exported too, not skipped.

`clientFilter` starts with `+` (keep only the listed rows) or `-` (drop the listed rows). The rest is a `.`-separated list of decimal numbers, each added to the running total to give the next row id, so `+10.5.2` lists rows 10, 15 and 17. `+` alone keeps no row; `-` alone or an empty value filters nothing. A wrong first character, or any list element that does not parse (`+10.`), logs a warning and filters nothing.
At most 1,000,000 rows are exported to `.xlsx` and 65,530 to `.xls`, counted on the rows kept: the first rows in forest order. Further rows are dropped silently, with no warning in the workbook.

Rows that `ForestAccessCache.getInvisibleRows` reports as invisible to the current `StructureAuth` user stay in the sheet at their place, but every attribute read for them gives null, so renderers show nothing for them.

The workbook has one sheet. With nothing to warn about the header is on row 0 and data from row 1. Otherwise warnings come first, one row each, merged across all columns, light yellow background and italic: `s.export.forest-outdated` (`The exported structure may be outdated. We could not access the most recent version in time, because the structure was busy.`) and then `s.export.inconsistent` (`The exported information may be inconsistent due to concurrent changes in Jira or Structure during the export.`). One blank row follows, then the header and data.

The sheet is named from `ForestService.getDisplayName`, made safe with POI's `WorkbookUtil.createSafeSheetName` (at most 31 characters, forbidden characters replaced), with any `:` removed and trimmed. When that leaves nothing the name is the text of `s.common.structure` (`Structure`).

While the forest cannot be read because the structure's lock is not free, or attributes cannot be calculated for the same reason, the export retries, adding up the time waited over both steps. After more than 120 s (dark feature `structure.export.trySnapshotTimeout`, in seconds) it uses the last generated forest when one exists (version above 0) and marks the export outdated. After more than 600 s (dark feature `structure.export.forestLockTimeout`) it fails with `StructureErrors.AUTOMATION_FAILED` and message `s.export.error.forest-lock-timeout` (`Could not access the structure in {0} seconds, because it's constantly busy. Please try again later, or contact your Jira administrator or Tempo support.`) with the seconds as `{0}`, which answers `503`. Dark features are read once per export.

Attributes required by renderers are loaded for the exported rows, by `StructureAttributeService.getConsistentAttributeValues` when dark feature `structure.export.tryConsistentAttributes` is true (default). If that throws a `StructureException` they are loaded with `getAttributeValues` and the export is marked inconsistent. With no attributes required the step counts as consistent. Attributes calculated on the snapshot after a lock wait also mark it inconsistent. Once one step is inconsistent, the next does not try consistent loading.

A column with parameter `forestSpec` = `unfiltered` calculates its values on the forest spec with the trailing filter and sorter transformations removed (all of them when only such transformations exist); its renderer sees those values for the same exported rows. All other columns use the export's forest spec.

`expand` is a `.`-separated list of tokens. A number N >= 0 sets the default level to N; `++` means everything expanded; `--` means level 0; `+<id>` and `-<id>` mark a row expanded or collapsed; a zero or unparseable id, any other token and empty tokens are ignored. When the forest spec has a title row the minimum level is 1 instead of 0. Without level tokens everything is expanded. A row of depth d is expanded when the level is above d, unless it is marked collapsed, or else when it is marked expanded.

With a non-empty `expand` the rows below each parent form an Excel outline group, nested by depth, with the summary row above (`setRowSumsBelow(false)`). A group is collapsed when its parent is not expanded; everything inside a collapsed row counts as collapsed too. With an empty or missing `expand` there are no groups and all rows show. In `.xlsx` the rows of a collapsed group are hidden and the row just after the group carries the collapsed mark (created when missing); in `.xls` the group is collapsed with POI's `setRowGroupCollapsed`.
When the forest spec has a pinned item (see `filter-item`), data cells of every row showing that item get a thin top border and a bold font on top of the style they had.

After the data is written each column is auto-sized. A date column (one where `setDate` or `setDatetime` was used) with a non-zero width gets 512 width units more; the width is capped at 15,360 units. Each cell of the last row gets a thin bottom border added; with no data rows this applies to the header row.

The sheet freezes all rows above the first data row, makes the first cell of that row active (of row 0 when there are no data rows), and is the selected sheet. Printing: row 1 of the sheet repeats on each page, landscape, automatic page breaks on, no notes, centred horizontally, not vertically, with fit-to-page switched off (a fit width of 1 and fit height of 0 are stored but not in force), paper Letter when the user's locale country is US or CA and otherwise A4.
The row repeated on printed pages is always the sheet's first row, so with a warning present the warning repeats instead of the header (as the original does).

The print header shows the sheet name on the left and `page / pages` on the right; the footer shows the file name on the left and the creation time on the right, in short date and time format of the user's locale. The workbook's title is the sheet name; author and last modified by are the user's display name, or the text of `common.words.anonymous` for anonymous; created and modified are the current time.

When no column is left (for example a view holding only `handle` and `actions` columns), finishing the sheet hits a null cell, so the export answers `500`, normally with a null message (as the original does).

An image in a cell (see `ExcelCell.setRichTextFromHtml`) is loaded only when its URL starts with the Jira base URL: the rest of the URL is read with `ServletContext.getResourceAsStream`. A missing, empty or unreadable resource, or one that is not JPEG (starts FF D8, ends FF D9) or PNG (the PNG signature), gives no image. One workbook stores each URL's picture once. The picture is anchored to the cell, moves with it, does not resize, and is shrunk to fit the cell's final width and height.

The module is a `jql-function` with key `jql-structure`, child `fname` = `structure` and `list` = `true`. Jira gets 0 as the minimum number of arguments and `JiraDataTypes.ISSUE` as the data type; the function also implements Jira's `ClauseSanitisingJqlFunction`.

With no arguments, the function searches the global default structure (`StructureConfiguration.getDefaultStructureId(null)`, project defaults are not consulted) with a query matching every row. If the current user cannot VIEW that structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible(id, VIEW)`, which also covers the unset value 0), validation gives the error `s.jql.error.no-default-structure` ('Default structure is missing or you do not have permissions to view it.'). Paused automation is not checked for the default structure.

A structure argument is first trimmed and read as a long (anything unparseable counts as 0). A value > 0 is a structure ID: if the user cannot VIEW it the error is `s.jql.error.bad-structure-id` with the ID as text ('There''s no structure with ID {0} or you don''t have permissions to view it.'). A value <= 0 is treated as a name, not an ID.

A structure argument that is not a positive number is looked up with `StructureManager.getStructuresByName(arg, VIEW)` (null argument is treated as an empty string). Exactly one match is that structure. Two or more give the error `s.jql.error.too-many-structures` with the argument ('There is more than one structure with name "{0}", please use structure ID instead.') and the structure value 0. No match gives `s.jql.error.unknown-structure` with the argument ('There''s no structure "{0}" or you don''t have permissions to view it.').

When the name matches nothing the user may VIEW and security is not overridden, the name is looked up again with security overridden and no level. If that finds structures, the first one's ID is remembered as the function's structure value (the error stays). This lets a one-argument call tell an existing hidden structure from text that is not a structure, and it is the ID that sanitisation then writes in place of the name.

With one argument the function first reads it as a structure. If that gives an error, the same text is parsed and validated as an S-JQL query. If the query has no errors, the function searches the global default structure with that query, so `structure("child of TS-1")` runs on the default structure, and the structure's errors are dropped. If the default structure is then not accessible, the messages are the structure's errors followed by `s.jql.error.no-default-structure`.

With one argument that is neither a usable structure nor a valid S-JQL query: when the structure value is <= 0 (no such structure at all, or an ambiguous name) the default structure is taken and checked as well; when it is > 0 (a positive ID the user cannot view, or a name of a structure hidden from the user) that structure value is kept and the default structure is not looked at. In both cases the messages returned are, in this order, the structure error, then the S-JQL errors, then any default-structure error; each is an error of the `MessageSet`.

When a structure named by argument resolves and is accessible but `generation-manager` reports it blocked (`isBlocked(ForestSpec.unsecuredStructure(id))`), validation fails with `s.jql.error.automation-stopped` with the structure's name and the ID as text ('Automation is paused for structure "{0}" (#{1}).'). The name is '' when reading the structure with VIEW throws `StructureException`. With one argument this does not fall through to S-JQL parsing: the error is reported and the argument stays a structure. With two arguments the S-JQL argument is still parsed and its errors are added after it.

With two arguments the first is a structure as described for the one-argument form (no S-JQL fallback) and the second is an S-JQL query. Errors from both are collected, structure errors first. A null query argument is parsed as the text `[]`. A `StructureException` from parsing adds its localized message as an error and the default all-rows query is kept.

With three or more arguments validation gives the single error `s.jql.error.bad-number-of-arguments` ('Structure function accepts up to two arguments: an optional structure name and an optional Structure query.'), and the structure value is -1.

Unless `StructureAuth` security is overridden, a user for whom `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` is false gets just one error, `s.jql.error.structure-unavailable` ('Sorry, you do not have access to the Structure function.'), whatever the arguments are; the other errors are not returned. The arguments are still resolved, so sanitisation can use them.

Jira's `validate(user, operand, clause)` runs as the given user (`StructureAuth.sudo(user, false, ...)`) and returns the `MessageSet` from the argument rules. In this mode a saved filter referenced by inner JQL in the S-JQL query is checked for referring to the filter being saved (`s.jql.error.cycle`, see `structure-query-parser`). Validate never evaluates the query against the forest and records no statistics.

`getValues` with valid arguments runs the query on the latest forest of `ForestSpec.structure(id)` (secured for the current user) and returns one `QueryLiteral(operand, issueId)` per distinct issue, in the order the query yields rows. Non-issue rows are skipped and an issue on several rows appears once.

In `getValues` only, a query that consists of nothing but an issue list matches those issues and all their descendants in the structure, not just the issues (`issue in structure("S", "TS-1")` also returns everything under TS-1). Any other query keeps its usual meaning. `validate` is not affected.
`getValues` with arguments that fail the rules returns an empty list and does not throw; no forest is read.
If reading the forest throws `StructureException`, a warning is logged and `getValues` returns an empty list. The call still counts as valid in the statistics.

While `getValues` or `sanitiseOperand` is running for an operand, a nested call on the same thread with an equal `FunctionOperand` (a filter reaching itself through inner JQL) does not evaluate: `getValues` logs a warning and returns an empty list, `sanitiseOperand` returns the operand unchanged. The guard is per thread and per operand: a different operand, or another thread, evaluates normally, and the operand is released when the call ends, also on an exception. `validate` is not guarded.

`getValues` and `sanitiseOperand` run under the ambient `StructureAuth` user, not under the one they are given: the `QueryCreationContext` user and its security-override flag only wrap the creation of the argument holder, so checking, forest access and query evaluation use whoever `StructureAuth.getUser()` is on the thread, with security not overridden (as the original does). A test: with a context for user A and security override set while the thread's user is B, permissions are those of B.

`sanitiseOperand(searcher, operand)`: when the arguments have no errors it returns the same operand. When they have errors it returns a new `FunctionOperand` with the same name and these arguments: first the structure value as decimal text (-1, 0, the default structure ID or the resolved ID), then the query's sanitised text (`StructureQuery.getSanitizedQueryString`) when that is not null. So a structure name the user cannot see never remains in the JQL shown to them.
When dark feature `structure.jql.bypassSanitization` (read once at creation, default false) is on, `sanitiseOperand` returns the operand unchanged without looking at it.

When dark feature `structure.jql.optimize.check.projects` (read once at creation, default false) is on, `getValues` returns an empty list without evaluation or statistics when it is called from inside one of these Jira Software or issue-create methods: `com.atlassian.greenhopper.service.query.QueryToProjectMapper.getProjectContextIdsForQuery`, `com.atlassian.jira.plugins.issue.create.rest.ContextResolutionHelper.possibleValuesForClause` or `com.atlassian.greenhopper.web.sidebar.ProjectBoardsHelper.getProjectBoards`. The call stack is inspected from the frame of `com.atlassian.query.clause.TerminalClauseImpl` outwards (from the innermost frame when that class is absent), stopping at the first method named `doFilter`. With Jira Software absent no such frame exists and evaluation is normal.

Each `getValues` that reaches the argument check adds usage statistics through `statistics-manager` (asynchronous total counts unless noted). Valid: `jqlFun`, unique-user `jqlFun.users`, one of `jqlFun.args.0`, `jqlFun.args.1-sjql`, `jqlFun.args.1-structure`, `jqlFun.args.2`; for the two with S-JQL also unique-user `<name>.users`. For a query with text: `jqlFun.sjql.length` in the value distribution 40, 100, 200, 300, and `jqlFun.sjql.multiLine` adding 1 when the text has a line feed, else 0. One `jqlFun.rel.<x>` for each relation kind used, with x from `empty`, `issueList`, `jql`, `custom.<constraint name>`, `or`, `and` and, for compositions, the binary relations joined by `|`. Invalid: `jqlFun.error`, unique-user `jqlFun.error.users`, and `jqlFun.error.<problem key>` when the S-JQL parser reported one.

The module is an `activity-streams-provider` with key `structure-activity-provider`, i18n name key `s.streams.provider.name` ('Structure') and a `filter-provider` child. `getActivityFeed(request)` returns a cancellable task; nothing is read until the task is called.

The filter provider's `getFilterOptions()` returns exactly three options, in this order: `structure` (type SELECT, display name and i18n key `s.streams.option.structure.name`, 'Structure'), `ancestor` (type LIST, unique, display name and i18n key `s.streams.option.ancestor.name`, 'Ancestor Issue Key', no fixed values), `synchronizer` (type SELECT, display name and i18n key `s.streams.option.synchronizer.name`, 'Synchronizer').

The `structure` option's values are the current user's non-archived structures with at least VIEW (`getAllStructures(VIEW, false)`, in that order), empty when there are none. Each map key is `<index>:<structure id>`, the display value is the structure's name. The index starts at 0 and is left-padded with spaces to the number of decimal digits of the list size, so option order survives sorting by key: with 12 structures the keys are ` 0:<id>` ... `11:<id>`.

The `synchronizer` option's values start with `<index>:-2` showing `s.streams.option.synchronizer.none` ('None (changed by a user)') and `<index>:-1` showing `s.streams.option.synchronizer.any` ('Any synchronizer'). Then come the installed synchronizers of every non-archived structure the user can ADMIN, by structure order then the manager's order, keyed `<index>:<instance id>` and shown as `<structure name>: <config description>`. An instance without a resolved synchronizer is left out. Two instances with the same shown text collapse into one, the later instance ID winning. The index is padded as in the `structure` option, to the digit count of (instances + 2).

`getActivities()` returns four activity options, all with object type `item` (IRI `http://structure.almworks.com/syndication/types/item`), in the order: verb `add` ('Items added', `s.streams.activity.item.add.name`), `copy` ('Items copied'), `move` ('Items moved'), `remove` ('Items removed'). The verbs `add`, `copy` and `remove` have IRIs under `http://activitystrea.ms/schema/1.0/`; `move` is `http://structure.almworks.com/syndication/verbs/move` with parent verb `update`.

In a request, a `structure` or `synchronizer` filter value is parsed as the long after the first ':', or as the whole text when there is no ':' or the ':' is the last character. An empty, null or unparseable value gives no ID (an error is logged for an unparseable one) and is skipped; leading spaces before a ':' are harmless.

An inclusive filter that is present but resolves to nothing makes the feed empty, with no history query: issue keys (`Filters.getIssueKeys`), project keys (`Filters.getProjectKeys`), `structure`, `ancestor` or `synchronizer` values. An issue counts only when it exists and `StructurePluginHelper.getIssueError(issue, false)` is null; a project only when `isProjectStructuredForCurrentUser(project)`; a structure only when the user can VIEW it; a synchronizer only when it is -1, -2, or installed on a structure the user can VIEW.

Issue keys in the issue and `ancestor` filters are looked up as given, then, when not found and the key changes when upper-cased in the user's locale (`JiraAuthenticationContext.getLocale`), upper-cased.

The history query gets the resolved IDs as sorted unique lists: inclusive and exclusive issue, project, structure and synchronizer lists; inclusive and exclusive ancestors as issue identities (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`); authors from the standard `USER` filter's IS and NOT values as given; min and max date from `Filters.getMinDate` and `Filters.getMaxDate`; no start ID. Exclusive values that do not resolve are dropped silently.

IDs named in both the IS and NOT values of `structure`, or of `synchronizer`, are removed from the IS list. When that empties the IS list the query has no inclusion for it, and with `history-service` semantics an empty inclusion means all but the excluded ones, so `structure IS 5 and NOT 5` lists every other visible structure rather than nothing (as the original does).

When the filters name exactly one issue and exactly one project and the issue belongs to that project, the project filter is left out of the query. Without a project filter, titles carry no per-project count.

The operations queried are those of the four activities that Atlassian Streams' `Filters.inActivities(ActivityRequest)` predicate accepts. If none is accepted, or the predicate cannot be obtained (it is invoked by reflection; failures are logged once), the feed is empty without a history query.

The feed has title `s.streams.feed.title` ('Structure Activity Stream'), no subtitle, and one entry per history change. The feed is empty, with no history read, when the app is not available to the current user (`isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` false), when no query can be built, or when the task was cancelled before the query.
A task can be called once. A second call logs a warning and returns the empty feed.

The task calls `HistoryService.queryActivity(query, request.getMaxResults(), changesLimit, consumer)`. `changesLimit` is dark feature `structure.activitystream.changesLimit`, read at creation, default 10. So `maxResults` limits history entries, not stream entries, and one history entry gives several stream entries.

While history is read, a `Pinger` ping every 500 ms checks the timeout. `ActivityRequest.getTimeout()` of 100 ms or less means no timeout. When the elapsed time reaches the timeout the task cancels itself and stops pinging, delivery of further entries stops (the consumer answers false) and the feed is empty, with a warning logged. `cancel()` from outside has the same effect without the warning and returns `Result.CANCELLED`. Pinging is stopped when the query ends, also on an exception.

Each change of a history entry gives a `StreamsEntry` with: id and alternate link `<canonical base URL>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>&v=<version>` (all changes of an entry share it), posted date from the entry's timestamp in the JVM default zone, the author, the verb of the operation (ADD add, COPY copy, MOVE move, REMOVE remove), application type `com.almworks.jira.structure`, and one activity object: id and link `<canonical base URL>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, title the structure's name, type `http://structure.almworks.com/syndication/types/structure`. The base URL is `ApplicationProperties.getBaseUrl(UrlMode.CANONICAL)`.

A change is left out, with no error, when `StructureManager.getStructure(id, VIEW)` throws `StructureException` for its structure. The author's profile comes from `UserProfileAccessor.getUserProfile(user name of the entry's user key)` and is looked up once per user key per feed.

An entry's title is the i18n text `s.streams.activity.item..text` with arguments subject, objects and structure: '{0} added {1} to {2}', '{0} copied {1} in {2}', '{0} moved {1} in {2}', '{0} removed {1} from {2}'. The structure is `name` with the name HTML-encoded. The entry has no summary; its content is the body.

The subject for a change by a user is `full name ` or, without a profile URI, `full name `, the name HTML-encoded and a trailing space kept in both. For a synchronizer change (entry's synchronizer ID > 0) with an installed, resolved synchronizer it is `s.streams.activity.item.synchronizer.known` with the encoded config description and the user text ('Synchronizer "{0}" on behalf of {1}'). For an ID < 0, an instance that is not installed, or an unresolved synchronizer it is `s.streams.activity.item.synchronizer.unknown` ('Unknown synchronizer on behalf of {0}'). A null or 0 ID is a user change.

The objects text of a change whose forest has exactly one row is that row's text: `description` when the item has a URL (description HTML-encoded), else the encoded description, else the encoded text of the item identity when no displayable value was found. A row that no longer exists gives null. Displayable values are fetched once per feed through `StructureUtil.getItemDisplayable` for the single root of a change that has one root, and for all rows on the changes' from- and to-paths; other rows are not fetched.

For a forest of several rows: when the whole forest is one subtree the text is `s.streams.activity.item.title.item-and-n-sub-items` with the root's text and the row count minus 1 ('{0} and {1,number,integer} {1,choice,1#sub-item|1<sub-items}'); otherwise, also for an empty forest, `s.streams.activity.item.title.n-items` with the row count ('{0,number,integer} items').

When the request filters by issue, the objects text uses the `.including-issues` variant of the key (`...item-and-n-sub-items.including-issues` or `...n-items.including-issues`), naming the filtered issues found among the forest's rows: sorted by issue key, joined by ', ', each ``. An issue that is the root is left out, and when none remains the plain variant is used. With assertions enabled (as the tests run) a forest holding none of the filtered issues throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the plain variant is used.

When the request filters by project and not by issue, the objects text uses the `.including-projects` variant, listing per filtered project how many issues of the forest are in it, by project name (`ProjectNameComparator`), joined by ', ', each `s.streams.activity.item.title.including.from-project` ('{0,number,integer} from {1}') with ``. Membership is decided with a JQL `project = ` through `StructurePluginHelper` issue matching; a `SearchException` for one project is logged and that project is skipped. Projects with no such issue are left out. With assertions enabled (as the tests run) no matching project at all throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the plain variant is used.

The content of an entry is built from paths: ADD and COPY give the to-path; REMOVE gives the from-path; a MOVE between different parents gives the from-path, a space, then the to-path. Each part is `s.streams.activity.item.<verb>.body.parent-path.<from|to>` with the path's rows joined by ' / ', or the `.top` key for a null or empty path ('from the top level of the structure', 'to the top level of the structure'). Row text is as for a single row. Note that `add` uses `.to` ('under {0}').

A MOVE whose from-path and to-path are equal gives one part from `s.streams.activity.item.move.body.parent-path.`: `under.down` when the change's direction is > 0 ('downwards under {0}'), `under.up` when < 0 ('upwards under {0}'), `under` when 0 ('under {0}'), each with `.top` for an empty path ('downwards at the top level of the structure', 'upwards at the top level of the structure', 'at the top level of the structure').

On the last change of a history entry whose reported change count is greater than the number of changes it carries, the text of `s.streams.activity.changes-hidden` ('+{0} changes hidden'), with {0} = count minus the changes limit, is appended directly to the body, with no separator. For an entry that had fewer changes than the limit and lost some to permission filtering, this reports a negative number, e.g. '+-7 changes hidden' for 3 changes loaded, 2 visible, limit 10 (as the original does).

The module is a `workflow-condition` with key `structure-workflow-condition`, name 'Issue Matches Structure Query', i18n name key `s.wf.condition.name`, `state="disabled"`, description key `s.wf.condition.desc`, `condition-class` `com.almworks.jira.structure.workflow.StructureWorkflowChecker`, and velocity resources `view`, `input-parameters` and `edit-parameters`. Jira's workflow editor therefore does not offer it until an administrator enables the module.

`com.almworks.jira.structure.workflow.StructureWorkflowChecker` extends Jira's `AbstractJiraCondition`, so `passesCondition(transientVars, args, propertySet)` returns a boolean. It never throws for a bad configuration or an internal failure: every case that blocks the validator (see `structure-workflow-validator`, same order of checks) returns false here with no message, and a `RuntimeException` during the check is logged and gives false.

With no issue in the transient variables (`AbstractJiraCondition.getIssue` gives null) or an issue without an ID (not created yet), the condition and the validator pass without looking at any argument.

The whole check runs under `StructureAuth.sudo(caller, false, ...)`, where caller is `AbstractJiraCondition.getCallerUser(transientVars, args)`, null for anonymous. Access to the structure, the forest read and query validation switch to the run-as user; everything else, including evaluating the query on the issue's rows, runs as the caller.

The S-JQL query is evaluated on the issue's rows as the transition's caller, not as the run-as user: the run-as user only decides whether the structure is accessible, gets the forest and has the query validated, while `StructureQuery.checkRow` runs in the caller's `StructureAuth` context (as the original does). So inner JQL sees the caller's issues, and a query that is invalid for the caller makes every row not match even if it is valid for the run-as user. With an anonymous caller the query runs as anonymous.

For the condition, a query that parses but fails validation for the run-as user does not stop the check (a warning is logged): it goes on with that query, so an issue on no row of the structure gives `allowUnstructured`, and an issue on a row gives whatever `checkRow` answers, which is false for a query invalid for the caller. A query that does not parse gives false before rows are looked at. The validator blocks in both cases.

When a condition check took more than 1000 ms, `statistics-manager` gets one asynchronous total count of `wf.execution.1sec`, or `wf.execution.10sec` when more than 10000 ms, with `.jql` appended when the query has inner JQL in a composition (the rule `wf-statistics` uses for `wf.installed.hasJqlInComposition`). The validator path records nothing.

For a new condition, Jira's `getVelocityParams("input-parameters", null)` gives `runAsLead` true, `structureType` `default`, `allowUnstructured` true, `forValidator` false, no `queryDesc`, and these form values: `factory`; `structures` (what the current user can VIEW, non-archived, in `StructureManager` order); `structureNames` (each structure's name abbreviated to 40 characters with '...'); `namesakeStructures` (the structures whose abbreviated name is shared by another listed structure; the form then adds ID and owner); `examples`.

The form's `examples` is a list of (S-JQL text, label) pairs in this order: `child not in [resolution is empty]` ('All sub-issues must have a resolution'), `descendant not in [resolution is empty]` ('All sub-issues on all levels must have a resolution'), then two status pairs when Jira has statuses named closed or resolved (ignoring case, in `ConstantsManager.getStatuses()` order), then `leaf` ('The issue must not have sub-issues'). With one such status: `child not in [status != <name>]` ('All sub-issues must be {0}') and `descendant not in [status != <name>]` ('All sub-issues on all levels must be {0}'). With several: `[status not in (<a>, <b>)]`, with the `.multiple` labels ('All sub-issues must be {0} or {1}'), where {1} is the last status and {0} the others joined by ', '. Queries use the stored names, labels `Status.getNameTranslation`.

For `edit-parameters` and `view`, the stored arguments are read as strings (a missing or non-string argument is ''): `runAsLead` and `allowUnstructured` are booleans true only for the text `true`; `structureType` and `queryString` as stored; `structure` and `structureId` only for `manual` (`structureId` a long, -1 when unparseable); `queryDesc` stripped, validator only; `runAsUserName` and, for a found user, `runAsUserFullNameHtml` when not running as lead. `errors` maps a field name to a message. `edit-parameters` adds the form values above. `view` adds only `factory` and `forValidator`. A descriptor of the wrong kind (a condition descriptor for the validator factory or the reverse) adds no stored values.

When not running as lead, `errors["runAsUserName"]` is: `s.wf.form.error.run-as-user.not-found` ('Selected user {0} cannot be found.', with `name [key]`, or just the name when name and key are equal) for a stored key with no user; `s.wf.form.error.run-as-user.inactive` ('Selected user is inactive.') for an inactive user, and `runAsUserName` then shows the user's current name; with no stored key, `s.wf.form.error.run-as-user.empty` ('No user was specified.') for a blank name or `s.wf.form.error.run-as-user.name` ('Could not find a user for username "{0}".') otherwise.

`errors["structureType"]` is `s.wf.form.error.structure-type` ('Unknown structure option was selected.') for any value other than `default`, `manual` or `containing`. For `manual`: when the current user cannot VIEW the structure, `errors["structureId"]` is `s.wf.form.error.structure.inaccessible` ('Selected structure (#{0}) does not exist or you don''t have View permissions on it.') for error `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, else the exception's localized message; when it can but the run-as user cannot, `s.wf.form.error.structure.inaccessible-for-user` ('Selected structure is not accessible to the selected user.'). The run-as check needs a found run-as user. `containing` gives no error here.

`errors["queryString"]` is the localized message of a `StructureException` from parsing. For a query that parses, it is validated as the run-as user when one was found, else as the current user (which is always so when running as lead), and errors give `s.wf.form.error.query.invalid.for-user` ('The query is invalid for the selected user: {0}') or `s.wf.form.error.query.invalid` ('The query is invalid: {0}') with the messages joined by a space.

`getDescriptorParams(formParams)` returns what Jira stores, as strings: `runAsLead`; only when that is `false`, `runAsUserName` stripped of whitespace and `runAsUserKey` of the user with that name (a null value when no such user); `structureType`; only when that is `manual`, `structureId` as given (not validated); `queryString`; `allowUnstructured`. Nothing else is stored for a condition. Each named parameter must be in the form: Jira's single-parameter extraction fails with `IllegalArgumentException` when one is missing.

The form's namesake hint uses a user text: empty for a null user or an empty name; `s.manage.user.someone` for a user the viewer may not see (the viewer must be an admin, hold the `USER_PICKER` global permission, or be that user); otherwise the user name, followed by ` (display name) ` when that differs, HTML-encoded. `runAsUserFullNameHtml` is the same text.

The module is a `workflow-validator` with key `structure-workflow-validator`, name 'Issue Matches Structure Query', i18n name key `s.wf.validator.name`, description key `s.wf.validator.desc`, `validator-class` `com.almworks.jira.structure.workflow.StructureWorkflowChecker`, and velocity resources `view`, `input-parameters` and `edit-parameters`. Unlike the condition it is enabled by default.

`StructureWorkflowChecker.validate(transientVars, args, propertySet)` returns normally when the transition may go on and otherwise throws `InvalidInputException` with one message: the prefix, a space, the reason. The prefix is `s.wf.validator-message.prefix` ('Workflow transition was blocked by the Structure Validator.') for a failed requirement, or `s.wf.validator-message.prefix.invalid-params` ('Workflow transition was blocked because Structure Validator parameters are incorrect.') for a bad configuration. A `RuntimeException` during the check is logged and becomes the plain prefix with `s.wf.block-reason.exception` ('An internal error occurred.').

First check: when `StructureConfiguration.isProjectEnabled(issue's project)` is false, the transition passes if `allowUnstructured` is `true`; otherwise it is blocked with the invalid-params prefix and `s.wf.block-reason.project-disabled` ('Structure should be enabled for the project that the issue belongs to.'). No other argument is looked at.

Second check, the run-as user, invalid-params prefix for all: with `runAsLead` `true` it is the project lead, and with no project or lead the reason is `s.wf.block-reason.run-as-user.lead` ('The project that the issue belongs to must have a lead user.'). Otherwise it is the user with key `runAsUserKey`; none found gives `s.wf.block-reason.run-as-user.manual` ('Could not find the user for username "{0}".') with the stored name, or `.manual.no-name` ('No user was specified.') for a blank name. Then an inactive user gives `s.wf.block-reason.run-as-user.inactive` ('User {0} is inactive.'), and a user without `ProjectPermissions.BROWSE_PROJECTS` on the issue gives `s.wf.block-reason.run-as-user.cant-browse-issue` ('The issue is inaccessible to user {0}.').

Third check, invalid-params prefix: `structureType` `containing` is read as `default` (a warning is logged). A value other than `default` or `manual`, or none, gives `s.wf.block-reason.structure-type` ('Invalid structure option: {0}.'). `manual` reads `structureId`; negative or unparseable gives `s.wf.block-reason.structure.id` ('Invalid structure ID: {0}.') with the stored text. `default` uses `StructureConfiguration.getDefaultStructureId(issue's project)`. A structure the run-as user cannot VIEW, including 0 for no default, gives `s.wf.block-reason.structure.inaccessible` ('Structure #{0} does not exist or is inaccessible to user {1}.').

In `s.wf.block-reason.structure.inaccessible` the ID goes to Jira's message formatting as a number, not as text, so it appears with the locale's digit grouping ('#1,234'), and likewise in `s.wf.form.error.structure.inaccessible` (as the original does).

Fourth check: the forest is read as the run-as user from `ForestSpec.unsecuredStructure(id)`, so it is not filtered by anyone's permissions. A `StructureException` gives the invalid-params prefix and `s.wf.block-reason.forest` ('Could not retrieve the forest of structure {0}.').

Fifth check, invalid-params prefix: a `queryString` that does not parse gives `s.wf.block-reason.query.syntax` ('S-JQL query is invalid.'). A missing argument is parsed as ''. A query with errors when validated as the run-as user is parsed again from `getSanitizedQueryString()` and validated again: if that gives errors, the reason is `s.wf.block-reason.query.invalid` ('S-JQL query is invalid for user {0}: {1}') with those messages joined by a space, so only sanitised text reaches the user. If it gives none, or the sanitised text does not parse, the reason is `s.wf.block-reason.query.invalid.generic` ('S-JQL query is invalid for user {0}.').

Last check, the rows: every row of the forest showing this issue (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`, the issue ID) is tried with `checkRow` until one matches, so an issue added several times passes when any of its rows matches. With rows and at least one match the transition passes.

When no row of the forest shows the issue, the transition passes if `allowUnstructured` is `true`. Any other value blocks it with the plain prefix and `s.wf.block-reason.unstructured` ('Issue must be contained in structure {0}.').

When the issue is on rows and none matches, the transition is blocked with the plain prefix and `s.wf.block-reason.match` ('{0}. Checked structure {1} on behalf of user {2}.') with {0} the stripped `queryDesc`, or, when that is empty, `s.wf.block-reason.match.default` ('Issue must match the specified S-JQL query').

In block reasons a structure is shown as `"<name abbreviated to 40>" (#<id>)` when the caller can VIEW it, else `#<id>`. A user is shown as `?` when null or blank-named; as the name alone when the display name is equal or blank, or when the caller may not see the user (`USER_PICKER` global permission, admin, or the user themselves); otherwise as `name (display name)`.

The validator's factory works as the condition's (`structure-workflow-condition`), with these differences. `forValidator` is true. For new validators `queryDesc` starts as `s.wf.block-reason.match.default`. `getDescriptorParams` also stores `queryDesc`, unstripped. Edit and view add `queryDesc` stripped of whitespace.

The `view` template shows, as facts: for a validator the `queryDesc` followed by '.' when it is not empty, else `s.wf.view.header` ('Issue must match the Structure query.'); the structure (the default option text, the name of a `manual` structure, the `containing` text with the warning `s.wf.form.structure-type.deprecated.option`, or '?'); the query; allow or block for unstructured issues; the run-as user (project lead, the user text, or '?'); and each message of `errors` beside its field.

The module is an `ownership-transfer-handler` with key `structure-ownership-transfer-handler` and `restrict application="jira" version="[8.7.0,)"`. `getAffectedEntities(param)` finds the user of `param.getCurrentUserKey()`. For a key with no user it returns an empty collection and asks no contributor. Otherwise it returns the contributors' lists concatenated, each entity of type `AffectedEntityType.TRANSFER_OWNERSHIP`, all computed under `StructureAuth.sudo` with security overridden, so everything the contributor would list is seen whoever runs it. The order between contributors is not defined.

Every entity keeps the contributor's description key and number of occurrences. It gets a link only when the contributor gave both a URI and a link text key; a URI that does not parse gives no link, logged once, and no error.

`update(param)` needs both `getCurrentUserKey()` and `getTransferToUserKey()` to resolve to users. If either does not, it returns a result without errors and does nothing. Otherwise it calls every contributor, under `StructureAuth.sudo` with security overridden, even after an earlier one reported errors, and returns one `ServiceResult` with all errors and warnings merged. A runtime exception from a contributor is not caught.

The module is a `user-key-change-handler` with key `structure-user-key-change-handler` and `restrict application="jira" version="[8.7.0,)"`. It gathers the contributions of `history-recorder` (`AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY.C_USER_KEY`), `ao-based-statistics-service` (`AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS.C_USERKEY`) and `effector-process-manager` (`AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.C_USER_KEY`). `getAffectedEntities(param)` finds the user of `param.getOriginal()`; with no such user it returns an empty collection and asks no contributor. Otherwise it returns the contributors' lists concatenated, each entity of type `AffectedEntityType.ANONYMIZE` with the description key, occurrences and link rule of the ownership handler, under `StructureAuth.sudo` with security overridden.

`update(param)` calls every contributor with `param.getOriginal()` and `param.getTarget()` under `StructureAuth.sudo` with security overridden, without checking that a user exists for either key, even after an earlier contributor reported errors. For a user with effector processes (`AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS` rows whose `C_USER_KEY` is the user's key, in any status) the contribution of `effector-process-manager` is one entity with description key `s.anonymize.effector-processes.description` ('Structure effector processes') and the number of processes as occurrences, no link. With no processes it contributes nothing.

Changing a key from old to new sets `C_USER_KEY` to new in the old key's `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS` rows and, when any row changed, drops the cached processes of those rows and the running-process lists of both keys, so `EffectorProcessManager` shows the new key at once. Any exception is logged and the result carries the error `s.anonymize.effector-processes.failed` ('Failed to anonymize Structure effector processes'); nothing is thrown.
