The module is a `simple-link-factory` with key `slf-structure-configs-factory`, name 'menu:Structure|Recent Structures Factory', section `wi-structure-link/ws-structure-configs`, weight 50 and `lazy="true"`.

The number of links is at most max(4, D / 2) with integer division, D being Jira's `jira.max.issue.filter.dropdown.items` (`ApplicationProperties.getDefaultBackedString`); a value that is not a number counts as 10 (a warning is logged). So D = 20 gives 10, D = 10 gives 5, D = 3 gives 4.

Links are the given user's recent structures first (from `recents-manager`, in its order), up to the limit. If the limit is not reached, the structures from `getAllStructures(VIEW)` follow, reordered by `StructureFavoriteManager.sortByPopularity(list, user)`, skipping those already listed, up to the limit. No structure appears twice. When the limit is reached by recents, the viewable list is not read.

A link has ID `wi-structure-recent-<id>`, label the structure's name abbreviated to 40 characters ('...' at the end, 37 characters kept), title the trimmed name or, with a non-empty trimmed description, `<name> - <description>`, URL `<base>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, and no icon, style or access key. The base URL comes from `VelocityRequestContextFactory.getJiraVelocityRequestContext().getBaseUrl()`.
`getLinks(user, params)` runs as the given user with security not overridden (`StructureAuth.sudo(user, false, ...)`), a null user meaning anonymous. `StructureStoppedException` gives an empty list.

The link factory gets its working part from the plugin's enabled `helper` module (`PluginAccessor.getEnabledPluginModule("com.almworks.jira.structure:helper")`). While that module is not enabled, gives no instance or has no factory, `getLinks` returns an empty list and logs a warning, without an exception, so the menu shows nothing during plugin start or stop. The helper creates the factory once, on first use.

When the working part throws `IllegalStateException` or an exception of class `org.springframework.osgi.service.importer.ServiceProxyDestroyedException` (a stale service after a plugin reload), the reference is dropped, a warning is logged, the `helper` module is looked up again and the call is retried once. A `StructureStoppedException` during the retry gives an empty list; any other exception of the retry reaches the caller. Any other runtime exception of the first attempt reaches the caller, without retry.

The module is a `simple-link-factory` with key `slf-favorite-structures-factory`, name 'menu:Structure|Favorite Structures Factory', section `wi-structure-link/ws-favorite-structures`, weight 60 and `lazy="true"`.

Links are the structures of `StructureFavoriteManager.getFavorites(user)` in that order, up to max(4, D / 2) with D as for `slf-structure-configs-factory`. A link has ID `wi-structure-favorite-<id>` and the label, title, URL and empty fields of a recent-structure link.

When there are more favourites than the limit, one extra link follows them: ID `wi-structure-favorite-more`, label `s.desc.structure-link.favorites.more.label` ('more...'), title `s.desc.structure-link.favorites.more.tooltip` ('View all your favorite structures'), URL `<base>/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?view=favorites`. So the list can hold limit + 1 links. With exactly the limit there is no such link.
`getLinks` has the run-as-user, stopped, helper-not-ready and retry behaviour of `slf-structure-configs-factory`.

On Jira 9.12 the module is a `url-reading-web-resource-transformer` with key `widget-i18n-transformer`, name 'web-resource-transformer:I18n-Jira9' and `restrict application="jira" version="[9.0.0,10.0.0)"`. Web resources use it through `<transformation extension="js"><transformer key="widget-i18n-transformer"/>`, among them `widget-i18n`.
The transformer's `makeUrlBuilder` adds to the web resource URL what `widget-i18n-transformer-common` claims, the `locale` query parameter, and nothing else.

When a resource is transformed, the transformer reads the query parameter `locale` from the request's parameters and asks `widget-i18n-transformer-common` for a bundle for the resource's location and that locale. No bundle: the original resource is served unchanged (`nextResource()`). A bundle: it is served in place of the original as a `DownloadableResource`.

The downloadable resource that replaces the original delegates to the bundle: `isResourceModified`, `serveResource`, `streamResource` and `getContentType` behave as `widget-i18n-transformer-cache` claims. `serveResource` sets the content type only when it is not empty, and a failure to get or write the output stream gives `DownloadException`. A failure to flush after writing is only logged.

The plugin descriptor has exactly one `ao` element, with key `ao` and namespace `com.almworks.jira.structure`. That namespace is what makes Active Objects use the table prefix `AO_8BAD1B_` (the last six hex digits of the namespace's MD5, `7f218d86d83be3046b5516c4528bad1b`, upper-cased), so with the same namespace a replacement sees the tables the original left in the database, and with any other it sees none of them.

The `ao` element lists 39 `entity` children, one for each table in SPEC §1.5 and no more: reading the descriptor and each entity's explicit table name gives exactly those 39 names, each entity with its own table, and nothing else. No entity relies on Active Objects deriving a table name from the entity's class name, so renaming an entity type does not move its table.

The `ao` element has only `entity` children: it declares no Active Objects upgrade task, so the module writes no model version of its own. On plugin start, Active Objects only compares the declared entities with the database: a missing table or column is created, and rows the original wrote are left in place. The module itself runs no data migration.

The module's whole job is to declare the schema: it does no reads or writes of its own. All access to these tables goes through the modules that use Active Objects (`ao-helper`, `structure-database-provider`, `ao-initializer` and the stores built on them), and it is those modules' claims that say when tables are first used and what happens before Active Objects is ready.

Those pages read: the REST back-off override and values, the job id, whether there is data and whether the log action applies, with the issue id for it; the login page's context path, error message and which of captcha, remember-me, forgot-password, admin form and one-time-password input it shows, public mode and the authentication resource; whether login is allowed, a global permission is missing or the structure was deleted, with the rendered login page and issue operations; migration configurations and their ids, names, status, structures, creator, run time, extensions and draft and ready flags; the structure field's name translation and id; each option's id, label, icon and selectability; the process name, activity, buttons, percent complete, process id, finished flag and state text; and a formatted owner. No listed method changes state.

Common access gate of `rest-v1` and `rest-v2`: the `loggedIn` check looks at the first `loggedIn` query parameter only and matches the exact lower-case text `true`. `loggedIn=TRUE`, `loggedIn=1`, or `loggedIn=false&loggedIn=true` do not trigger it; the caller then goes on to the next gate step. The caller counts as anonymous when `StructureAuth.getUser()` is null. The 401 has no body and carries `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`.

Common access gate: a marker on the method wins over one on its resource class. When either is present only the administrator check runs: a Jira administrator without the plugin's 'use' permission passes, and a resource marked system-administrator-only asks for Jira's system administrator permission instead of administrator. An anonymous caller on a marked endpoint gets 403 `permission violation` (401 only with `loggedIn=true`).

Administrator-only resources beyond the four endpoints SPEC.md §1.3 lists: every method of `/rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity`, `/rest/structure/2.0/configuration` and `/rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` needs a Jira administrator (the last also a websudo session), and every method of `/rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration` needs a Jira system administrator. A plain administrator gets 403 `permission violation` on `cloudmigration`.

Exception mapper of `rest-v1` and `rest-v2`: an `InvocationTargetException` is unwrapped to its cause first (one without a cause gives 500 with an empty text body). The first matching rule then wins, in this order: unparseable JSON; plugin stopped or job failure; explicit error response; invalid input; forest lock timeout; domain error; anything else. So an explicit error response wrapping a stopped-plugin exception answers 503, not its own status, and a domain error whose root cause is invalid data answers 400 `Invalid request data`.

Exception mapper: the 400 for unparseable JSON applies to every exception descending from Jackson 1's `org.codehaus.jackson.JsonProcessingException`, so a well-formed body that cannot be bound to the target shape (mapping failure) is answered the same way as broken syntax. The error object has `error` = `Cannot parse request JSON`, `message` and `localizedMessage` both from the exception, and no `code`.

Exception mapper: 503 `service unavailable` is given when the root cause of the exception chain, at any depth, is a `StructureStoppedException`, or when the exception itself (not a cause of it) is a `StructureJobException`. A `StructureJobException` wrapped in another exception is not matched by this rule.

Exception mapper: the 400 `Invalid request data` applies when the root cause of the chain, at any depth, is the plugin's invalid-data exception, or when the exception itself is an `IllegalArgumentException` or a subclass such as `NumberFormatException`. An `IllegalArgumentException` that is only a cause of another exception is not matched and ends up as a 500. The body's `message` is the message of the outer exception, and `code` and `localizedMessage` are absent.

Exception mapper, domain error (`StructureException`): `code` is the numeric code and `error` is `<NAME>[<code>]`, for example `INVALID_PARAMETER[2400]` and `INVALID_JQL[6003]`, for public and for the plugin's own codes. `structureId` and `viewId` appear only when positive. `rowId` is always present, 0 when the error has no row. `itemId` and `itemDescription` appear only when the error names an item. `message` and `localizedMessage` come from the exception.

Exception mapper, anything else: 500 with the exception's message as plain text. An exception without a message (a null message) gives 500 with no body and no content type. An `IllegalAccessException` raised by the invocation gives 500 with its message and is not logged.

Exception mapper logging: an unmapped exception is logged at error level with the text `[Structure REST API] error when calling <HTTP method> /<path and query relative to the REST base>`. A stopped-plugin or job failure, invalid input, and a domain error outside the not-found and no-permission categories are logged only discreetly (warning without stack trace unless debug logging is on). Not-found and no-permission domain errors, explicit error responses, JSON errors and lock timeouts are not logged.

Every reply built by the exception mapper and by the common access gate carries `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`, whatever its status; plain-text replies with a message have `Content-Type: text/plain`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/dateFormatStyle`: it lists the seven styles of `format-helper` in that module's order, each with `style` and `sample`, where `sample` is the time of the request formatted by that style for the current user. There are no parameters, and anonymous callers who pass the gate get samples in Jira's default locale.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/userPickerPermission`: it answers exactly Jira's `GlobalPermissionManager.hasPermission(USER_PICKER, user)` for the `StructureAuth` user, null for anonymous. There is no administrator shortcut: an administrator without the user picker permission gets `false`, unlike `canBrowseUsers` of `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/timezone`: an omitted or empty `name` uses `TimeZoneManager.getLoggedInUserTimeZone()`. Any other value goes through `java.util.TimeZone.getTimeZone`, so `GMT+2` answers `GMT+02:00`, and a blank or unknown id answers `GMT` with 200, never an error. `offset` is the negated offset of the zone at the time of the request, so it follows daylight saving.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/roles`: an anonymous caller who passes the gate gets 403 with no body and no content type. A logged-in caller gets every role from Jira's `ProjectRoleManager.getProjectRoles()` in that order, with `id`, `name` and `description`. The list is not limited by the caller's memberships.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/groups` with `assignable=true`: the reply is `StructurePluginHelper.getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser()` in its order, so no 'browse users' permission is needed. The rule choosing the groups is the helper's (see C-0008). Null group entries are dropped.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/groups` without `assignable` or with `assignable=false`: the caller, taken from `StructureAuth`, must hold Jira's administer or user picker global permission. Otherwise the reply is 403 with the plain text `listing all groups requires "Browse Users" permission`. Anonymous callers hold neither unless Jira grants the user picker to anonymous. When allowed, every group of `GroupManager.getAllGroups()` is listed in that order.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects`: `permission` goes through Jira's `ProjectPermissions.systemProjectPermissionKeyByShortName`, which ignores case and matches by prefix. So `browse`, `Browse` and `BROWSE_PROJECTS` select Browse Projects, and `create`, `CREATE`, `createIssue` and `createattachment` select Create Issues. Everything else gives 400 `invalid permission requested`: names of other permissions, names with no match, and a blank value such as `permission=`. The check comes before any project is read. Only an omitted parameter means Browse Projects.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects`: the candidates are `StructureConfiguration.getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()`, filtered by the chosen permission for the Jira-logged-in user (`StructurePluginHelper.getUser()`) and sorted with Jira's `ProjectNameComparator`. Each entry has `key`, `id`, `name`, `description` and `iconUrl` = `AvatarService.getProjectAvatarURL(project, SMALL)`. With no matching project the reply is 200 with an empty `projects`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects` with `withRoles=true`: a logged-in caller gets the same `userRoles` on every project (ids of all Jira project roles, roles with a null id skipped) and `roles` holding those roles, in no fixed order. An anonymous caller gets `userRoles: []` on every project and no `roles`. With no project in the reply `roles` is absent too, even for a logged-in caller. Without `withRoles`, `userRoles` and `roles` are both absent.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types`, `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions` read `projects` the same way: only the exact text `*` means all, and other values are split on commas with pieces trimmed. Empty pieces and pieces that are not integers are skipped silently, so `projects=abc` is an empty selection with 200, not an error. The set selected from is `StructurePluginHelper.getStructureProjectsForCurrentUser()`. `types` is split the same way, trimmed and compared as strings against the ids of the selected projects' types; unknown ids are ignored.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types`: types of all selected projects' issue type schemes (`IssueTypeSchemeManager.getIssueTypesForProject`) are merged by id, sub-task types included, and sorted by Jira's standard order for issue constants, which is by name. Each element has `id`, translated `name` and `description`, `iconUrl` from `getCompleteIconUrl()`, `sequence` and `subTask`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions` choose workflows from `WorkflowSchemeManager.getWorkflowMap(project)` of each selected project; a project with a null map is skipped. Each selected type uses the workflow name mapped to its id. A type with no name or an empty name uses the map's default entry (null key). Names are merged, and a name for which `WorkflowManager.getWorkflow` returns null is skipped. No selected project or no selected type means no workflows and an empty list with 200.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses`: the linked statuses of all selected workflows are merged without duplicates and sorted by Jira's natural order of `StatusCategory`; statuses of equal category keep their merge order, which depends on workflow order and is not fixed. Each element has the `issue-status-constant` keys, `color` being `getStatusCategory().getColorName()`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions`: a null or empty `status` gives 400 `must have status` before anything else is read. A `status` for which `ConstantsManager.getStatus` returns null gives 400 `unknown status`, also when the project or type selection is empty.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions`: for each selected workflow with a step linked to the status, it lists the workflow's actions from `getAllActions()`, skipping the initial action and any action without an unconditional result. An action is listed when its unconditional result names exactly that step. An action whose result stays in the current step is therefore not listed, even when it is available from that status. A workflow without such a step adds nothing. A known status that no selected workflow uses gives 200 with empty `transitions`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions`: each entry has `workflow` = the workflow name, `action` = the action id, `name` = the action name, and `sourceStatuses` = the statuses linked to `JiraWorkflow.getStepsForTransition(action)` (steps with no linked status skipped) as `issue-constant`, without `color`. The same transition is listed once per workflow that has it; no merging is done across workflows.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/license`: for a Jira administrator it answers 200 with a `license-info` that reports the fixed state of `license-manager`, with exactly the values of SPEC.md 1.1: `type` `commercial`, `licensee` and `serial` empty, `unlimitedUsers` true, `maxUsers` 0, `serverLocked` false, `marketplaceLicense` false and `source` `none`; `licensedServers`, `licenseExpiration` and `maintenanceExpiration` are absent. It reads no stored licence, and non-administrators get the gate's 403.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/licenses`: for a Jira administrator it answers 200 with an object that always has the key `com.almworks.jira.structure` and one key per companion extension reporting a product key, by `StructureCoreExtension.getAppSupportInfo()`. Every value is the same fixed `license-info` as `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/license`, for the extensions too. Non-administrators get the gate's 403.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate`: a missing `issue` gives 400 `no issues requested`. A non-existent issue gives 200 with `issue` echoed and top-level `error`, i18n `s.rest.config.fields.bad-issue-id` ('The requested issue does not exist or you don't have permission to view it. Try reloading the page, or speak with your Jira administrator.'), as does an issue with a project the `StructureAuth` user cannot browse. On that path `canChangeOriginalEstimate` is false and `fields` is absent. An issue in a project where the plugin is disabled is served normally; no project check is made.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: with no `field`, all fields of Jira's screen renderer for the operation are taken except `issuelinks`, `worklogged` and `attachment`. With `field` given, exactly those ids are taken, and an explicitly requested `issuelinks`, `worklogged` or `attachment` is rendered when it is on the screen.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: each field on the screen gets an entry with `name` = its name key translated for the user. When Jira says it is not shown for the issue, when ScriptRunner lists it as read-only for the issue, or when rendering throws, the entry has `error` = `s.rest.config.fields.not-applicable` ('Cannot edit {0} of issue {1}.', field name, issue key) and no HTML. Otherwise it has `createHtml` for create or `editHtml` for update, rendered with display parameters `theme` = `aui`, `noHeader` = `true`, `isFirstField` = true and `isLastField` = true. A failure in one field never fails the reply.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: a requested id that is not on the screen, unknown ids included, gets an entry holding only `error` = `s.w.config.fields.load-got-nothing` ('No editor for this field, sorry. Perhaps it's read-only, or not added to the edit screen.'), with no `name`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate`: before rendering, every field shown for the issue is filled from the issue. A field whose fill-in throws is skipped silently here (and rendered without its value). ScriptRunner's read-only list is asked only for an issue with an id; when ScriptRunner is absent no field is read-only for that reason. A prospective issue of `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate` is not filled this way.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: when fields are loaded, `canChangeOriginalEstimate` is true if the issue has no time spent, or time spent is not positive, or Jira's option `jira.timetracking.estimates.legacy.behaviour` is off. The key is always in the reply and is false on every path that loads no fields, including the top-level `error` paths and the project and issue type picker case.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: when Jira gives no screen renderer, the reply is 200 with top-level `error` = `s.rest.config.fields.no-renderer` ('Cannot load renderer for issue {0}.', issue key or empty) and `fields` as an empty object.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` with `field=status`: the `status` entry has `name` = the literal `status` and `editHtml` = `<select class="s-issue-status-editor" name="status">` holding one option per line, of the form `<option value="<status id>" status-color="<category colour name>" selected-or-empty data-transition-with-view="<action id or empty>"><HTML-escaped status name></option>`. `selected` is present on the issue's current status. The action id is filled only when the transition has a non-empty view.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` with `field=status`: the options are the issue's current status first, then the target status of each action of Jira's `IssueWorkflowManager.getSortedAvailableActions(issue, user)` in that order, without duplicates. An option's transition is looked up in the issue's workflow from the current status; when none or several lead there, its action is empty but the option stays. `status` is only rendered when requested by name, never in the all-fields case.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forUpdate` with `field=status`: when the status editor cannot be built (no workflow for the issue, current status not in the workflow, or any exception), the entry for `status` carries the generic `s.w.config.fields.load-got-nothing` text, not `s.rest.config.fields.not-applicable` (as the original does). The reply stays 200 and other fields are unaffected.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: with neither `sample` nor both `project` and `issuetype`, the reply is 400 `specify either sample issue, or project and type or both`. Unless the project-and-type picker case applies, an unknown `project` gives 400 with the message of Jira's `IllegalArgumentException`, and an `issuetype` that gives no issue type gives 400 `cannot find issue type`. Nothing else is rendered in those cases.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate` with `sample`: a sample that does not exist or that the `StructureAuth` user cannot browse gives 200 with `issue` = the sample id, `forCreate` true and top-level `error` = `s.rest.config.fields.bad-issue-id`, even when `project` and `issuetype` are given. Otherwise a missing `project` or `issuetype` is taken from the sample, and `project` and `issueType` are echoed in the reply.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: the prospective issue is new and is never stored. For each item of Jira's create screen except `project`, `summary` and, unless the sample is a sub-task, `issuetype`, values are copied from the sample or defaulted and applied to the prospective issue, so later fields see the earlier values. The sample's parent id is set on the prospective issue when the sample is a sub-task. An exception here is not caught per field and goes to the exception mapper.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate` with a sample: a field's value is copied from the sample when its id is one of `issuetype`, `assignee`, `environment`, `priority`, `security`, `versions`, `fixVersions`, `components`, or when it is a custom field that is required in the field layout. Every other field gets Jira's default (`populateDefaults`) instead of the sample's value.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: `summary`, and `project` or `issuetype` if the create screen has them, are skipped only for filling values. They are still rendered like any other field when selected, so `summary` appears with `createHtml` in the all-fields reply when it is on the create screen.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: the Browse Projects check also applies to the prospective issue. A caller who cannot browse the target project gets 200 with top-level `error` = `s.rest.config.fields.bad-issue-id` and no `fields`, with `forCreate`, `project` and `issueType` still set. `structuredProjects` is absent outside the picker case, and no Create Issues permission or plugin enablement is checked here.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: when `sample` is absent and `field` holds exactly `project` and `issuetype` once each, in any order, the picker case applies even if `project` or `issuetype` parameters are given. The reply has `forCreate` true, `fields` with those two ids, each holding `createHtml` from Jira's project and issue type system fields for a new issue. If the HTML is null or empty, the entry has `error` = `s.w.config.fields.load-got-nothing` instead. No `name` is set, and neither `issue`, `project` nor `issueType`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`, picker case: `structuredProjects` is absent when `StructureConfiguration.isEnabledForAllProjects()` is true. Otherwise it holds the ids, in no fixed order, of the projects in both `PermissionManager.getProjects(CREATE_ISSUES, user)` and `getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()`, for the Jira-logged-in user; it is an empty array when there are none. The case itself needs no permission beyond the gate.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forCreate`: when `sample` is absent, one `project` and one `issuetype` are removed from the `field` list before anything else, and if the picker case does not apply the remaining list is used. So `field=project&field=assignee` renders only `assignee`, and `field=project` alone, with `project` and `issuetype` parameters, leaves an empty list and renders all fields (as the original does). With `sample` the list is used as given.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate`: checks run in this order after the gate: a missing `type` gives 400 `no item type requested`; a missing `field` gives 400 `no field requested`; a `type` other than exactly `memo` or `planning-task` gives 400 `item type is not supported`, an empty `type` included. A `type` long enough to make the full type id exceed 190 characters is rejected by `ItemIdentity` with the mapper's 400 `Invalid request data`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate`: `id`, `itemId` (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-<type>/<id>`) and `itemType` are in the reply on every 200 path, also when it carries `error`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate`: the item is looked up by id and its stored type must equal the requested type. A missing item, id 0, or an item of the other type gives 200 with `error` = `s.rest.config.fields.bad-item-id` ('The requested item does not exist or you don't have permission to view it. Try reloading the page, or speak with your Jira administrator.'). No ownership or per-item permission check is made: any caller past the gate gets the editor of any existing memo or planning task.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate`: a `field` unknown to `structure-field-manager` or hidden by the item's field configuration gives 200 with `error` = `s.rest.config.memo.fields.not-supported` ('Editing of '{0}' is not supported for this item.', the requested id). A visible but not editable field gives `error` = `s.ext.type.memo.error.uneditable-field` ('Field {0} isn't editable', the name translated to the user's locale). The configuration is that of `generic-item-field-config-service`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate`: on success `fields` has the one requested id, with `id`, `name` = the field's plain, untranslated name, and `editHtml` = the HTML of the field's type for the item's current value and field configuration. When reading or rendering throws, the entry has `error` = `s.rest.config.memo.fields.not-applicable` ('Cannot edit {0} of memo {1}.', field name, item id) and no HTML, the word 'memo' being used for planning tasks too. The reply stays 200.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forMemoUpdate`: it answers exactly as `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/forGenericItemUpdate` with `type` = `memo`, `id` = `memoId` and `field` = `fieldId`. A missing `memoId` gives 500 before `fieldId` is looked at, so with both missing the reply is 500, not 400. A missing `fieldId` alone gives 400 `no field requested`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: a context exists when `forIssue` is positive, `forProject` is non-empty, or `forAgileBoard` is positive. Without one the reply is 400 `missing forIssue or forProject or forAgileBoard`, before any issue or project is read. So `forIssue=0` alone is a 400, but `forIssue=0&forProject=KEY` passes.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: the page type goes by which parameters are present, not by their being positive or non-empty: any `forAgileBoard`, even 0, makes it the agile board page; otherwise any `forProject`, even empty, the project page; otherwise the issue page. On the agile board page the auto-switch mode is always `off`, by `structure-configuration`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: any non-null `forIssue`, also 0 or negative, is looked up. A missing or not browsable issue gives 404 with plain text `cannot process settings for issue <id>, code ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE[4700]`. So `forIssue=-1&forProject=KEY` passes the context check and then answers 404. An issue with no project gives 500 `issue <issue> without a project`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: the issue is checked without the project-enablement check, so an issue in a project where the plugin is disabled is served like any other, with or without `forAgileBoard`. It is never rejected for that reason.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: a resolved issue decides the project, and `forProject` is then ignored without being checked, even if it does not exist. Without an issue, a non-null `forProject` is looked up by key: an unknown key, an empty key, or a project the `StructureAuth` user cannot browse all give 404 with plain text `cannot process settings for the project`. With neither, the project is null and the instance-wide values apply.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: on the project page the reply has `projectAdmin`, true when a project is known and the user has Administer Projects on it, and no issue keys. On any other page with a resolved issue, agile board page included, it has `autoCollapse` and `keepStructureWhenNavigating` (true when unset) and `issueMissingFromInitialStructure`, and no `projectAdmin`. On an agile board page with no issue it has none of those keys.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: `autoSwitch`, the code of the strategy from `ui-configurator`, and `userConfigurable`, true when `StructureAuth.getUser()` is non-null, are always present. `singleStructure` is true or absent, never false. `defaultStructure` and `initialStructure` are absent when `ui-configurator` gives none, and otherwise are `structure-summary` objects without permissions or owner.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: `issueMissingFromInitialStructure` is true when there is no initial structure or when the issue is not in that structure's stored forest, checked without any access check.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: `preferredStructure` and the cookie `structure3.navigation.hint` go to `ui-configurator` unvalidated; an unknown, unviewable or malformed value is skipped and never gives an error. `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` honours the cookie but has no preferred structure.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: checks run in this order, the first failure answering: anonymous gives 403 `permission violation`; a null body gives 400 `null request`; no context gives 400 `missing forIssue or forProject or forAgileBoard`; the issue (only when `forIssue` is positive) and the project give their errors; an `autoSwitch` other than exactly `off`, `withIssue` or `default` gives 400 `unknown auto-switch mode`, an empty string included. Nothing is stored unless all of these pass.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: it stores through `StructureConfiguration.setUISettings(user, project, settings)` for the caller only, never instance-wide values. `project` is the issue's project or the `forProject` project, and null when only `forAgileBoard` is given. The auto-switch mode is set for `StructurePage.ISSUE_VIEW` when `forIssue` is positive, and otherwise for `StructurePage.PROJECT_TAB`, also on the agile board. `autoCollapse` and `keepStructureWhenNavigating` are set when non-null, so JSON null means unchanged.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui`: with no `autoSwitch`, `autoCollapse` or `keepStructureWhenNavigating` in the body, `setUISettings` is not called at all and the reply is the current panel configuration with 200.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` with a non-positive `forIssue` plus a valid `forProject`: the preferences are stored for the project and the recomputed configuration then fails with the 404 of an unknown issue, so the caller sees an error although the change was saved (as the original does).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `structureVersion` is the installed plugin version and `jiraVersion` the Jira version from `BuildUtilsInfo` (null if unavailable). `jiraClusterNodeId` is `ClusterManager.getNodeId()`. `jiraEmailNotificationsEnabled` is the opposite of `MailFactory.getSettings().isSendingDisabled()`.
`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `licenseInvalid` is never in the reply, since the plugin always counts as licensed (`license-manager`).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `jiraDateTimeFormats` holds `dateFormat`, `dateTimeFormat`, `datePickerJavascriptFormat` and `datePickerJavaFormat` from Jira's default-backed application properties `jira.lf.date.dmy`, `jira.lf.date.time`, `jira.date.picker.javascript.format` and `jira.date.picker.java.format`. `firstDayOfWeek` is `Calendar.getInstance(locale).getFirstDayOfWeek() - 1`, with the locale of the `StructureAuth` user.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `jiraFields` starts from `FieldManager.getAvailableNavigableFields(user)` for the Jira-logged-in user. A custom field is left out when its type has neither a view template nor a column view template. The rest are sorted with Jira's `FieldNameComparator` for the user's language. Each has `id`, `name` and `visible`; `type`, `items`, `customId` and `custom` come from `getJsonSchema()` and are given only for a field implementing Jira's `RestAwareField`.
`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: a field's `visible` is true when its id appears on any tab of any screen from `FieldScreenManager.getFieldScreens()`, whatever the project or scheme.
`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: a Jira `FieldException` while listing fields gives 500 with plain text `cannot retrieve columns: <message>` and a warning in the log.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `jiraAgileRankFields` holds the numeric ids from Jira Software's `RankService.getRankFields()`. It is an empty array, never an error, when Jira Software is absent, the service is not found, or the lookup throws any exception or linkage error.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`, all for the Jira-logged-in user: `canCreate` comes from `permissions-cache`; `canBrowseUsers` is true for an administrator or with the global user picker permission; `canBulkChange` is the global bulk change permission; `canCreateViews`, `canShareViews` and `canManageGlobalSavedColumns` are the `StructurePluginHelper` answers; `canCreatePerspective` is the `perspective-manager` answer; `canRunEffectorsOnQueryResults` is the `CoreAppPermissions.EXECUTE_EFFECTORS_ON_QUERIES` answer of `permissions-cache`. All are always present as booleans.
`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `admin` is true for a Jira administrator and absent otherwise; `anonymous` is true for an anonymous caller and absent otherwise. Neither is ever false.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `features.useStructuresActionsLink` is the setting `structure.feature.useStructuresActionsLink` (default true). `features.altInitialValuesInDialog` is present, as true, only when the setting `structure.feature.altInitialValuesInDialog` is on (default off). These settings are read as a Jira application property when non-empty, else as a JVM system property.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: with the setting `structure.welcome.enabled` off, `hideHelp` is true and `hideHelpAdminTips` absent. With it on (default) `hideHelp` is absent and `hideHelpAdminTips` is true only when `help-content-manager` has no stored content. Neither is ever false.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `extensions` maps each extension's key to its `StructureCoreExtension.getConfigurationForWidget()`, in the extensions' order, skipping null or empty maps. It is absent when nothing remains.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `exportLinks` comes from the web interface manager's displayable web items of location `structure.export.menu`, asked with a context holding the HTTP request under `request`, in that order. Each has `label`, `title`, `iconClasses` = the item's style class, `moduleKey` = its complete key and `url`. It is absent when there are none.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `externalGenericItemTypes` lists item types of other apps: types implementing `GenericItemType` whose descriptor is not hidden and whose plugin key is not `com.almworks.jira.structure`. A type with an empty title or empty new-item title is left out with a warning. A type without a weight gets `Integer.MAX_VALUE`. They are sorted by weight, then title. The array is empty, not absent, when there are none.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `restAsyncBackoff` comes from the setting `structure.rest.async.backoff`, read once when the plugin starts (Jira application property when non-empty, else JVM system property): comma-separated integers, each trimmed, in the given order. It is absent when unset or empty, and also when any piece is not an integer, in which case a warning is logged and no partial list is used.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `globalError` is `sw.widget.ph.global-error.inconsistent-index` in the current user's language ('Index is inconsistent with the database and should be rebuilt. Structure will be in read-only mode until the problem is resolved.') while `reindex-locker` says the index consistency check failed, and absent otherwise.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`: `enabledPlugins` holds those keys of `PluginAccessor.getEnabledPlugins()`, in that order, that are `is.origo.jira.tempo-plugin`, `com.tempoplugin.tempo-plan-core` or `com.jiraeditor.jeditor`. It is an empty array when none of those apps is enabled.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction`: for a logged-in caller the value of the Jira user preference `structure.board.issueLinkAction` is used when it is one of the three codes; an unknown stored value is ignored with a warning. Otherwise, and always for anonymous callers, the instance default applies, and without one `showDetails`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction`: the instance default is read once when the plugin starts, from setting `structure.board.issueLinkAction` (Jira application property when non-empty, else JVM system property). An unknown value counts as no default, and a later change needs a plugin restart.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction`: for a logged-in caller a known `type` is stored with `setString` under `structure.board.issueLinkAction` in the caller's Jira extended preferences (`UserPreferencesManager`), and takes effect at the next read. The caller's own value is the only one changed.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction`: anonymous callers get 400 with plain text `cannot set issue link action for anonymous user`, whatever the body. For a logged-in caller an unknown or missing `type` gives 400 with `structure-error` `INVALID_PARAMETER` and message `Invalid Structure Board link action '<type>'` (`null` for a missing `type`), and nothing is stored. A null body gives 500. A failure of Jira's preference store goes to the exception mapper.

The five gadget endpoints `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures`, `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`, `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`, `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetConfigs` skip the common access gate: `loggedIn=true` in the query string does not give 401 for an anonymous caller, and a caller without the 'use' permission never gets 403 `permission violation`. The reply is still marked `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`. Each endpoint answers with status 200 or 400 as its own claims say.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures`: given a caller who lacks the 'use' permission, it answers 200 with a `validation-errors` object whose `errorMessages` is the single entry `s.g.structure-unavailable` (the key itself, not its text) and whose `errors` is empty; nothing is searched, whatever `query` says.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures`: given a `query` that is not blank after trimming, it looks at the non-archived structures the caller can VIEW, in the order `StructureManager.getAllStructures(PermissionLevel.VIEW)` gives them, and keeps those whose full name contains the trimmed query as literal text, ignoring case (Unicode case folding; regular expression characters have no meaning). The reply is one group labelled with the text of `s.g.config.structureId.search.label` (`Structures found:`), also when nothing matches (then `items` is empty); `query` echoes the parameter exactly as sent, untrimmed.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views` with a search: up to 9 matches are all returned with no footer; with 10 or more matches only the first 8 are returned and the group's `footer` is the localized `s.g.config.structureId.search.n-more` (structures, `{0} more structures found`) or `s.g.config.viewId.search.n-more` (views, `{0} more views found`), where {0} = matches minus 8. So 9 matches give 9 items, and 10 matches give 8 items and `2 more ...`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views`: each `picker-search-item` has `value` and `id` = the decimal id as a string, `label` = the name shortened to 40 characters (a longer name becomes its first 37 characters plus `...`; a null name becomes empty), `title` = the description, unshortened, `icon` null and no `params`. `html` is the HTML-escaped `label`; with a search, the first match inside `label` is wrapped in `...` (text around and inside the span escaped). The match is looked for in the shortened `label`, so a name matching only beyond its cut gets no highlight. `entity` is a `structure-summary` for structures and a `grid-view` without permissions and owner for views.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures`: given no `query`, or one blank after trimming, it suggests from the caller's recent structures (recents-manager) and favourite structures (favorite-manager, `getFavorites(user)`). When the two lists together hold at most 8, both are kept whole. Otherwise: with fewer than 4 favourites, all favourites are kept and recents are cut to 8 minus the favourites count; else with fewer than 4 recents, all recents are kept and favourites are cut to 8 minus the recents count; else the first 4 of each are kept. A structure in both lists is not de-duplicated.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structures` without a search answers 200 with `query` null and groups in this order: recents (label text of `s.g.config.structureId.recents.label`, `Recent Structures`), then favourites (`s.g.config.structureId.favorites.label`, `Favorite Structures`); an empty list gets no group. Only the last group has a `footer`, the localized `s.g.config.structureId.suggestions.footer` (`Start typing for structures`). With no recents and no favourites `groups` is empty.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate` checks everything and reports every problem, in this order: `structureId`, `viewId`, `canvas-viewId` (only with `useCanvasSettings=true`), the filter, `numRows`, `canvas-numRows` (only with `useCanvasSettings=true`). Each problem is one entry of `errors` in `validation-errors`, with `field`, `error` and `params` (empty list when none); `errorMessages` stays empty. With no problem it answers 200 `empty-ok`, otherwise 400. A failed check does not stop later checks, also when the caller lacks the 'use' permission.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: the `structureId` field gets, by first match: `s.g.structure-unavailable` when the caller lacks the 'use' permission; `s.g.config.err.no.structureId` when the parameter is missing or not a whole number (Java long syntax, no trimming); `s.g.config.err.bad.structureId` with params [the raw parameter] when `StructureManager.isAccessible(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)` is false (missing, not viewable, zero or negative id). `error` is the key itself, not its text.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: `viewId`, and `canvas-viewId` with `useCanvasSettings=true`, are checked the same way under their own field name: `s.g.config.err.no.viewId` when missing or not a whole number; `s.g.config.err.bad.viewId` with params [the raw value] when `StructureViewManager.isAccessible(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)` is false. Without `useCanvasSettings=true`, `canvas-viewId` and `canvas-numRows` are ignored.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: a blank or missing `filterType` gives field error `filterType` / `s.g.config.err.bad.filterType` (no params), and so does any value other than the exact lower-case `none`, `text`, `jql`, `sjql`, `saved`. `none` needs nothing else: `filterQuery` and `filterId` are ignored. `saved` ignores `filterQuery`; the other types ignore `filterId`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: for `text`, `jql` and `sjql`, `filterQuery` is URL-decoded as UTF-8 once more on top of the query-string decoding (`+` becomes a space; text that is not valid percent-encoding is kept as it is). Blank or missing gives field error `filterQuery` / `s.g.config.err.no.filterQuery`. `text` needs nothing more. `jql`: the text is parsed by Jira's `JqlQueryParser` and validated by `SearchService.validateQuery` for the current user; the field error text is the parse problem's localized message, or the first error message of the validation result. `sjql`: parsed with `StructureQueryParser` and validated; the field error text is the `StructureException`'s localized message or the first validation error. In these cases `error` is that already-localized text and `params` is empty.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: for `filterType=saved`, a missing or blank `filterId` gives field error `filterId` / `s.g.config.err.no.filterId`. A value that does not start with exactly `filter-`, or whose rest is not a whole number, gives `s.g.config.err.bad.filterId` with params [the raw value]; so does a filter that `SearchRequestService.getFilter` does not return for the current user. A bare number such as `10000` is therefore invalid.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate`: `numRows`, and `canvas-numRows` with `useCanvasSettings=true`, must parse as a Java int and lie in 2..50 inclusive; `2` and `50` pass, `1`, `51`, empty, missing, `10.5` and ` 10` (with a space) fail. Failure gives a field error under that parameter's name with `s.g.config.err.bad.numRows` and params [`2`, `50`] (strings).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: given a caller who lacks the 'use' permission, it answers 200 with `errors.errorMessages` = [`s.g.structure-unavailable`] (the key), and `structure`, `view`, `canvasView` and `filter` absent, without looking them up. `loggedInUser` and `operations` are still filled.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: `structureId` is looked up only when positive and no error is recorded yet, with `StructureManager.getStructure(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)`. On `StructureException` the `errorMessages` entry is the key `s.g.no-such-structure` (no parameters), and then `view`, `canvasView` and `filter` are all left out even if they would be valid. A zero, negative or missing `structureId` adds nothing.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: `viewId` and `canvasViewId` are each read only when positive and no error is recorded yet, with `StructureViewManager.getView(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)`; a `StructureException` leaves that key absent and adds no error. Note the parameter is `canvasViewId` here, not `canvas-viewId` as in validation. Each view is a `grid-view` without permissions and owner.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: `filterId` is read only when positive and no error is recorded yet, with `SearchRequestService.getFilter` in a service context for the current user. A filter gives `filter` = `saved-filter-ref` (`id`, `name`). When Jira returns none, `filter` is absent and each message in the context's error collection is added to `errorMessages` as is; with no messages nothing is added.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: `loggedInUser` is always present. For a logged-in user it has `userKey`, `name` and `displayName`; for anonymous all three are empty strings. In both cases `avatarUrl` and `profileUrl` are empty strings. No localized 'anonymous' text is used here.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta`: `operations` is always present, also without the 'use' permission. It asks Jira's `SimpleLinkManager` for the sections at location `opsbar-operations` for the current user, with a helper built for the request whose context holds `issueId` = the literal text `{0}`, and for each section in order lists `getLinksForSectionIgnoreConditions`, so link conditions are not evaluated. Each link gives `id`, `styleClass` and `url`; no link means an empty list.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views`: given a caller who lacks the 'use' permission, it answers 200 with a `validation-errors` object holding `errorMessages` = [`s.g.structure-unavailable`]; nothing is searched.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views`: given a non-empty `query`, it searches `StructureViewManager.getViews(PermissionLevel.VIEW)` (sorted by name by that manager), ignoring `structureId`, with the same matching as the structure search (trimmed literal text, ignoring case). The one group is labelled with the text of `s.w.view.list.found` (`Views found:`), and `query` echoes the parameter as sent. `structureId` is not validated in this case.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views`: a `query` of only whitespace counts as a search (only an empty or missing `query` means suggestions), and since the trimmed text is empty nothing matches: the reply is one empty `Views found:` group with `query` echoed (as the original does). The structure picker treats the same input as no query.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views`: given an empty or missing `query`, it takes `StructureViewManager.getMenuItems(structure, StructurePage.GADGET)`, where structure is `structureId` parsed as a long, or null (global default menu) when `structureId` is missing, not a number, or `StructureManager.isAccessible` at VIEW says false. The first 8 items are kept. The reply has `query` null and exactly one group, also when empty, labelled with the text of `s.w.view.list.suggested` (`Associated Views`) with footer `s.g.config.viewId.suggestions.footer` (`Start typing for views`).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetConfigs` makes no permission check and answers 200 `gadget-grid-tuning`. `local` is always pollInterval 15000, minCachedRows 20, preloadRowsFactor 2.0. `remote` is 15000 / 100 / 5.0 on Server and 30000 / 500 / 10.0 on Data Center (as reported by the plugin's Data Center check), plus `allowNodeWandering` true.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetConfigs`: each value is read on every request through `DarkFeatures`, so an application property wins over a system property of the same name. Keys: `structure.gadget.<local|remote>.pollInterval`, `.minCachedRows` (`DarkFeatures.getInteger`; not an integer means the default), `.preloadRowsFactor` (a value that does not parse as a double, or is NaN or infinite, means the default) and `structure.gadget.remote.allowNodeWandering` (`DarkFeatures.getBoolean`, default true).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetConfigs`: `retryBackoff` is present only on Data Center and only when `structure.gadget.dc.retryBackoff` (`DarkFeatures.getProperty`) is non-empty and every comma-separated part parses as an int with no trimming: `100,200` gives [100, 200]; `100, 200` or `100,x` drops the key entirely, and so does a value of only commas. On Server the key is absent whatever the property says.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/share` validates in this order, each a 400 in plain text: missing body `no perspective`; body with an `id` `received perspective shouldn't have an ID`; `spec` absent or JSON null `cannot create perspective with empty spec`. Only then does it call perspective-manager, whose refusal gives 403 with `structure-error` (`PERSPECTIVE_CREATION_DENIED`). Licence state never blocks it.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/share`: `spec` may be any non-null JSON value. It is stored as its re-serialised compact JSON text: whitespace of the request is gone, and a JSON string is stored with its quotes, so `""` is accepted and stored as two quote characters. The 200 reply is `shared-perspective` with key order `id`, `spec`, the `spec` being that stored JSON embedded as a raw value.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/shareByEmail` validates in this order, each a 400 in plain text: `perspectiveId` null `no perspective id`; `recipients` null or empty `no recipients`; Jira outgoing mail unavailable: the text of `s.p.dialog.email.not-configured` (`Outgoing Mail is not configured`); a recipient key with no user `user with key '<key>' is not found` (first unknown key, in list order; a null entry reads `null`). Outgoing mail counts as unavailable when sending is disabled, no default SMTP server is defined, or asking Jira fails. Nothing is counted or sent when any of these fail.
`POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/shareByEmail`: a missing body fails with a null dereference, so the reply is 500 with an empty or message-only plain-text body, not a 400 (as the original does).

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/shareByEmail`: after validation it adds 1 to the total statistic `perspectiveShareCount` (statistics-manager, asynchronously) and then hands perspective id, recipient users in list order, and `message` to perspective-mail-sender. The count is made first, so a request that then fails with 404 is still counted. Success is 200 `empty-ok`; errors of the mail sender (see perspective-mail-sender) surface through the exception mapper.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/{id}`: an id below 1 gives 400 in plain text `Incorrect perspective id <id>`, with nothing counted. Otherwise it adds 1 to the total statistic `perspectiveAccessCount` and records the current user under the unique-user statistic `activeUser` (nothing for anonymous, see statistics-manager), and only then looks the perspective up, so an unknown id is counted too. Unknown id: 404 in plain text `Perspective with id <id> does not exist`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/{id}`: the 200 body is a JSON string whose content is the stored spec text (after the saved-column refresh of perspective-manager), not the spec's JSON structure itself. A stored `{"primary":{}}` is answered as `"{\"primary\":{}}"`, with `application/json`. A client must parse the body as JSON to get a string, then parse that string. The plugin's own board does this.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check`: it validates exactly the two-argument form of the `structure()` JQL function, with `structure` and `query` as first and second argument, without running the query. Valid arguments give 200 `empty-ok`. Nothing is stored. Warnings alone do not fail the call and are not returned.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check`: when there is at least one error, it answers 400 with a JSON array of strings: the distinct error messages sorted by natural String order, followed by the distinct warning messages sorted the same way. Both arguments are always checked, so a bad structure and a bad query give two entries. Texts come from `s.jql.error.*` in the current user's language.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: `structure`, trimmed, that parses as a positive long is an id: not accessible at VIEW gives `s.jql.error.bad-structure-id` with the id. Anything else is a name, matched against non-archived viewable structures, ignoring case and outer spaces: one match is used, several give `s.jql.error.too-many-structures` with the argument as sent, none gives `s.jql.error.unknown-structure` with the argument as sent. A missing or empty `structure` is therefore the `unknown-structure` error with an empty name; the default structure is not used in this two-argument form.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: a resolved structure whose automation is paused (generation blocked for its unsecured forest spec) gives an error, not a warning: `s.jql.error.automation-stopped` with the name and the id (English `Automation is paused for structure "<name>" (#<id>).`).

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: a missing `query` is treated as the query text `[]` (an empty inner JQL), which is valid. An empty or whitespace-only `query` that is present is not the same: it fails to parse, so it gives an error (a query is expected at the end of the text). `check` validates for the search form, `logs` for execution, and the text must parse and pass the structure query validator for the current user.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs` always answers 200 with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="S-JQL_Troubleshooting.zip"`, `application/zip`, no-cache, whatever the arguments are; only the common access gate can refuse it. The body is a ZIP with exactly one entry `S-JQL_Troubleshooting.log`. Three warnings go to the server log: requested, started and finished.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: with argument errors the query is not run and the ZIP entry stays empty: every message (errors sorted, then warnings sorted) is written at error level to the server log under logger `com.almworks.jira.structure.query`, not into the archive.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: with valid arguments the query runs on the structure's forest, secured for the caller, and all results are consumed but not reported. During the run, logger `com.almworks.jira.structure.query` is set to TRACE and its output from the request's thread only goes into the ZIP entry instead of the normal log (output of other threads is not captured). When the forest cannot be loaded, a warning is logged and the entry holds only what was logged until then. Failure during the run is logged, and the ZIP is closed normally. Levels and logger set-up are restored at the end.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs`: `messagePattern` is the log4j pattern layout of captured lines; when missing, `%d %m%n` is used. With `includeRelOutput=true` logger `com.almworks.jira.structure.query.sjql.binaryRelLog` is set to TRACE during the run; otherwise (default) it is switched off during the run, so its lines are left out.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: for an anonymous caller (even with a missing body), or when `stats` is null or empty, or `timestamp` is null, it answers 200 `empty-ok` and records nothing.
`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: a logged-in caller with a missing body gets a null dereference, so 500, not 200 (as the original does).

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: for a logged-in caller with non-empty `stats` and a `timestamp`, it writes to `AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS` immediately, not at the next flush, all rows with C_TIMESTAMP = `timestamp` as given. Each `stats` entry gives one row with C_STAT = the name, C_USERKEY null and C_VALUE = the amount (0.0 for a null amount). Plus one `userCount` row with the caller's key and C_VALUE 0.0. An entry with an empty name is skipped. A whitespace-only name is stored.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: an additional `activeUser` unique-user row with the caller's key is written when `stats` has at least one of exactly these 20 names: `forestSpec.change`, `forestSpec.transform`, `layout.switch`, `search.toggle`, `expandClick`, `expandOrMoveToNext`, `expandNextLevel`, `expandAll`, `expandLevel`, `collapseClick`, `collapseOrMoveToParent`, `collapseNextLevel`, `collapseAll`, `view.addColumn`, `view.changeColumn`, `view.removeColumn`, `view.moveColumn`, `view.switch`, `jira.showActions`, `jira.actions.dropdown.click`. The presence of the name counts; its amount does not, so 0 also counts.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: a `stats` entry named `userCount`, or `activeUser` together with one of the 20 interactive names, collides with the entry the endpoint adds itself: the call fails with 400 `structure-error` (`error` = `Invalid request data`) and nothing is recorded (as the original does).

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`: after recording, when the cached answer to 'are at least 3 users recorded?' is no, it is dropped, so the 'enable statistics' offer of statistics-manager can appear right away without waiting for a flush.

`PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` and `PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/dismissOffer`: the common access gate checks only that the caller is a Jira administrator; a non-administrator, and anonymous, gets 403 `permission violation`. An administrator without the 'use' permission passes, since for these two endpoints that permission is not looked at.

`PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` stores global property `statistics.sendingEnabled` = true and answers 200 `empty-ok`. It takes no parameters, repeating it changes nothing, and it causes no network traffic: nothing is sent to the vendor now or later (see statistics-manager). There is no endpoint that turns the property off.

`PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/dismissOffer` sets the caller's Jira user property `com.almworks.jira.structure.statistics.offerRejected` to true and answers 200 `empty-ok`. It concerns only the calling administrator: others still see the offer.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/menu`: `forPage` is checked first: any value that is not exactly one of the lower-case page ids `structure`, `structure-with-details`, `issue`, `project`, `component`, `version`, `navigator`, `gadget`, `greenhopper` gives 400 with the JSON string `unknown page`; so does an empty value. Otherwise `views` = `StructureViewManager.getMenuItems(forStructure, page)` in that order, as `grid-view` objects without permissions and owner, and `preferred` = the ids of the items flagged preferred, in the same order (empty list when none). A structure the caller cannot view gives empty `views` and `preferred`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/menu` and `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/default`: the menu is read for an effective page: `forPage` missing, `structure-with-details`, `navigator` and `greenhopper` read the structure board's menu and defaults; `component` and `version` read the project page's; `structure`, `issue`, `project` and `gadget` read their own. So a missing `forPage` is not 'no restriction': it is the same as `forPage=structure`.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/default`: it validates `forPage` as `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/menu` does, then answers 200 with the first menu item flagged preferred as a `grid-view` without permissions and owner, or 200 `empty-ok` when no item is preferred, including when the structure is not viewable.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}` reads the view with `StructureViewManager.getView(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)`; a failure is the manager's `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, 404 `structure-error` with `viewId` set. It reports `writable` (caller has EDIT), `adminable` (caller has ADMIN), `shared` and `sharedWithAll`.

A `grid-view` reply's `shared` is true when any rule is not a set-level rule or sets a level other than NONE. `sharedWithAll` is decided by walking the rules in order: a set-level rule of `Anyone` at VIEW or higher makes it true; a set-level rule at NONE for any subject, and any rule that is not a set-level rule, makes it false; other rules change nothing. Applies to `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}` and every other view reply.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}` with `withPermissions=true` includes `permissions` only when the caller holds ADMIN on the view; otherwise the key is absent, and no error is raised. Without the flag the key is absent for everyone.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}` with `withOwner=true`: a view with no owner gives `hasOwner` false and no `owner`. A view with an owner gives `owner` (and no `hasOwner`) when the caller is the owner or holds Jira's global ADMINISTER or USER_PICKER permission; otherwise `hasOwner` true and no `owner`. Without the flag both keys are absent.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view`: `permission` is parsed first, before `ids`, by comparing with the level names ignoring case (`NONE`, `VIEW`, `EDIT`, `EDIT_GENERATORS`, `AUTOMATE`, `ADMIN`). Anything else, including an empty value, gives 400 `structure-error` with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message` = `Unknown level. Known values for level: NONE,VIEW,EDIT,EDIT_GENERATORS,AUTOMATE,ADMIN`. Missing, `none` and `view` all search at VIEW.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view`: given `ids`, it is split on commas, and each part must parse as a positive long with no trimming (`1, 2` keeps only 1). With no valid part (also an empty `ids`) the reply is 400 in plain text `specify correct view ids`. The views are returned in the given order; a repeated id gives the view repeated; ids that fail `getView(id, level)` are left out silently.
`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view`: without `ids` it returns `StructureViewManager.getViews(level)`, sorted by name as that manager sorts. The reply is a `grid-view-list` with no `preferred` key.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view`: `name` narrows the result, with or without `ids`, to views whose name contains the trimmed text as literal characters anywhere, ignoring case with Unicode case folding: `ann` matches `Planning`. Regular-expression characters are plain text. A `name` that is blank after trimming filters nothing.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view` validates in this order: missing body gives 400 plain text `no view`; a body with `id` gives `created view cannot have id parameter`; a `name` that is null or blank after trimming gives `created view must have a name`. Then the body's columns and rules are converted, where invalid data gives 400 `structure-error` `Invalid request data` even for a caller who may not create views. Only then does saving check the right to create and to share views (view-manager).

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view`: a body without `spec` is refused when saving, with 400 `structure-error` `INVALID_PARAMETER`; nothing is stored. An empty object `spec` is enough: the view is created with no columns.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view`: the name is stored as sent, not trimmed. A logged-in caller becomes the owner and an `owner` in the body is ignored. For an anonymous caller the body's `owner` is used if any. The 200 reply is the new `grid-view` built with permissions and owner requested, with the caller's real 'browse users' answer.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/update` checks in this order: missing body 400 plain text `no view`; body `id` different from the path id 400 `cannot reassign view id`; `owner` present with no `userKey`, whose `name` is not a Jira user (null or empty included), 400 with the text of `s.w.view.d.det.user-not-found` (`An error occurred while saving: user not found`); only then the view is read at ADMIN. So an unknown owner name gives 400 even to a caller with no access to the view.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/update`: a caller with less than ADMIN on the view gets 404 `structure-error` `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, not 403, the same as for a missing view. `POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/updateSpec` does the same below EDIT, and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/makePublic` below ADMIN. Invalid columns or rules in the body are only looked at after this check.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/update` changes only what is non-null in the body: `name`, `description`, `owner`, `permissions`, `spec`. An empty `description` clears it. Null cannot clear anything, so the owner cannot be removed. `permissions` replaces all rules, with null list entries dropped; `spec` replaces the whole specification. An `owner` with a `userKey` is taken without checking that the user exists, and `userKey` wins over `name`. A blank `name` gives 400 `INVALID_PARAMETER` from saving. The reply is `grid-view` with permissions and owner requested.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/updateSpec`: missing body gives 400 plain text `no specification`. The view is read at EDIT, then its whole specification is replaced by the body; name, owner and rules stay. The reply is `grid-view` with permissions and owner requested, so a caller with EDIT but not ADMIN gets no `permissions` key.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view`, `POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/update` and `POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/updateSpec`, for each column of a `view-layout`: a null entry gives 400 `structure-error` `Invalid request data` with `message` `null column`; a missing `key` gives `no key`; a missing `csid` gives `no csid`. A `columnDisplayMode` or `rowDisplayMode` of 0 or of an unsupported value is not an error: it is ignored (the latter with a logged warning) and the specification default applies, not the view's previous mode. Missing `columns` or `pins` means none.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/update`: when the change leaves the caller below VIEW on the view (for example the owner hands it over and no rule covers them), the change is saved, then building the reply fails: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the reply is 200 with `writable` and `adminable` false.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/makePublic`: the view is read at ADMIN; the body is ignored and may be any JSON object. When `sharedWithAll` is already true nothing is saved. Otherwise the rules become: first `anyone VIEW`, then, in order, only the old set-level rules with a level above VIEW; all others are dropped, so rules giving VIEW to a group and NONE rules are lost. The reply is `grid-view` with permissions and owner requested.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/makeDefault`: a missing body gives 500. It validates `pageId` as a page id (400 JSON string `unknown page`), reads the view at VIEW (404 `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`), and only then calls `makeDefaultForStructure` (view-manager), which requires ADMIN on the structure. So a bad view is reported before a bad structure. A missing `structureId` is 0, and gives 404 `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. The reply is `grid-view` without permissions and owner.

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/makeDefault` with no `pageId`: if the view is already the structure board default for that structure it answers 200 and writes nothing; otherwise it fails with a null dereference, so 500, and nothing is written (as the original does).

`POST /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/makeDefault`: only `structure`, `issue` and `project` can hold a default. For `pageId=gadget` it answers 200 and saves the structure's settings: the view is placed on the gadget menu but no default is recorded. For `component`, `version`, `navigator`, `greenhopper` and `structure-with-details` the page itself is dropped from what is stored, so an associated view that had unset menu pages ends up on no menu (as the original does); `component` and `version` are a no-op when the view is already the project page default.

`GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}/associations`: when `StructureViewManager.isAccessible(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)` is false it answers 403 with no body. Otherwise `associatedStructures` is `getAssociatedStructures(id)` in that order as `structure-summary` objects (empty list when none); `associatedDefault` is true when the view is listed in the global default view settings, on any page, and absent otherwise, never false.

`DELETE /rest/structure/1.0/view/{id}`: an id of 0 or below gives 400 with no body. When the view is not accessible at VIEW the reply is 404 `structure-error` `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` with `viewId` set and no message. Otherwise `deleteView` runs (view-manager): a caller below ADMIN gets 403 `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED`. Success is 200 `empty-ok`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest`: the query parameter `s` is parsed as JSON text into a `forest-spec`. When `s` is missing, empty or not parsable as such JSON, the parse failure is only logged and the reply is 400 with the error object `error` = `Invalid request data`, `message` = `Forest spec is required` (never the `Cannot parse request JSON` form). A parsable `s` then behaves exactly like the body of `POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest`: given a valid `forest-spec`, it asks forest-service for the source of that spec, secured for the caller (a clipboard spec means the caller's own session clipboard), takes `getLatest()` and answers a `forest-snapshot`: `spec` is the request's object echoed unchanged, `version` and `formula` come from that one latest forest, and `itemTypes` lists, in ascending type number, only the non-issue item types that occur in `formula` (an empty object for a forest of issues only). A missing body gives the same 400 `Forest spec is required`. Errors from forest-service pass through (for example 404 for a structure the caller cannot view).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest` and `POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest` compute on the request thread: they wait for generation to finish, never answer an `async-job-ticket`, and do not read `jobId`. They change nothing and record no usage counter.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: on a first call (no `jobId`) the request is checked on the request thread before any job starts, in this order, each failure being 400 with `error` = `Invalid request data` and nothing applied: `spec` is parsed (a missing or invalid spec gives the message of `ForestSpec.fromRest`, e.g. `Forest spec is required`); `version` missing gives `Version is required`; then, for each action in order that has `cutFrom` with a `spec`, that spec is parsed, a missing `cutFrom.version` gives `Version is required` and a missing or empty `cutFrom.rowIds` gives `Row IDs are required`. `cutFrom` without `spec` is not checked here. These `cutFrom` checks apply to any action name, not only `add`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: a request with a valid `spec` and `version` but no `actions` key, an action entry that is JSON null, or a missing request body fails with `NullPointerException`, which the mapper answers 500 in plain text; no 400 is produced for them. Nothing is applied.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: with an empty `actions` list the forest source is never requested, so an unknown structure or a forest the caller cannot see is not noticed: the reply is 200 with `successfulActions` 0, no `updateError`, and empty `forestUpdates`, `effects`, `undoEffects` and `problems`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: the work runs through structure-async-request-handler as a job on the job-manager executor `generator`, under the caller's identity and security context, and answers per that module (`async-job-ticket` after the wait). A call with `jobId` starts nothing and reads no other field of the body, so `spec`, `version` and `actions` may be absent then. A job id of another user is unknown (404, code 4603). A job that failed is not forgotten: repeating the call with its `jobId` gives the same failure again until the job is cleaned up (job-manager: 3 minutes after it finished).

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: on a first call the caller's HTTP session is obtained (and created when there is none), even when no action touches the clipboard; its id selects the clipboard that is cleared for `viaClipboard` actions. The session is not read in the job.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: actions run strictly in list order. The first action that is refused or asks a question ends the run: later actions are not looked at, not even their content, and the reply is 200 with `updateError` set and `successfulActions` = the number of actions finished before it. Actions already finished stay applied (there is no rollback of earlier actions), and their `forestUpdates`, `effects`, `oldRowIds`/`newRowIds` and `problems` are in the reply.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an action's own content (name, `forest`, `rowId`/`rowIds`, `originalRowIds`) is checked in the job only when the run reaches that action, not up front.
